limit of AI calls. If one refuses, the card says why and PULSE tries again until the
approval lapses.
The national do-not-call registry is not connected. The card says "not
checked": PULSE never shows a number as clear of a list it did not read.
What happens when the call ends
When the call ends, the lead gets one of these outcomes and a short summary.



Outcome
What PULSE does




Interested, with a time the person agreed to
The lead moves to Meeting proposed, the sequence stops, a task to confirm the meeting is created at that time. A proposed meeting is not a booked one


Interested, no time
The lead moves to Replied, the sequence stops, a task to follow up


Not now
A task to try again in two weeks; the sequence goes on


Not interested
The sequence stops


Referral
The sequence stops, a task to follow the referral


Callback requested
A task at the time given


Wrong person
The sequence stops, a task to check the contact


Asked not to be called again
The number goes on the do-not-call list, the address on the suppression list, consent is revoked and the sequence stops


Voicemail, no answer, hung up
The sequence goes on; a task where useful



For email, an
interested reply moves the lead to Replied, the meeting proposal you approve
moves it to Meeting proposed when it is sent, and only Confirm the
meeting (or moving the lead yourself) sets Meeting booked.
Transcripts and recording
No audio is recorded. The transcript is stored encrypted with the call,
never written to the server log, and erased after the retention period
(7 days unless your administrator set another; at most 90). The outcome, the
answers and the summary stay on the lead. Nothing is played back.

docs/user-guide/website-form/.title: Website form
docs/user-guide/website-form/.body:
Website form

Your website's contact form can send each enquiry straight to Leads. Every
enquiry becomes a lead in the New column, so the bell shows it as a lead
waiting. When HubSpot is connected, the contact is also added to HubSpot.
Turn it on

Open Settings → Integrations and find the Website form card.
Under Sites allowed to post, add the address of each site the form lives
on, such as https://example.com. Use https://. http:// is accepted only
for localhost, so you can test a page on your own computer. A browser on
any other site is refused.
Select Create link. The card shows the link and an HTML snippet once.
Copy them now: PULSE cannot show the link again. If you lose it, select New link and
update your site. The old link stops working at once.

The snippet

  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  Send


The card fills in your real link. Copy the snippet from the card rather than
writing it by hand: it also carries what Attribution needs, and
belongs on every page of your site, not only on the contact page.



Field
Used for




name, or first_name and last_name
The lead's name


email
The lead's email. An email or a phone is required.


company, phone
Copied onto the lead


message
Kept in the lead's notes, with the date


source_page (or about)
The lead's source becomes website form: . For a web address, only the host and path are kept.


landing_url, referrer
Filled by the card's snippet. See Attribution.


_redirect
Where the visitor goes after sending. Only an address on one of your listed sites is followed; otherwise PULSE shows a short thank-you page.


_hp or _gotcha
Honeypot. A post that fills either is answered normally and stored nowhere.



A script can post JSON instead (Content-Type: application/json, the same field
names). It gets {"ok":true} back, or {"ok":false,"error":"…"}.
What PULSE does with an enquiry

A new email creates a lead: stage New, source website form: .
An email you already have (in any letter case) adds the enquiry to that
lead's notes instead of creating a second lead. Its stage is not changed.
HubSpot connected: the contact is created in HubSpot, or updated if it is
already there. A HubSpot failure is logged; the lead is still saved in PULSE.

Limits



Limit
Value




Size of one enquiry
16 KiB (HTTP 413 above it)


Many enquiries in a short time
Answered with HTTP 429


Sites per link
10



A wrong or turned-off link answers HTTP 404. The link carries no session and
no cookie: the secret in the address is the only credential, which is why it is
shown once and can be replaced at any time. Turn off on the card deletes it.

docs/user-guide/website-chat/.title: Website chat
docs/user-guide/website-chat/.body:
Website chat

The website chat puts a PULSE assistant on your own website, for your
visitors, to answer questions about your business.

Warning: Off until configured. The website chat answers nothing until your
administrator sets it up on the server. Until then Settings › Website
chat says "This server cannot serve the website chat yet" and why.

What a visitor sees
A small chat window on your site. It says first that it is an AI
assistant. A visitor needs no account and never signs in.

To leave their details, a visitor fills in the contact form in the chat.
Only that form makes a lead: it lands on Leads › Inbound with the source
"website chat". Nothing a visitor types elsewhere becomes a lead.
A visitor can ask for a person. That puts an item in your bell and in
Visitors who asked for a person.

Set it up
Open Settings › Website chat:

Switch Website chat on.
List your site addresses, one per line (like https://example.com).
The widget answers only on those sites.
Optionally write a greeting and pick the widget language.
Save. PULSE makes a site key and shows the snippet: Copy it and
paste it before  on your site. If your site sends a
Content-Security-Policy, allow the address the page names in
script-src and connect-src.

New key stops the old snippet at once: paste the new one. Revoke the
key stops the widget and turns the chat off.
Visitor chats are kept for a limited time and then deleted; the widget tells
the visitor, and the page shows the period.
Visitors who asked for a person
Each request shows the visitor's contact details if they left them and the
chat, while it is still kept. Mark handled closes it.
Administrators: the server settings are listed in
Switches and arming order.

docs/user-guide/attribution/.title: Attribution
docs/user-guide/attribution/.body:
Attribution

Where your leads came from shows, for the chosen period, which channel and
which campaign brought each lead and each won deal, and how much won revenue
followed. It is on the Brand Analysis overview and on the Results page.
Links PULSE sends
Links that PULSE publishes in a post, or sends in an outreach or lead email,
to your own site are marked so that a visit from them can be traced back to
the post or email. A link to any other site is never changed, and nothing is
marked that your approvals and publishing switches withheld.

Your own site is what you list in Settings → Integrations → Link
tagging. When you list none, PULSE uses the sites allowed to post to your
website form and the site of your latest
check-up. The card shows which sites are used.
This is on for every account until you turn it off on that card.

What you see

Each lead and each won deal shows the channel and campaign that brought it.
A lead PULSE cannot trace is shown as unattributed, with where it came
from (added by hand, website form, HubSpot, found by PULSE). PULSE never
guesses.
Won revenue is shown per currency. A won deal with no value is counted and
said, never valued at 0.
When nothing in the period could be traced, the card says Not enough data
yet instead of showing zeros.

PULSE records only what it needs to show this, and no personal browsing
details.

docs/user-guide/google-business-profile/.title: Google reviews
docs/user-guide/google-business-profile/.body:
Google Business Profile and reviews


Warning: Not yet available. This feature is built and is waiting on Google's
approval of API access, so reading reviews, replying and posting do not work
today. This
page describes how it is meant to work once access is granted.

With your Google Business Profile connected, PULSE is meant to:

Read your reviews and the basic figures Google reports for the last 28
days (views on Search and Maps, calls, website visits, direction requests).
A figure Google does not report is left out, never shown as 0.
Draft a reply to each new review on your own PULSE model. Only your
Approve posts a reply. A negative review is flagged, and you must also
tick that you read it before the reply can be approved.
Make posts (an update, an offer or an event). They wait for approval in
Campaigns like any other post.
Ask won customers for a review: when a deal is marked won, PULSE proposes
one review-request email from your own mailbox, after your approval. Every
won customer gets the same request; PULSE refuses a request that offers
something in return, as Google requires.

Replies and posts also need your administrator to arm the Google Business
Profile switches, which are off by default. The connection is made from
Settings › Integrations by an editor. Administrators: see
Google.
Brand awareness, reputation and customer approvals
On Brand Analysis, PULSE watches your brand and suggests a campaign
when something shifts. Each card cites its public sources. A suggestion is a
proposal you accept or dismiss on Campaigns; nothing is published or
sent.

docs/user-guide/weekly-results-review/.title: Weekly results review
docs/user-guide/weekly-results-review/.body:
Weekly results review

Once a week PULSE can read what your published and approved work achieved and
propose changes to your 90-day plan. It is off until you switch it on in
Settings › Account › Weekly results review.
What it reads. Which channel and campaign brought leads and won deals
(Attribution), the results PULSE read back from
your posts, and the replies it recorded. Outcomes only: no message text and no
contact details.
What it proposes. For each open action of the plan that has results of its
own, keep, stop or move to another week, with a reason and the measured
figures it rests on. It appears on the plan page.
Nothing happens by itself. You approve or reject it. Approving makes exactly
the listed changes to your plan, as if you had made them by hand; rejecting
changes nothing. Nothing is sent or published.
Honest about data. A figure nobody measured says not measured, never
zero: a won deal with no value recorded, link tagging switched off, a channel
PULSE cannot read results from. A row with fewer outcomes than the minimum your
administrator configured decides nothing; when no action has enough, the week
says so with the numbers (for example "the most outcomes any action's results
have is 2, and the minimum is 3") and proposes nothing.
An administrator can pause the loop for everyone from the loop controls
("paused by your administrator").

docs/user-guide/campaigns/.title: Campaigns
docs/user-guide/campaigns/.body:
Campaigns

Campaigns (/campaigns) is where posts are planned, approved, scheduled
and followed until they go out. It is one page, built like Leads: what needs
you, a few counts, your campaigns, then one board of every post.
Every card on the board is one post, never a whole campaign. How a post
moves from idea to sent is explained in
Drafts, approval and publishing.
The top of the page

Needs you now: each post that waits for you, one line each: Approve
"…", Write "…" (a post that is still only an idea), or "…" did not go
out with the reason. Do it acts on it; Skip puts it off until your
next visit. When nothing waits it says Nothing waits for you.
The counts: Running campaigns, Proposals waiting, Drafts to
approve, Scheduled this week, Sent this week. A count PULSE could
not read shows —, never 0.
Replies waiting for you: the replies Autopilot drafted to comments,
mentions and messages. See
Autopilot.
What your audit found: the campaigns PULSE proposes. See
below.

Two buttons float at the bottom right: New Campaign, and Check a
competitor's content, which compares what a competitor publishes with
yours.
The campaign strip
One row per campaign, newest first (archived ones and proposals you set
aside are left out). Each row shows its state and its counts: N planned · N to
approve · N scheduled · N sent. Why shows why PULSE proposed it.

Tap a campaign to narrow the board to its posts.
Open campaign opens its own page.
A campaign PULSE proposed and you have not accepted is read only, marked
Proposed by PULSE, with Review and accept and Dismiss. While its
plan is being prepared it says Preparing its plan, then Plan ready
(or Plan failed).

The board
Four columns, in order:



Column
What is in it




Planned
Posts a campaign's plan holds that are not written yet. Create opens Studio to write one.


Drafts to approve
Written posts waiting for your OK. Each says when it is planned for, or Not scheduled, and its next step.


Scheduled
Approved posts with a time to go out (Goes out …), or Approved: pick a time to send it. A post that did not go out stays here with its reason.


Sent
Posts that went out, with the day.



A card names its channel and where it came from: its campaign, From your
check-up of …, Placed by Autopilot, or Not in a campaign. Open a
card to read the post, its steps and its actions:

Draft opens it in Studio to write or change it.
Download saves it as files you can post yourself (approved, scheduled
and sent posts). See Download.
Move moves it to another column (see the rules below).
Discard (drafts) rejects it. A rejected post leaves the board.
Reschedule and Remove (scheduled posts).
Automate opens its own automation. See Automate.

Approve and schedule

Move a draft to Scheduled to approve it and schedule it in one step:
PULSE asks for the day and time.
Approve from Needs you now approves it without a time. With
Autopilot on for that account,
PULSE then queues it at the account's best time. With Autopilot off, it goes
out when you approve it, or at its planned time if it already has one that
is still ahead.
Move a scheduled post to Scheduled again to pick a new time.

Some moves are refused, with the reason:

A post that is only an idea cannot be scheduled: Write it first.
Nothing moves to Sent by hand. A post reaches Sent only when it really
went out.
A written post never goes back to Planned.

Approving does not by itself publish. Whether a post goes out is decided when
it is due: its channel must be connected and Active, and your
administrator must have publishing switched on. Otherwise the post stays in
Scheduled marked held back (withheld) or failed, with the reason. A post
whose time passed while it waited for approval is marked missed and is
never sent late; reschedule it or remove it.
A campaign's own page
Open campaign opens /campaigns/. All campaigns takes you back.
At the top:

its state (Not started, Running, Paused, Finished,
Archived), its dates, budget, spend and channels, with Edit Campaign and
Start, Pause or Resume. A running campaign gets PULSE's daily
drafts; a paused one does not. Spend is shown only when an ad account
reports it;
Why PULSE proposed it, for a campaign PULSE proposed;
its phases, one line each: name, weeks, and how many of its posts are made;
About this plan, for a campaign with a plan (see
below);
its milestones, each with its done criteria and who approves it;
Results: the plan's targets with what was measured against them. A
result PULSE has not measured says so, never 0. Without a plan it says No
targets yet.

Below, Board shows the same board narrowed to this campaign, and
Timeline shows every recorded step of every post in date order. Steps with
no recorded time are counted, not placed.
About this plan
One line sums up the campaign's plan, for example About this plan: Plan
accepted · tone: friendly, expert · 3 Story ideas · 1 check failed. Tap it
to open the details:

Verdict: what the plan gate said, with its
reason. Plan accepted; Plan not checked by the reviewer (the reviewer
could not judge it, which is not an approval); Plan not reviewed (the
reviewer is switched off on this server); or Plan withheld. A new plan
the gate withholds is not saved: Plan your calendar shows why, and the
plan you had stays.
Tone: how you sound to each persona, with an example line.
Story ideas: the Instagram Stories, under the phase their day falls in,
each with its day, time, picture, text and sticker.
Checks: each of PULSE's checks on the plan (your capacity, the selling
ratio, each post's details, the Story days, repeated topics, the three
targets), passed or failed, a failure with what it found. A plan with no
checks recorded says not checked, never "0 failed".
Where PULSE won't post: for each channel of the plan PULSE cannot post
to today, PULSE won't post on … because: …, read from the same rules
that decide sending (for example no publisher for Facebook, the channel
switched off, or publishing switched off for the server). A channel that
can post gets no line. If PULSE could not check, it says so.
Notes: what PULSE could not do or measure when it made the plan.

Make its plan
A campaign without a plan offers Make its plan (Change the plan once it
has one). Plan your calendar asks what you can manage:

the first and last day, and an event if there is one (its day and how many
days it lasts);
how many posts a week you can manage per channel, and Instagram Stories a
day during the event;
how often a post sells something (One post in every N sells something).

PULSE lays the posts out inside that. It places each post at your best time
where it has measured one (otherwise at a starting time it labels as such),
and writes a first idea for each post: topic, format, who it is for, first
line and what readers should do, plus a tone for each
persona and three results to aim for. Its checks
test your capacity, the selling ratio, the dates and duplicates, and the
plan gate reviews the plan against your check-up.
Writing it can take a few minutes; you can leave the page.
PULSE needs to know who you talk to. If no check-up or lead tells it, the plan
is refused with: PULSE does not know who you talk to yet: run a site audit
(it asks who buys from you) or add leads, then plan again.
The plan's posts appear in Planned. Studio writes them, and Autopilot never
queues a post before its planned time.
The step trail
Open any card, or use Timeline, to see Its steps:
Planned → Drafted → Approved → Scheduled → Sent, or
Withheld, Failed or Missed.
Each step says when it happened and what PULSE recorded: the phase and planned
date, which skill wrote the draft and its check results, who approved it, when
it was queued and for when, and where it went out or why it did not. Every
step is read from what PULSE stored:

not yet: the step has not happened;
not recorded: it happened (a later step proves it) but PULSE kept no
record of it, for example who approved a post approved before approvals were
recorded.

A post sent through a channel you have not connected says to download it and
post it yourself, rather than showing the platform's raw error.
Campaigns PULSE proposes
From a check-up's content gaps, PULSE may propose a campaign whose objective
matches your goal. It waits under What your audit found and in the strip as
Proposed by PULSE:

Review and accept shows the proposal; you can change its name,
objective (required) and description, then accept it. Accepting prepares
its content strategy and plan. Nothing is published.
Dismiss sets it aside. Set-aside proposals are kept, and you can open one
again and accept it.

Automate
Every card (posts, leads, public tenders, partners) has Automate. It opens
that item's own automation over the page: a trigger, then steps. Tap a step to
change it; add or remove steps. The assistant can propose steps; you approve
them.
An automation is disarmed until you arm it: then it runs only as a Dry
run, which shows what it would do. Once armed, it runs by itself when its
trigger fires, and anything it sends still needs the server's publishing
switches. A step the server cannot carry out says so, and an automation that
cannot run yet lists why.
Starting an automation from an inbound event
Besides a new lead, a changed stage, a finished check-up, a post that was approved
or published, a schedule or a due task, a trigger can be:

Website enquiry arrived: a new lead came in through your website form;
Reply received: a lead replied to an email you sent;
Comment, mention or message arrived: read from a connected channel;
Meeting detected: PULSE proposed a meeting it found in a reply;
Lead's qualification changed: a lead moved to another band in Leads › Inbound.

An event carries only ids and fixed codes, such as the channel or the band. It never
carries the words of a message, so what a stranger writes cannot steer a flow.
A Condition step can test whether the lead replied (ever, since the flow
started, or within a number of days or hours), its inbound band, the event's
channel or its source. A trigger with Stop when the lead replies set makes
the flow stop acting once the lead has replied after the flow began.
Two more steps: Tell me adds an item to your bell (and goes to your own contact
only if you allowed that in Settings; the same limits as questions from PULSE
apply, and nothing goes to a lead), and Enrol in outreach sequence starts the
outreach sequence for each lead, with the same rules as the Leads screen and with
every email waiting for your approval.
A step Send a WhatsApp or SMS (with your tap) makes a text message for each
contact, and sends nothing by itself. Four rules hold, in this order:

The contact must have a consent you recorded: open Content › Automations ›
Messages, pick the basis (signed form, website checkbox, they wrote to us,
in person, other documented) and record it for that channel. Without it the step
is refused and says so. You can withdraw a consent at any time.
The number always comes from your contact list (a lead's recorded number, or a
contact an administrator added), never from text a lead wrote. A lead is
offered SMS only; WhatsApp needs a contact from your list.
The words are yours, typed in the step ({lead} becomes a plain first
name). PULSE writes nothing here.
Each message then waits for your tap: in Messages, Send checks everything
again (consent, a STOP reply, your contact hours, the daily limit, the switches)
and sends through the same path as the Send dialog; Don't send discards it.
A number that replied STOP is never messaged again. The default limit is 10
messages a day.

every email waiting for your approval. Draft a follow-up for quiet leads drafts one short follow-up for a lead that never replied, only when the account switched Re-engage a quiet lead on (see Outreach sequences): each draft waits for your approval. There is no step that sends a WhatsApp or
an SMS: that stays a task for you.
Old addresses
/approval, /publishing, /strategy, /content-strategy, /content-gaps,
/strategy-roadmap and /automations open this page; /approval and
/publishing bring Drafts to approve into view.

docs/user-guide/weekly-site-reaudit/.title: Weekly site re-audit
docs/user-guide/weekly-site-reaudit/.body:
Weekly site re-audit

Once a week PULSE can re-audit your own site and draft a report of what
improved and what regressed since the last audit. It is off until you switch it
on in Settings › Account › Weekly reviews.
Which site. The first own site you listed under Attribution, else the site
of your latest check-up. With none, nothing is audited and nothing is spent.
What it does. It runs the same site score as "Audit a domain" with the score
only: no leads, campaigns or drafts are made. It only reads your public site.
The report waits on the plan page; Mark as reviewed or Dismiss it. Nothing is
applied to your site or your plan, sent or published.
Compared with. Last week's re-audit; the first time, your latest check-up of
the same site; with neither, the report is a baseline.
Honest about what was measured. A check measured in both audits is improved,
regressed or unchanged. A check measured in only one is shown as newly
measured or no longer measured, never compared as if the other were zero. The
overall score is compared only when both audits measured the same data sources.
If the site could not be read, the week says so and no comparison is drawn.
Limits. One report per account per week; the loop controls (including the
administrator's pause) and the daily model-call cap apply per account; three
failed audits of one site hand it to a person.

docs/user-guide/studio/.title: Studio
docs/user-guide/studio/.body:
Studio

Studio (/studio) makes content and keeps what was made. It has two parts:
Make something new, a list of everything Studio can make (on the left on a
wide screen, folded at the top on a phone), and My Library, what was made,
grouped the same way.
Making or opening a piece opens it as a card over the page, never as a page of
its own; closing the card brings you back.
What Studio makes
The list comes from your PULSE server, so it shows only what your PULSE can
make right now. A format that cannot be made is left out, or shown with the
reason (for example Video making is not installed on this PULSE yet).



Group
Formats




Instagram
Instagram post · Instagram carousel · Instagram Reel script · Instagram Stories · Instagram profile makeover · Plan for the week · What works on your Instagram


YouTube
YouTube Short script (what Studio makes when you ask for a video: PULSE turns the script into the video)


LinkedIn
LinkedIn post · LinkedIn carousel (PDF) · LinkedIn Page update


Facebook and X
Facebook or X post


Blog and email
Blog article · Questions and answers page · Newsletter email · Follow-up emails


Long reads and audio
Guide · Customer story · Report · Presentation · Podcast episode


Learning
Online course · Study guide with quiz


Visual
Infographic · Mind map · Timeline · Comparison table



Make a piece
Pick a format. Its card shows that format's own form and nothing else;
Change format swaps it. Studio also opens from other pages with the
details filled in: Create on a planned post in Campaigns, Draft on a
board card.
Most social and written formats are written by a skill: PULSE writes a
draft, checks it, and saves it to your Campaigns board in Drafts to
approve. Nothing is posted until you approve it.
The checks
Under What PULSE checked, each check is a small chip: green when it
passed, amber when it needs work, grey when it could not be checked
(never shown as a pass). Checks depend on the format, for example Opening
line, Caption, Sounds human, Slides and Hashtags. Then:

if a check failed, PULSE rewrote it to fix what the checks found;
PULSE's reviewer (the plan gate) gives its
verdict: The reviewer agreed with it, The reviewer could not check it,
so it is not approved by the reviewer, or The reviewer is switched off on
this server;
PULSE also reads the draft against what you gave it (your brief, your
figures, your dates and names, and any research it fetched for the draft).
The result is one line under the verdict: Checked against what you gave
PULSE: every figure, date and name in it is there; 1 sentence states
something that is not in what you gave PULSE (the draft is kept as written
and the sentences are listed, so you can read them before you use it); or
Not checked: it has no figure, date or name that could be compared with
what you gave PULSE. "Checked" means only that: it says the draft matches
what you gave, never that what you gave is true. "Not checked" is never shown
as checked;
a draft the safety rules or the reviewer refused is Not shown, with the
reason. So is a draft that states figures, dates or names that are not in
what you gave PULSE (most of its checkable sentences): PULSE keeps nothing
and lists the sentences, so you add the missing facts and ask again. This
check is always on; there is no setting for it.

An Instagram carousel shows its slide images, drawn by PULSE, exactly as they
would be posted: you approve the slides, not a description of them. Text that
does not fit a slide fails its check; it is never cut. Each hashtag shows its
size (posts a day: niche, medium or broad), measured from Instagram, or why it
was not measured.
A piece in My Library
My Library holds what was made, newest first, filed under its format's
group. A piece opens as the product itself: its words, slides, file, video or
episode, its checks and its status, and what you can do with it:

Edit its words and save them back to the same piece.
Approve and Schedule: the same as on the Campaigns board (see
Approve and schedule).
Automate: its own automation.
Download: see below.
Make another like this: a new card, prefilled with this piece's title and
what it was asked for.
How this was made: what you asked for, when PULSE kept it.
Delete: it leaves your library and will not be posted.

A PDF opens with Open the PDF, a video with Watch the video, and a
podcast plays in place.
Instagram pictures and videos
An Instagram piece needs your own picture or video before it can go out,
except a carousel (it posts its slides):

Instagram post: Attach your photo (one photo, from upright 4:5 to
wide 1.91:1).
Instagram Reel: Attach your video (MP4 or MOV, 3 seconds to 15
minutes; upright 9:16 looks best).
Instagram Stories: each photo or video you attach becomes one Story, in
order. Instagram does not let apps add stickers (polls, questions, links):
add those in the Instagram app after it is posted. Mentions need no
sticker: PULSE tags the checked accounts under Mentions (below).

PULSE checks the file against Instagram's rules before anything is sent.
Attaching publishes nothing.
A video made by PULSE. An Instagram post without a photo of your own is
posted as a Reel (add a photo in Studio to post it as a photo). When you
approve a Reel or Stories piece without a
video of your own, PULSE makes one from the script: the script's lines drawn on
upright frames and read aloud by your PULSE's speech service. The piece then
says Video made from the script: N s (Stories: N parts, each with
Watch part N). With no speech service, the video is made silent and says
No voiceover: speech service unavailable. If a video cannot be made, the
piece says why; the approval still goes through.
Instagram mentions
An Instagram piece (post, carousel, Reel or Stories) can mention other
accounts as @name. The Instagram skills propose mentions only from what PULSE
has on record, never a made-up name:

Partners you track with an Instagram handle (added by you, or found on a
page PULSE could verify);
Leads whose notes give their Instagram (Instagram: @name or an
instagram.com/name link);
Competitors PULSE found, only when you switch on May mention
competitors PULSE found before writing;
an @name you wrote in what you asked for.

A check refuses any other name in the draft, and its @ is taken away, so it
is neither mentioned nor tagged.
The piece shows its Mentions as chips. PULSE looks each account up on
Instagram (business discovery, which finds business and creator accounts):

checked: Instagram found it. It is written in the caption as @name and
tagged when the piece is posted: at the centre of the photo (a post, a
carousel's first slide), on the Reel, or on the first Story.
not checked: Instagram could not look it up (a personal account, a
name that does not exist, no Instagram connection, or a missing permission;
hover the chip for the reason). It stays in the caption as @name and is not
tagged. Keep it or remove it.

Remove a mention with the chip's ×, add one by typing a username or an
instagram.com link, or tap an account listed On record, not mentioned
yet (switch on Suggest competitors too to list competitors). Check
again on Instagram looks every mention up again. PULSE also looks them up
once more right before posting. Instagram allows 20 mentions in one caption.
Download
Download saves an approved, scheduled or sent piece as files you can post
yourself, whether the channel is connected or not:

An Instagram piece comes as one zip: the pictures (image.png for the
image PULSE drew when a photo post has no photo of yours, media-01,
media-02 … for your own photos, or
slide-01, slide-02 … for a carousel), the video PULSE made (reel.mp4, or
story-part-01.mp4 … for Stories) when it is small enough, and
caption.txt with the caption, each picture's description and the
Mentions (which PULSE tags and which it does not, and why). A video you
uploaded yourself is offered on its own, not in the zip.
Any other piece comes as one text file (a Markdown file for a blog
article) with its title, words, hashtags and call to action.

Or each file lists the files one by one, and anything missing says why
(for example an opening line too long to draw on one image).
Publishing
Approving a piece hands it to the schedule. Whether it goes out is decided
when it is due, behind several switches, all of which must agree:

The channel is connected and switched Active in Settings →
Integrations, and its card says Ready to publish.
Your administrator has publishing switched on for the whole PULSE and for
that channel. LinkedIn, the blog, the podcast and the audiobook also need you
to be one of your PULSE's named publishers.
With Autopilot on, the post waits for the account's best time.

If one says no, the post is held back (withheld), never sent later
without you, and the card says which. A channel PULSE cannot post to, or one
you have not connected, says: Not connected, so PULSE will not post it.
Download it and post it yourself, or connect it in Settings → Integrations.



Channel
What PULSE posts




Instagram
Posts, carousels, Reels and Stories


LinkedIn
Posts, as you or as a company page you administer


YouTube
YouTube Shorts, uploaded to your channel


Website
Blog articles, to your site through GitHub


Podcast and audiobook
Episodes in PULSE's own podcast feed



Facebook, X, newsletters and the other formats are yours to post: download
them. See Drafts, approval and publishing
and, for administrators, Switches and arming order.
Reports and PDFs
Report (under Long reads and audio) writes a performance report over a
period and the figures you ask it to highlight, as a PDF or a CSV. Guides,
study guides, mind maps, timelines and comparison tables are made as PDFs. See
Results and reports.

docs/user-guide/weekly-growth-advisor/.title: Weekly growth advisor
docs/user-guide/weekly-growth-advisor/.body:
Weekly growth advisor

Once a week PULSE can weigh a few ways to move your 90-day plan forward and
suggest one. It is off until you switch it on in Settings › Account › Weekly
results review. It only suggests: nothing is sent, posted, called or changed
until you approve, and approving makes one edit of your plan, as your own.
What it weighs. Two to four options, built only from what PULSE holds: the
open actions of your plan that are due, the weekly results review when one waits
for you, what PULSE has learned about your market (when you switched that on),
your own daily limits from My rules and Outreach settings, and the outcomes it
measured recently.
What each option shows. Only what the facts show:

Cost — a post or a send the option would use from your limits. Nothing
else is called a cost, and when it is not measured it is not shown.
Risks — too few measured results, a memory that is contradicted, a
pitfall PULSE remembered, a channel close to your own daily limit, or a kind
of suggestion you declined before.
Reversible — shown only when it is known. Work that ends in a post or a
send cannot be taken back once done (each step still waits for your approval);
changes to the plan itself can be edited back.

How it chooses. In a fixed order: measured results first, then fewer risks,
then reversibility, then cost, then the earlier planned week. The card says which
criterion decided and why each other option was dropped. An option whose channel
is already at your own daily limit is dropped.
When it says nothing. With no current plan, too little measured evidence
(the minimum comes from configuration), or fewer than two options, the week says
exactly that and suggests nothing. A figure nobody measured is never shown as
zero.
Your answer. Approve, or reject with one of five reasons (not the right
moment, the wrong channel, already handled, too risky, another reason). Leaving
it is an answer too: next week it is recorded as ignored. If you switched market
memory on, the outcome is kept there as a short structured note you can read,
correct or forget; nothing you wrote is overwritten.
What it did. "What it weighed" opens the options, the criterion and the facts
behind them, in your language.

docs/user-guide/digital-twins/.title: Digital twins
docs/user-guide/digital-twins/.body:
Digital twins and presenter videos

Digital twins are presenters for your presentations and course materials.
Open Digital twins in the Content group of the rail. A twin has a name,
an optional role ("Course instructor", "Product presenter"), a language
(English, Spanish, French or Portuguese), a voice and an appearance.
Status: built. Presenter videos with a voice-over work wherever the
platform's voice service runs. Your own recorded voice speaks only where that
service supports custom voices, and lip-synced videos only where your
administrator switched them on; the app says so when either is not available.
Built-in personas
PULSE comes with a small set of built-in personas. Their voices are the
platform's stock voices, each shown with its licence and attribution. A
built-in persona has a drawn cartoon face, not a photo. Tap one to hear a
short spoken greeting. Built-in personas need no consent
and cannot be deleted.
Your own twin
Choose New twin, give it a name, pick a language and a voice, and choose
an appearance: Initials only, a Photo or a Video. Then you can add:

Your voice: record it in the app ("Recording… speak naturally") or choose
a WAV file, 5 to 60 seconds, at most 16 MB.
A photo or video of yourself: a photo (PNG or JPEG, at most 10 MB) or a
short video (MP4 or QuickTime, at most 60 seconds and 100 MB).

Use only recordings of yourself. You see only your own twins and media; an
agency's client sees only its own.
Consent
Before any voice sample, photo or video is accepted, PULSE shows the consent
text with its version. You tick I have read this and I agree and confirm a
statement ("I confirm that the recording is of me and I agree to the consent
text."). The consent is recorded with the time. Without it, the upload is
refused. Consents on record lists each consent and when it was accepted or
withdrawn.
Withdraw consent deletes the recordings and videos made from them at once,
and the twin can no longer speak. Voice-overs
made in your own voice from that recording are deleted too. To use your voice or face again, make a new
twin with a new consent.
Edit a twin
Edit changes the twin's name, language, stock voice and appearance:

Replace photo or video attaches another photo or video (with its own
consent). The one it replaces is deleted, with the videos made from it.
Remove photo or video deletes the file and the videos made from it.
A twin that speaks with your own recorded voice keeps it; to use a stock
voice, make a new twin.
After a withdrawn consent, only the name can change.

Hear the twin speaks up to 300 characters in its voice. Delete twin
deletes the twin and its recordings.
Presenter videos
A presenter video is made from a script: up to 40 slides, each with a title,
up to 6 short points and the narration the twin reads (at most 1,500
characters a slide, 2,400 words in all). Its voice reads the narration over
the slides. The finished video is an MP4, at most 10 minutes. Text that does
not fit is refused with the slide named; it is never cut.
Every video says what it is:



Kind
Made from




Animated presenter (illustration), voice-over
A built-in persona


Presenter video, voice-over
Your own twin


Presenter video, lip-synced (AI-generated)
Your own twin, after Make it speak as me. Carries an "AI-generated" label. See Lip-synced presenter videos.



Videos are made in the background; when the server is busy, a new one waits
its turn. The panel shows progress. When a video is
ready, play or download it. A video still being made cannot be deleted.
Your twins, recordings and videos are part of your account data and are
deleted with your account. See the privacy policy.

docs/user-guide/market-memory/.title: What PULSE has learned about your market
docs/user-guide/market-memory/.body:
What PULSE has learned about your market

PULSE can keep a short list of plain statements about your market, built only
from counts of your own results: which channels and campaigns brought leads,
which posts got readable results, how many replies came in. It is off until you
switch on Learn from my results every week in Settings › Account. Nothing is
learned from a result with too little evidence, and a figure nobody measured is
never kept as zero.
Each entry says where it comes from (observed, stated or inferred), how
confident it is, how many results support it and how many said something
different. Entries hold no message text and no contact details: a statement with
a link, an e-mail address or a phone number is refused before it is kept.
You decide what stays. An editor or administrator can forget an entry
(it stays listed as forgotten, with the reason), correct it in their own words,
or delete everything that is kept. What you corrected or forgot is never
overwritten and never brought back by PULSE.
The tidy-up
When the app is quiet, PULSE tidies the list once a day for accounts that
switched learning on. It sets aside entries that have not been confirmed for a
long time and statements that were recorded twice, and it reports entries whose
results disagree without touching them. It never touches an entry you corrected
or forgot.
When a tidy-up found or set aside something, Settings shows one line with the
date and the counts, for example "2 not confirmed for a long time, 1 repeated,
3 with evidence that disagrees". When it had nothing to report, nothing is shown.
Entries set aside stay in the list as forgotten, and correcting one brings it
back.
Export and import (Open Knowledge Format)
Your list is yours to take with you. In Settings › Account, Export what PULSE
learned (OKF) saves what PULSE learned about your market, and only that, as a
bundle in the open Open Knowledge Format (a ZIP of plain text files). Entries you
forgot are left out; entries you corrected are marked as corrected by a person.
The download link works for a short time, and you can export once an hour. An
editor or administrator, signed in as a person, asks for it; the bundle is kept
sealed under your account and removed after two hours.
Import knowledge (OKF) reads a bundle your own account exported back into the
list, for example after you deleted everything. Learning must be switched on first.
Three things to know:

Only your own. A bundle from another account, or from another Runink app,
is refused, and so is a file that does not follow the format. The reason is
said in plain words.
Not yet confirmed. Every imported entry is marked "Imported, not yet
confirmed" and counts for little. Whatever the bundle says about itself, for
example that a person confirmed it, is ignored. Correct an entry to
confirm it.
Nothing you decided is changed. An entry you corrected or forgot, and one
already in the list, is left as it is. Statements with a link, an e-mail
address, a phone number or too much text are left out and counted, and at most
300 imported entries are kept per account.

The file is read in memory only and is limited in size and number of files, so a
damaged or oversized file is refused before anything is read. An export or import
writes one line with counts only in the server log, never a statement.
Drafting with what PULSE learned
A second switch, Use what PULSE learned when drafting (Settings › Account,
right under the learning switch), lets PULSE use some of these entries when it
writes a post, caption, story, reel or video script, a LinkedIn company update,
a newsletter or a blog article. It is off until you switch it on, and it works
only while weekly learning is on too.
What PULSE hands the writer:

A few entries only. At most five (your administrator can set up to ten),
chosen by plain rules, not by a model: the ones that name the channel being
written for or a word of your topic first, then the most confident, then the
most recent. Two drafts with the same inputs get the same entries.
Only entries PULSE can stand behind. An entry you forgot, one set aside as
not confirmed for a long time, one whose results disagree, one imported from a
bundle and not yet confirmed, and one that has faded below the confidence PULSE
needs are never used. Only entries built from counts of your own results
(channels, campaigns, posts and replies) are used, never anything about a
customer or a lead, and never text with a link, an e-mail address or a phone
number.
As data, not instructions. The writer is told to use them only where they
fit and never to state a figure they do not hold. A draft that cites one of
these figures is checked against it like any other fact you gave PULSE; a
draft that invents a figure is still held back.
Never in a reply or a message to a person. Comment replies, direct
messages, review replies and every extraction or audit step never see what
PULSE learned.

Under the switch Settings says what is missing: that learning is still off, that
the server still needs a setting, or No learned facts yet, which means no
entry qualifies yet and nothing is added to drafts (it is not a count of zero
results).
Which facts did a draft use? A draft written with learned facts shows
Informed by N learned facts in Studio. Tap it to see the entries, as they
are in your list now: a fact you forgot since says so. The draft itself keeps
only the entries' numbers, not a second copy of their text. If you forget or
correct an entry, the next draft changes; drafts already written keep what they
were written with. Each saved draft writes one line with counts only in the
server log, never a statement.

docs/user-guide/meeting-detection/.title: Meeting detection
docs/user-guide/meeting-detection/.body:
Meeting detection

PULSE can notice that a lead may have booked a meeting and ask you to
confirm it. It is off until you switch it on in Settings › Account › Weekly
results review. It never moves a lead by itself.
What it looks for. Only structured signals in replies to outreach you sent
from your own mailbox, read the same way replies are tracked:

a calendar invitation or an acceptance from the lead's own address. When a reply
shows nothing in its text, PULSE asks your Gmail mailbox for that one reply's
calendar part (at most 64 KiB, read-only, read for the moment and not kept). A
part that is too large to read whole is treated as unable to judge: nothing is
proposed from it. Other mailbox types give no calendar part for now;
a link to a known booking service (Calendly, Cal.com, SavvyCal, HubSpot
Meetings, Google Calendar and Outlook booking pages) in the reply. The link is
read as text and never opened;
a notification from a known calendar service.

What it keeps. A code (invitation received, invitation accepted, booking
link sent by the lead), the lead, a fixed source name and the start time when an
invitation names one. It does not keep the reply text, anyone's address or the
invitation itself.
What you do. A "Meeting detected" card appears on the plan page: We think a
meeting is booked. You choose Confirm (the lead moves to meeting booked, as
your own change, and its outreach sequence stops sending steps), Not a
meeting, or Ignore. Confirmed meetings are counted per channel and
campaign in Attribution.
Honest limits. Only calendar invitations and known links are detected.
Nothing detected is not the same as no meeting: a time agreed in plain words, by
phone or by a link PULSE does not know is not seen. If you have not switched
detection on, meetings per channel show as not measured, never as zero.

docs/user-guide/short-videos/.title: Short videos
docs/user-guide/short-videos/.body:
Short videos

PULSE can turn the script of a piece into a short video of 15 to 60 seconds:
your own pictures (or cards in your brand colours when you have none), each line
read aloud and shown as captions, slow movement between the pictures, and a
closing card with your brand. Every short is a draft. It waits in the
approval queue with the piece, and nothing is scheduled, posted or sent until you
approve the piece.
Make one. Open Studio › My Library › Short videos, choose Make a short
video, pick one of your pieces that has a script, the shape (vertical, square or
wide) and the file type (MP4 or WebM). The list shows each video as queued,
composing, ready or failed, with the scenes done so far. When it is ready you can
play it in the app, approve the piece, discard the video or make it again. A
failure says why in plain words (for example, the script is too long for a short,
or the voice could not be made).
Your pictures. PULSE uses the pictures already in your account, newest first.
It never uses another account's. A scene without a picture is drawn as a card in
your brand colours; with no brand known, the closing card uses PULSE's own colours
and logo.
The voice. The script is read by a synthetic voice, in the piece's language.
A video made with it says so: it is labelled AI-generated voice in the app and
in the file. If the voice is not available, a video you ask for is made without
a voice and says so; the daily draft is not made at all. There is no background
music.
One a day, if you ask for it. In Settings › Account you can switch on the
daily short-video draft. It is off until you do. Then, at most once a day, for
one of your active campaigns that has YouTube switched on, PULSE writes the lines
of a short, makes the video and puts the piece in your approval queue. It never
publishes by itself; approving the piece goes through the same checks as any other
piece. Your administrator can stop it for everyone.
When it is not available. If the server cannot make video, the page says so
and the Make button is disabled; nothing is sent anywhere.
Deleting. Discarding a video deletes its file. Deleting your account deletes
your videos.
Made with the script
When you ask Studio for a script (a YouTube Short, an Instagram Reel or Story), the
same request also makes a short video of it and a picture for it, as drafts on the
piece. You see the script, the video with its progress (queued, being made, ready) and
the picture together, and each part has its own "make again". The picture is a
branded card in your colours, or an AI picture when you have switched AI pictures on
in Settings; each says which it is. If the video takes a while it says it is still
being made. Nothing is sent or published until you approve the piece.
Audio, and what to do when something is missing
The same request also makes the audio of the script: the lines spoken with a synthetic
voice, kept as a draft voice-over on the piece (listed in the Voice-over studio too) and labelled
"AI-generated voice". Any piece with words, not only a script, has the same two actions on its card:
Make a short video and Make audio (the Voice-over studio). Neither needs a switch to be turned on. When the voice service is not
available the card does not stay empty: it says why in words (voice switched off, the
server's voice key missing or refused, the service not answering) and offers to try again.
A video made while the voice was unavailable is marked "No voice"; make the audio, or make
the video again, once the voice is back.

docs/user-guide/answer-vendor-pitches/.title: Answer vendor pitches
docs/user-guide/answer-vendor-pitches/.body:
Answer vendor pitches

Companies and freelancers write to you to sell what you sell, or something close
to it: an agency, an outsourcing team, a lead-generation or marketing tool.
Answer vendor pitches in Runink PULSE: Prescriptive Unified Lead & Social
Engine answers them for you with your own counter-offer: become our client,
or partner with us, with your team paid upfront as your terms say. A vendor who
answers with interest becomes a record in your partner pipeline.
It is off until you switch it on, in Settings › Account › Answer vendor
pitches, for your account only. Switching it on means that, from then on, a
pitch PULSE is sure about is answered without asking you first. A message it
is not sure about waits for you.
Your terms are the only wording
You fill in, in your own words:

what you offer a vendor who becomes your client;
what you offer a vendor who becomes your partner;
how your team is paid upfront;
your signature, and optionally a booking link (https).

PULSE writes the reply from these and from the vendor's own words, quoted back.
It never adds a price, a term, a discount or a figure of its own: a number
appears only if you typed it. Until every term and your Outreach sender name and
postal address are filled in, PULSE does nothing, and the card lists exactly
what is missing. There are no default terms.
The reply is in the vendor's language when it is English, French, Spanish or
Portuguese, otherwise English. It says it was written by an AI assistant and sent
on behalf of your team, and carries your sender name, postal address and a
one-click unsubscribe link, like your other emails.
What it answers, and what it never does
PULSE decides what a message is from fixed rules, not from guesses. It answers
only an unsolicited pitch for a service or tool. It never answers:

a lead, a customer, someone already in your pipeline, or a reply in a
conversation you already have;
your own address or domain;
an automatic message: an out-of-office, a bounce, a mailing list, a no-reply
sender;
spam or a phishing attempt (no link is opened);
anything that tries to give PULSE instructions.

It answers each sender once, and at most ten a day. Someone who writes
"stop", "unsubscribe" or the same in French, Spanish or Portuguese goes on your
suppression list and nothing more is sent to them; "not interested" ends their
record.
Where it listens
Each channel is shown on the card with what is on, what is off and why, taken
from what is really set up:

Your website form: the vendor's email is in the enquiry, and the answer
goes from your own mailbox. A pitch PULSE answers is not made into a lead.
Instagram direct messages: through the same reader as Autopilot, inside
Instagram's 24-hour answer window.
E-mail: PULSE follows replies to the emails it sent. To also see a pitch that
arrives only in your mailbox, switch on Read my inbox for vendor pitches
(below). It is off until you do, Gmail only for now, and the card says why when
it cannot read (reconnect to allow, Gmail only, slowed down by the provider).
LinkedIn: not available. LinkedIn gives PULSE no way to read direct
messages.
WhatsApp and SMS: not available. Only contacts you have allowed reach
PULSE, and each message needs a person's confirm tap.
Website chat: not available. A visitor stays anonymous, so there is no
address to answer.

Read my inbox for vendor pitches
A second switch in Settings › Account, separate from the one above and OFF until
you turn it on. Both must be on. With it on, PULSE reads new mail in your
connected Gmail inbox, read-only, and gives each message to the same answering
steps as a website enquiry.

What it reads: the inbox folder only. A sub-option, also off, adds the
promotions, updates, social and forums tabs. Spam is never read, and mail you
sent is never looked at.
From when: only mail received after you switched it on. The moment is
shown on the card. Turning it off and on again, or adding the promotions
option, moves that moment forward. The first read goes back no further than 7
days from it.
What it never answers: automatic replies, mailing lists, bulk mail and
no-reply senders (the usual headers say so), a message that is itself a reply
in a thread, and anyone you already know.
What it keeps: a position marker and counts, nothing of the messages. The
sender, subject and a short snippet are read for the moment and never written to
a log; what a pitch record keeps is what it kept before.
What the card shows: the last read time, counts by kind (read, skipped
because sent, spam or older than the switch, and each class of pitch) and, when
something is wrong, the reason in words: reconnect your mailbox and allow
reading, Gmail only for now, the provider asked PULSE to slow down (with the
time of the next try), the provider could not be reached, or the daily limit was
reached.

Safety rules that still apply
An answer goes out only if your administrator has armed sending, the channel's
own switch is on, and My rules and the conscience check allow it: your
never-contact list, working hours, daily caps and any rule that asks for approval
of a first contact. Each answer is recorded, and What PULSE did and why shows
what was checked. If a rule holds a reply, it waits for you.
What you do
Under Leads › Partners, Vendors who answered our offer lists every vendor
with its stage: pitched, answered, interested, call proposed, agreed or
declined. PULSE moves a record forward as the vendor answers, and proposes; only
you mark a vendor agreed.
A reply that waits for you shows its text with Approve (sent through the same
checks), Edit and Reject. The card keeps a short log of what PULSE did:
the channel, the kind of message and the outcome, never the vendor's words.
From a pitch to a lead or a partner
A vendor is not only someone to answer. When a sender shows interest in your
counter-offer, or the message itself shows they could buy from you, PULSE
proposes two things and you decide:

Partner: the record is already in your partner pipeline.
Lead: Could this vendor be a lead? with Accept and Dismiss. Accepting
makes a lead from a business email address (never a personal mailbox, never a
sender who asked to stop), with the source vendor pitch and the stage new. If
you already have a lead at that address, the two are linked, not duplicated.
Nothing is sent and no outreach sequence starts: your outreach approval rules
are unchanged.

A sender stays one record, whether it moves between partner and lead.
What vendors pitching us tell us
From each pitch PULSE keeps a few codes, not the message: what the sender sells
(a category such as SEO, lead generation, outsourcing or software), the
differentiators they claim (a free audit, a guarantee, and so on), the kind of
pricing they name (per seat, per lead, retainer, performance, flat, or not stated;
never the amounts), the channel, which of your own offerings the message overlaps
and what the sender did after your counter-offer.
Settings › Account › What vendors pitching us tell us adds them up over a window:
the most common categories, which are rising, the common claims, how many overlap
what you sell, and categories senders pitch that your offerings never mention.
Every line is what senders claimed, never a fact about the market, and each shows
how many pitches are behind it, with the records in Leads › Partners. A count nobody
measured is not shown, never shown as zero. Until the window and the minimum number
of pitches are set by your administrator, and until that many pitches have arrived,
the card says so and shows nothing.
Each week with something measured, PULSE adds a weekly digest to the card for
you to read and mark reviewed. It is shown in the app only; nothing is emailed or
sent. You can also ask the assistant about these insights.
What PULSE keeps, and for how long
For each pitch it answers, PULSE keeps a summary: the sender's address and
company, one sentence they wrote about what they sell, the reply it drafted, and
the codes above. It does not keep the message itself. After 90 days (your
administrator can change this) the address, company, quoted sentence and draft are
erased; the codes, the stage and a one-way marker stay, so the same sender is still
answered only once and the insights still count. A reply still waiting for you, or
a lead proposal you have not decided, is kept until you decide. Deleting your
account removes all of it, and your data export includes it.
Questions: contact@runink.org.

docs/user-guide/lip-synced-presenter-vid.title: Lip-synced presenter videos
docs/user-guide/lip-synced-presenter-vid.body:
Lip-synced presenter videos

A lip-synced presenter video is a presenter video in which your own twin
speaks the script and the mouth follows what is said. It is made from your
own photo, or a short video of your face, on the platform's own servers: no
outside service sees your photo.
Before you start

It is for your own twin, the one you made from your own photo or video.
The built-in personas are not real people and use their own drawn avatar.
The twin's appearance consent must be active. If you withdraw it, a
lip-synced video in progress is stopped and every lip-synced video made from
your face is deleted; deleting the twin does the same.
A clear, front-facing photo works best.
The button Make it speak as me is disabled, with the reason, when your
administrator has not switched lip-sync on (PULSE_LIPSYNC), the service is
not available, or the consent was withdrawn.

What happens when you press it

PULSE first makes the usual voice-over presenter video from your script.
It is ready straight away, and it says plainly that the lips do not move.
Your request then waits its turn, so it can take several minutes. The panel
shows its progress and an estimate ("about 4 minutes").
When it is done, the voice-over video is replaced by the lip-synced one,
labelled "presenter video, lip-synced (AI-generated)". You can play and
download it.

You can cancel at any time: the voice-over video stays as it is.
If something goes wrong, the voice-over video is kept and the panel says why in
plain words, for example "try a clear front-facing photo". Try again starts
a new request.
The AI-generated label
Every lip-synced video shows an "AI-generated" label on the picture.
PULSE offers no way to switch the label off.
Your photo and your privacy
Your photo is used only to make the video. The lip-synced video is yours alone,
listed with your account data and deleted with it.

docs/user-guide/weekly-roadmap-suggestio.title: Weekly roadmap suggestions
docs/user-guide/weekly-roadmap-suggestio.body:
Weekly roadmap suggestions

Once a week Runink PULSE can suggest new posts for your roadmap, so the
roadmap does not wait for you to write it. It is off until you switch on
Suggest new roadmap posts every week in Settings › Account. It only
suggests: nothing is added to your roadmap, drafted, scheduled or sent until you
approve, and what you approve is added as your own.
What it works from. Only what PULSE holds for your active campaign:

the results it measured (post results and which channel or campaign brought
leads, first touch);
the content gaps your audit found, and the ideas of your audit's content
scenarios;
what your roadmap already holds, so a topic is never suggested twice;
how many posts a week you said you can manage on each channel, so it never
fills a week beyond that;
what PULSE has learned about your market, when you switched that on (only as a
risk noted on a post, for example a pitfall it remembered).

What a suggestion contains. A channel, a format, a day and time, a topic and,
when PULSE could word one, an opening line (a hook). The topic is the wording of
the audit row it comes from, never invented. The channel is one where enough
results were measured; a channel nobody measured gets nothing and is listed as
not measured, never as zero. The format is a starting choice, because results
are not measured per format, and the card says so. At the ratio your plan sets,
one post in every few is the one that sells.
Every post shows its evidence. Each suggested post lists the measured
results it rests on. A post PULSE has no evidence for is not suggested.
When it says nothing. With no active campaign that has a content plan, no
free capacity in the coming two weeks, too few measured results (the minimum
comes from configuration), or no topic that is not already on your roadmap, the
week says exactly that and suggests nothing.
Your answer. On the Plan page, the card Roadmap suggestions offers:

Add to my roadmap — exactly the listed posts are added, as your own;
Edit — change a topic, a hook or a day, or leave a post out, then add;
Reject — with one of five reasons (not the right moment, the wrong topics,
the wrong channel, already planned, another reason). Rejecting changes nothing.

Leaving it is an answer too: next week it is recorded as ignored and replaced.
What it weighed opens the record of what PULSE looked at and chose, in your
language.
Drafts ahead of time
A second, separate switch, Draft approved roadmap posts ahead of time, is
also off until you switch it on. For the posts you approved from these
suggestions, PULSE writes the draft a few days before the post's day, the way
the Studio writes one for you, and leaves it in your approval queue.

It drafts only posts you approved from a suggestion, and only when their day is
today or coming soon (three days ahead unless your administrator sets another
number). A post whose day has passed is left alone.
It writes at most a couple of drafts a day (your administrator sets the
number), and one at a time behind the other background work.
A draft is never approved, scheduled or sent for you. You approve it as
you would any draft; only then does your best-time queue and every check you
have set (My rules, the channel switches, the approval itself) decide what
happens next. Your Autopilot works as it did.
Each draft carries the same scores and the same note about what it could and
could not check against your facts as any draft from the Studio.

Settings › Account shows what was recorded: the latest week, how many posts it
listed and whether it was answered, how many drafts were made in the last 24
hours out of the daily limit, how many approved posts still wait for a draft, and
when the latest draft was made.

docs/user-guide/autopilot-and-agencies/.title: Autopilot and agencies
docs/user-guide/autopilot-and-agencies/.body:
Autopilot and agencies

PULSE is your marketing agency in an app. You approve the posts; PULSE does
the rest of the work an agency would: it posts them at the right time, keeps
an eye on the comments, and tells you every week what it did and what came of
it. Agencies use the same app to run all their clients, each in its own
space.
Autopilot: PULSE runs the account after you approve
Turn it on per account under Settings › Integrations › Autopilot. With
Autopilot on:

Approving a post queues it at the account's best time instead of
sending it at once. Nothing you have not approved is ever queued.
Best time comes from the results of your own posts. Until there are
enough, and enough in the same weekday and hour to compare them, the card
says PULSE's starting schedule, not measured yet.
How often follows your campaign board (the number of pieces planned
for that week on that channel). You can set your own pace instead, or go
back to the board.
Every send is recorded, with what happened: posted,
held back by a switch, or failed with the platform's reason (on the post's step trail, and under Recent dispatches on its Integrations card). A short outage
is retried.
It stops by itself when the connection expires, when the platform asks
PULSE to slow down, or after repeated failed posts. Leads › To do
today then says so in plain words with a Reconnect link. Resume moves
the posts that waited to the next good times, so nothing goes out in a
burst.
Pause and Resume are one tap. Turning Autopilot off cancels its
queued posts; the content stays approved.

The server's publishing switches still have the last word: if your
administrator has switched publishing off, Autopilot posts nothing and the
card says so. See Switches and arming order.
Comments and replies
On LinkedIn, Instagram and YouTube, each new comment on a post PULSE
published gets a drafted reply under Replies waiting for you on Campaigns
(Needs you now on Brand Analysis counts them). Edit it, send it, or dismiss it. On Instagram, posts that tag your
account (mentions) and direct messages land there too, each marked as a
comment, a mention or a message. A message can be answered only within 24 hours
of the person's last message; after that PULSE says so and sends nothing.
YouTube has no mentions or direct messages, and the app says "not available on
YouTube". If the connection lacks a permission, the account says Reconnect to
allow … (see Connect your accounts).
PULSE never makes comments up.
Answer simple comments by itself is off until you turn it on, and then
covers only:

a thank-you to a kind comment,
an answer taken from FAQ content you approved,
your opening hours or a link to your own website.

Even then the reply goes out only after PULSE's safety rules and
its plan check both agree; otherwise it waits for you. Everything else, a
complaint, a price question, an order, always waits for you.
Your rules apply to every reply
Every reply is checked against My rules and the persona you chose, the same
way an email or a post is, before it leaves. When PULSE answers by itself it
acts as an agent with its own limits: a public comment reply follows the
marketing agent's (at most 10 a day), a direct message follows the
partnerships agent's (contact hours 9 to 18, at most 10 a day, no first-contact
approval because the person wrote first). Those limits only restrict. A reply
that your rules do not allow, or that only warn and nobody was there to
confirm, is never sent: it waits under Replies waiting for you with the
reason, and What was checked shows each step in your language. When you
send a waiting reply yourself, a warning asks you to confirm it; a block stays
held and says why. Your own approval is not restricted by an agent's limits.
What PULSE did, this week
In What PULSE did on Brand Analysis, This week shows: posts published,
replies sent (and how many PULSE sent on its own), the
reactions, comments and views the platforms reported, and what is queued
next. A figure no platform reported is shown as not measured, never as 0.
Email me this sends it to you from your own connected mailbox.
For agencies: one space per client
Under Settings › Clients, add each client business. Each client has its
own brand, accounts, Autopilot, approvals and reports, and one client never
sees another client's data. Switch between your own business and your
clients from the business switcher at the top right of every page.
Give people a role on each client:

Agency admin: runs everything for that client and adds people.
Client approver: sees the work and approves or rejects posts and
replies. Nothing else. Use this for the client's owner.

Everyone you add must already use this PULSE; billing stays per seat.
Not yet: billing per client, a white-label report, and per-client HubSpot and
GitHub connections (those stay on each person's own account).

docs/user-guide/create-an-image/.title: Create an image
docs/user-guide/create-an-image/.body:
Create an image

Create image turns a short description into up to four pictures, made
on the platform's own servers. Every picture is a draft marked
"AI-generated". Nothing is used in a post, published or sent until you
approve it, and the piece it belongs to still goes through its own approval.
Before you start

It is off until you switch it on: Settings › Account › Image creation (or
the button on the Create image card). Your administrator also has to have it
switched on for the server; when they have not, the card says so.
Only a person can make an image: an editor or an administrator, in the app.
Automated agents never make one, they may only suggest a description.
Each account can ask for a fixed number of pictures a day, and up to four at
a time.

Make one

Open Studio and pick Create image (or open a piece and choose
Create image in its card).
Describe what the picture shows. Pick the shape (square, portrait,
landscape or story), a style and how many.
The picture is made around your brand colours (Settings › Account ›
Brand colours). With none set, neutral tones are used. Pictures carry no
text and no logos: write text and add your logo in your post.
The card shows each step: waiting in line, making your image, ready.
Approve a draft to let its piece use it, Discard it to delete the
file, or Make again for a new set from the same description.

What is not made
A request is checked before anything is made, and a refusal says why in plain
words. Images are not made of children or young people, sexual or violent
content, hate or self-harm, real people (or anyone who looks like them), other
brands, logos or artists' styles, medical or legal claims, fake reviews,
testimonials or endorsements, or political persuasion. A picture that does not
pass the safety check after it is made is deleted and never shown.
Where the pictures live
Your pictures are stored privately under your account and are deleted with it.
Discard deletes the file at once. Each file carries a note that it is
AI-generated.

docs/user-guide/first-response-to-enquir.title: First response to enquiries
docs/user-guide/first-response-to-enquir.body:
First response to enquiries

When someone writes to you through your website form,
the first answer matters. First response in Runink PULSE: Prescriptive Unified
Lead & Social Engine writes a short acknowledgement for each new enquiry: it
says the message was received, what you do, and when a person will follow up, in
your own words. It also measures how long you take to answer.
It is off until you switch it on, in Settings › Account › First response to
website enquiries, for your account only. By default it only prepares a draft
and waits for you: nothing is sent until you tap Send.
What it answers, and what it never does
PULSE answers only a new lead that arrived through the website form with a
business email address. It never answers:

a personal address (a free mailbox);
an address on your suppression list, or your own address or domain;
a customer, or someone at a company that is already your customer;
someone you already contacted, or who is in an outreach sequence;
an enquiry that arrived before you switched it on: arming it never answers
a backlog;
someone a second time. One acknowledgement per lead, ever.

What the message says
The acknowledgement is a fixed template, not a model's writing. It uses the
person's first name only when it is a plain name, your business name, up to three
of your own offering names, and your own follow-up wording. It never repeats
what the person wrote, and nothing the person wrote can change the reply or where
it goes. It never contains a price, a delivery date or a promise: a figure appears
only if you typed one yourself.
You set the follow-up sentence in the card, in one line (for example, "We answer
within one working day."). If you leave it empty, the message says only that a
person on your team will read it and get back to you.
The message is in the person's language when it is English, French, Spanish or
Portuguese, otherwise English. It says it was written by an AI assistant and sent
on behalf of your team, and carries your sender name, postal address and a
one-click unsubscribe link, like your other emails.
Until your Outreach sender name and postal address are filled in, and your
administrator has set an https public address for the unsubscribe link, PULSE does
nothing, and the card lists exactly what is missing.
Draft first, automatic only if you ask



Setting
Default
What it does




First response
Off
Prepares a draft for each new enquiry.


Send acknowledgements automatically
Off
Sends only the clearest cases without your tap.



A drafted acknowledgement appears under Leads › Inbound with Send, Edit
and Reject. Send runs the same checks as an automatic send, with you as
the sender.
Automatic sending covers only a form with a business address that is not
suppressed and not a customer, and whose text holds nothing that looks like an
instruction. It sends only inside your working hours and under your daily cap;
otherwise it waits and sends later. Everything else stays a draft for you. It
applies only to enquiries that arrive after you switched automatic sending on.
The checks every message passes
An acknowledgement goes out only if your administrator has armed email sending,
and My rules and the conscience check allow it (your never-contact list,
working hours, caps and any rule that asks for approval). If a rule holds it, it
stays a draft with the reason, and What PULSE did and why shows what was
checked. Each automatic send is recorded there.
Response time
Under Leads › Inbound, the Response time card shows:

the median and the 90th percentile time from "received" to your first
email to that lead (the acknowledgement or your own first email, whichever came
first), over a window, once there are enough answered leads. With too few, or
when the window is not set up on the server, it says Not measured, never
zero;
how many leads have no first response yet. If you set a number of hours in
the card, only leads that have waited longer than that count; otherwise all of
them.

Only two timestamps are kept for this, when the enquiry arrived and when the first
email went out. The enquiry's text is not kept for it.
Related

Website form and Leads
Automations on enquiries and replies
Administrator: First response to enquiries

docs/user-guide/inbox/.title: Inbox
docs/user-guide/inbox/.body:
Inbox

Leads › Inbox is one read-only place that shows what Runink PULSE:
Prescriptive Unified Lead & Social Engine has read and what it did about it. It
covers every channel PULSE reads for you: your website form,
your mailbox (when you switched inbox reading on), replies to your outreach
emails and Instagram direct messages.
It changes nothing. You cannot send, approve or edit from here. Anyone who can
read your leads can open it, and it shows your own account only.
What a row shows
Each row is one message PULSE handled, written as facts. The message itself is
never shown here: no subject, no text, no address, no company name. Those stay
on their own screens (the lead, the partner pitch), which the row links to.



Fact
What it tells you




Channel
Website form, Mailbox, Replies to outreach or Instagram DMs.


Received
When the message reached you. For a record made before PULSE kept that time, the time PULSE read it, and the row says so.


Class
What kind of sender it is: a vendor-pitch class, the lead's status in Leads › Inbound, a reply, or a direct message.


What PULSE did
Replied, Held for a person, Skipped, Spam ignored, Recorded, Not handled yet or Failed, with a reason when there is one.


Decided by
PULSE under your own rules, a person, or nobody yet.


First response
How long it took from "received" to the first email or message actually sent, or why it is not measured.


Links
Open the lead, Open the partner pitch or Open the reply queue, and What was checked when a check was made before a send.



Filters and counts
Filter by channel, by what PULSE did and by when it was received
(last 7, 30 or 90 days, or any time). The count above the list and the chips
under it follow the filters. The list shows 50 rows at a time; Show more loads
the next ones. If your account holds more records than one read looks at, the
newest are listed and the screen says the oldest are left out.
First-response time
At the top, each channel that has a first-response clock shows the median and
the 90th percentile of the time from "received" to "first sent", over the
window your administrator set, once enough messages were answered. With too few,
or when the window is not set up on the server, it says Not measured and says
