The public https origin. The base of every sign-in redirect (/oauth/social/callback, /oauth/search-console/callback, /oauth/mail/callback), of the signed /media/ links Instagram fetches, and of absolute podcast-feed links. See Public address and redirects.


APP_VERSION
The version stamped on log lines.


FEATURED_MESSAGES_PATH
The file behind the featured-message strip.


A2A_ORGANIZATION
The organization named on the A2A agent card. Falls back to RUNINK_ORG, then TIDDE_GITHUB_ORG, then empty.


SELF_HEAL_AUTONOMOUS
false (or another no) turns automatic self-healing remediation off; plans are still recorded. Default: on. See Operations.



Security



Variable
Effect




PULSE_JWT_SECRET
Required. The key that signs and verifies every session. There is no default. It must never be a value that has been committed anywhere.


TIDDE_ENVELOPE_KEK
Required. The key that seals OAuth tokens in PULSE's store. The store refuses to open without it.


SECRET_BACKEND
Where secrets are read from. file reads each one from SECRETS_DIR/; any other value reads the process environment.


SECRETS_DIR
The directory the file backend reads. Default /var/run/secrets.


PULSE_TLS_CERT, PULSE_TLS_KEY
In-process TLS for direct exposure. Set both or neither. TLS 1.2 minimum, forward-secret AEAD suites only.


MESH_MTLS
true requires mutual TLS on the listener, with rotating certificates from the shared mesh CA. Takes precedence over PULSE_TLS_*. TLS 1.3 only.


MESH_CA_CERT, MESH_CA_KEY
The mesh CA, from the secret store. Needed when MESH_MTLS=true.


MESH_ISSUER_URL, MESH_ISSUER_TOKEN_FILE
The preferred mesh identity: the pod makes its own key and enrols it with TIDDE's mesh issuer, authenticated by the projected ServiceAccount token in the file. MESH_CA_CERT is then only the trust bundle and MESH_CA_KEY is not read. Without MESH_ISSUER_URL, the older shared-CA path (MESH_CA_CERT + MESH_CA_KEY) still works and logs an error on every start.


MESH_ADVERTISE_IP, MESH_ADVERTISE_HOST
Extra IP and DNS names on the mesh certificate.


LICENSE, LICENSE_FILE, LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY
An offline licence, inline or as a file, and the key that verifies it. With no licence there is no gating.



Sign-in and users



Variable
Effect




PULSE_ADMIN_PASSWORD (or ADMIN_PASSWORD)
Seeds the break-glass admin. Without it, no password login exists.


PULSE_ADMIN_USERNAME, PULSE_ADMIN_EMAIL
Overrides the break-glass admin's username (admin) and email.


GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
The Google OAuth client. Without it, Google sign-in is off.


OIDC_ISSUER
Overrides the token issuer that Google sign-in trusts.


AUTH_GOOGLE_ONLY
true hides the password form.


AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS
The Google sign-in allowlist. Empty means nobody signs in with Google.


AUTH_SEED_USERS
Operator-granted roles as email=persona,…. Applied at every start.


PULSE_CLIENT_INSTANCE, PULSE_CLIENT_INSTANCE_NAMESPACE
Set by Runink: which deployment this is, so the Admin page can write member changes back to the platform.


GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
The Google OAuth client's secret: Connect with YouTube, Search Console and Gmail, and token refresh. See Google.


GOOGLE_TOKEN_ENDPOINT
Overrides Google's token endpoint (tests).



See Users and access.
Storage



Variable
Effect




PULSE_DATA_DIR
Scratch directory (renders, clones). Nothing durable is kept there. Default ./data.


PULSE_APPFS_BUCKET
Bucket of the sealed app root on the object store: every table, account, session and media file. Default pulse; the TIDDE platform sets it.


PULSE_APPFS_DIR
Local sealed app root when there is no object store. Default $PULSE_DATA_DIR/appfs.


OBJECTSTORE_ENDPOINT, OBJECTSTORE_ACCESS_KEY, OBJECTSTORE_SECRET_KEY
The object store the app root is mounted on (the platform's object store).


OBJECTSTORE_BUCKET
The object store bucket.



Inference



Variable
Effect




INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL
Use the shared inference plane at this address: the platform's model router in your deployment.


INFERENCE_MODEL
The model name PULSE asks the inference plane for. Unset, PULSE uses the platform default. In a cluster the name is only a label.


INFERENCE_API_KEY
Key for the inference server.


MODEL_VISION, VISION_REMOTE_URL
The vision model that describes photos and video frames attached to an audit, and where to send them. off turns it off. Without it, attached photos are marked "image understanding unavailable".


PULSE_JUDGEMENT
off disables the plan gate.


PULSE_EGRESS_ALL_AGENTS
Widens output screening to every agent. Screened answers arrive whole instead of streaming.


TIDDE_HEALTH_URL
Where agent health reports go. Unset means no reports.



See Sovereign inference.
Connections
Each person connects their own accounts under Settings › Integrations. These
are the instance's app clients that make one-click sign-in possible; all are
secrets from the instance's secret store.



Variable
Effect




META_APP_ID, META_APP_SECRET
Connect with Instagram. See Meta.


LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID, LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET
Connect with LinkedIn. See LinkedIn.


LINKEDIN_COMPANY_PAGES
true once LinkedIn approved the Community Management API: offers company pages.


MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID, MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET, MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID
Connect Microsoft 365 (tenant default common). See Email.



GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET (under Sign-in) serve YouTube,
Search Console and Gmail too.
Site audit and scoring



Variable
Effect




PULSE_SCORING_CONFIG
A JSON file overlaid on the built-in scoring config.


PULSE_SITE_AUDIT_URL
The site the daily audit engine checks. Falls back to PULSE_SITE_BASE_URL. The engine also needs PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true before it starts.



Weekly learning



Variable
Effect




PULSE_RESULTS_PLAN_WINDOW_DAYS, PULSE_RESULTS_PLAN_MIN_EVIDENCE
The weekly results review: how many days of results it reads, and how many outcomes one row needs before it may propose a change. Whole numbers above zero. Unset or invalid means the review proposes nothing. Each account still switches the review on itself.


PULSE_MARKET_MEMORY_WINDOW_DAYS, PULSE_MARKET_MEMORY_MIN_EVIDENCE
The weekly market learning: how many days of results it reads, and how many outcomes one row needs before anything is remembered from it. Whole numbers above zero. Unset or invalid means it learns nothing. Each account still switches it on itself.


PULSE_ADVISOR_WINDOW_DAYS, PULSE_ADVISOR_MIN_EVIDENCE
The weekly growth advisor: how many days of results it reads, and how many outcomes one row needs before an option may rest on it. Whole numbers above zero. Unset or invalid means it suggests nothing. Each account still switches it on itself.



Publishing



Variable
Effect




PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED
The global kill switch. Only the exact value true arms anything.


PULSE_PUBLISH_
Narrows one channel: BLOG, PODCAST, AUDIOBOOK, YOUTUBE, INSTAGRAM, SPOTIFY, LINKEDIN, EMAIL, WHATSAPP, SMS, and the reply keys LINKEDIN_REPLIES, INSTAGRAM_REPLIES, INSTAGRAM_DMS, YOUTUBE_REPLIES.


PULSE_PUBLISH_AUTOMATIONS
Lets automations do outbound work. Off by default.


PULSE_EMAIL_DAILY_LIMIT
Emails one person may send per 24 hours. Default 50.


PULSE_OPPORTUNITIES_DISCOVERY
The daily read of open procurement data. On by default.


PULSE_PUBLISH_CONFIG_PATH, PULSE_PUBLISH_CONFIG_JSON
The per-channel arming file, or the same JSON inline.


PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS
Comma-separated PULSE user ids allowed to publish through the deployment-global channels (LinkedIn, blog, podcast, audiobook). Empty means nobody.


PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY
Arms the audit-fix modes of ApplyAuditActions (apply/commit/pr), on top of PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true. Off unless an explicit yes. Admins only.


PULSE_APPLY_ROOT
The only directory an audit-fix repo_path may resolve into. Unset refuses every mode, plan included.


PULSE_SITE_REPO, PULSE_SITE_BRANCH, PULSE_SITE_BLOG_DIR, PULSE_SITE_PUBLISH_MODE, PULSE_SITE_AUTHOR, PULSE_SITE_BASE_URL
Blog publishing to your website.


PULSE_GIT_AUTHOR_NAME, PULSE_GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL
The author on commits PULSE makes.


YOUTUBE_PRIVACY_STATUS
public, unlisted, or private. Unset means private.


LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN, LINKEDIN_AUTHOR_URN, LINKEDIN_API_VERSION
The deployment's LinkedIn token (from a secret) and author (person or organization URN), used only for a user with no LinkedIn connection; and the API version header.


LINKEDIN_API_BASE
Overrides LinkedIn's API base (tests).


PULSE_LINKEDIN_CTA_URL
The link the daily LinkedIn draft ends with. Default https://runink.org.


PULSE_PODCAST_TITLE, PULSE_PODCAST_DESCRIPTION, PULSE_PODCAST_LANGUAGE
Podcast feed metadata.



The defaults and the safe order to turn these on are on
Switches and arming order. See
Publishing controls and
Site pipeline.
Media



Variable
Effect




PULSE_SHORTS_ENGINE
Default on. Exactly off stops the daily short-video draft for every account (the kill switch). Each account also switches the draft on for itself in Settings › Account (default off); see Short videos.


PULSE_SHORTS_DAILY_CAP
How many short-video drafts one account gets a day (0 to 10). Default and fallback 1.


PULSE_VOICEOVER_MAX_PARALLEL
How many voice-overs the server speaks at once, for all accounts together (1 to 4). Default and fallback 1: the speech service is shared GPU capacity, so a job waits as "queued" for a free slot. Each account still has one voice-over being made at a time. A voice-over is a kept job that goes on when the app is closed; a server restart marks the ones it was making as interrupted, and the person tries them again.


FFMPEG_PATH
Overrides the ffmpeg binary for the audiobook assembler. Short videos use the server's own video tool, which is checked when the server starts: if the check fails no video is made, and /health says so.



Telephony and messaging



Variable
Effect




PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS
One of the switches an AI call needs (with PULSE_AI_CALLS). Off by default. Callers must also be editor or admin.


TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID, TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
The carrier account behind WhatsApp, SMS and Send / Call. Both are secrets.


TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM, TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER, TWILIO_VOICE_FROM
The WhatsApp sender, the SMS number, and the number calls are placed from. TWILIO_VOICE_FROM is optional and falls back to TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER.


PULSE_WHATSAPP_USER_ID
Which user's HubSpot connection backs the WhatsApp sender allowlist, and as whom replies run.


PULSE_WHATSAPP_AUTOREPLY
true turns automatic WhatsApp/SMS replies on; they also need PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true and PULSE_PUBLISH_WHATSAPP / PULSE_PUBLISH_SMS. Default: off.



See Telephony and messaging.
Billing and tenancy



Variable
Effect




TENANT_ID
This deployment's tenant.


SUBSCRIPTION_TIER, SUBSCRIPTION_SEATS, SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS
The subscription the Billing page shows.


SUBSCRIPTION_PERIOD_END
The current billing period's end (RFC 3339).


RUNINK_ACCOUNTS_FILE
The member-to-purchaser file the TIDDE platform provides. Each signed-in person's plan and seats come from the purchaser it names.


RUNINK_USAGE_*
The usage bucket the TIDDE platform provides.


TIDDE_ROUTER_BILLING_KEY_FILE, TIDDE_ROUTER_BILLING_KID
The service key file and key id PULSE signs its model-router billing claim with. Unset, model calls carry no claim and the router treats them as spot work.



Usage is kept on the object store configured under Storage. See
Billing and
Plans.
Names that are no longer read
Some variables of earlier releases are read by nothing now. Setting one does
nothing, and PULSE does not warn: a deployment that still sets only an old
model variable runs on the default model. The list is under
Old names and addresses. Use
INFERENCE_MODEL and INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL.

docs/admin-guide/users-and-access/.title: Users and access
docs/admin-guide/users-and-access/.body:
Users and access

PULSE keeps its own accounts. Each account has one role:
admin, editor, or viewer. There are three ways an account comes to exist.
The break-glass admin
When PULSE_ADMIN_PASSWORD is set, the server creates or updates an account
named admin with the admin role at every start. Change the username or email
with PULSE_ADMIN_USERNAME and PULSE_ADMIN_EMAIL.
Without the variable, the log says No admin password injected
(PULSE_ADMIN_PASSWORD/ADMIN_PASSWORD unset) — skipping admin seed; break-glass
login unavailable until one is provided.

Warning: This is an emergency account. Give it a strong password from the secret store,
and use Google sign-in and seeded roles for everyday access.

Google sign-in
Set GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID to turn on Sign in with Google, and set
AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS to the people allowed to use it. Google sign-in fails
closed:



Situation
Result




GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID unset
No Google button. The exchange endpoint answers google sign-in not configured (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID unset).


Allowlist empty
Nobody signs in with Google. The user sees google sign-in is not available on this instance.


Email not on the allowlist
Refused with this account is not authorized for this instance.


First sign-in of an allowed email
A new viewer account with an unusable random password.


Email removed from the allowlist while signed in
The next request is refused with PermissionDenied (this account is no longer on this PULSE instance's sign-in allowlist), and /auth/refresh answers 403.



The allowlist is re-checked on every authenticated request (gRPC, HTTP
routes, A2A, media) and on every refresh, not only at sign-in. Removing an
address, or a TIDDE add_users grant expiring, ends that person's access at
once instead of when their refresh token runs out. With no allowlist configured
(a local, password-only run) there is nothing to re-check. The break-glass
admin is exempt.
Set AUTH_GOOGLE_ONLY=true to hide the password form. The break-glass admin
still exists, but the app no longer shows the form to reach it.
Roles from the subscription
Runink's TIDDE platform is the only writer of your organisation's accounts. It
gives PULSE a file of the accounts your subscription covers, and PULSE applies
it when a person signs in and whenever the file changes:



Subscription state
Role




Active, or past due
The listed role (editor or viewer)


Trial
The listed role until the trial ends (14 days), then read-only


Suspended or cancelled
Read-only (viewer)



The file never lets anyone sign in (that stays on AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS) and
never makes anyone an admin. An admin's role, a seeded role and the
break-glass admin are left as they are. Administrators are added by Runink.
Seeded roles
AUTH_SEED_USERS grants roles by email, as a comma-separated list of
email=persona pairs. The TIDDE platform sets it from your organisation's
user list. It is applied at every start, and it is the roster: it applies
exactly, downwards as well as upwards.



Persona
Role




admin, org_admin, owner
admin


writer, editor
editor


reader, viewer
viewer




A seeded email that has no account yet gets one with an unusable password, so
that person signs in with Google.
A listed user whose persona is now lower is lowered to it.
An admin or editor the seed no longer lists, or lists with an unknown persona,
is demoted to viewer (the log says Seeding: demoted …). Whether that
person may still sign in at all is decided by AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS.
The break-glass admin (PULSE_ADMIN_EMAIL) is never raised, lowered or
disabled by the seed.
If every entry is malformed, nobody is demoted and the log says
AUTH_SEED_USERS is set but grants nothing PULSE recognises.

What each role may call
Every RPC has a minimum role. The gate runs in both the unary and the streaming
interceptor and fails closed: a method with no entry is refused for
everyone, admins included, and the build will not pass until it has one. The
role comes from the caller's stored account (cached for at most 5 seconds), never
from the token's role claim, so a demotion takes effect within seconds even
for a token that is still valid.



Tier
Who
Covers




public
anyone, before sign-in
IdentityService/Login, ModelService/GetModelStatus


session
any signed-in account, even one with no recognised role
IdentityService/GetCurrentUser, Logout


read
viewer, editor, admin
every List* / Get* of your own records, the activity stream, exports, AuditPipelineService/GetAuditRun and ListAuditRuns, RadarService/ListDiscoveredChannels and ListTrendingPosts


write
editor, admin
everything that generates (spends model time) or changes data: all Generate*, ModelService/Complete, AuditPipelineService/RunAudit and ApplyAuditActions, live market research, lead create/scrape/outreach, PlaceAICall and SendOutreachEmail, campaign, content, publishing and integration changes


admin
admin
the Admin page (AccessService) and the messaging contacts and carrier settings



A viewer can therefore read every page but cannot run an audit, generate, or
approve. New Google accounts start as viewer (see above), so an admin or the
seed must raise them before they can work.
Some write-tier calls have a stricter gate in their handler as well:
ApplyAuditActions apply/commit/pr need an admin and
PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY; PlaceAICall needs PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS and PULSE_AI_CALLS. See
Publishing controls.
If the server cannot read the caller's role, the call fails with
Unavailable: RBAC: could not read your role, never with an allow.
The Admin page
Admin lives inside the Account page. There is no Admin entry in the
navigation rail: an admin opens Account, which leads with Admin (the
way into Members) and then Messaging. Someone who is not an admin
of this instance sees neither section. Members itself is the shared Runink
members page (runink.ui.access.v1.AccessService) at /admin: list members,
invite, change a role, remove. The server reads the caller's role fresh from
the stored account on every call, not from the token, and refuses anyone who is
not an admin of this instance.
Billing is not under Account. Plan, seats and usage are on their own tab,
Settings → Subscription; see Billing.
What a change does depends on where the roster lives:



Deployment
What happens to a change




The platform keeps your roster and lets PULSE write to it
Written to the platform first, then to PULSE. It is pending until the platform applies the roster and PULSE restarts.


AUTH_SEED_USERS is set, but PULSE cannot write to the platform
Refused, with a sentence saying where access is changed. A local change would be undone at the next start.


Neither
PULSE's own accounts are the roster. Changes apply at once.



When a role changes, PULSE ends that person's sessions, so the new role takes
effect at their next sign-in (the RBAC gate already applies it within seconds). PULSE keeps no seat roster, so invites are not
limited by the number of seats on the subscription.
PULSE serves one instance per deployment. Its ID is PULSE_CLIENT_INSTANCE,
else TENANT_ID, else pulse.
Sessions
Sessions live in the sealed app root, so every replica
sees the same state.

An access token lasts 24 hours. A refresh token lasts 7 days and works once.
A session lasts at most 30 days.
Signing out revokes the session and every token issued in it.
The Account page can end all of a person's sessions on every device. It
also carries Appearance, the person's own light or dark preference.

Tokens issued before server-side sessions existed carry no session ID and are
refused. Those users sign in again once.

docs/admin-guide/setup/.title: Setup
docs/admin-guide/setup/.body:
Setup

Runink PULSE: Prescriptive Unified Lead & Social Engine writes and
publishes in your brand's name, so it starts by learning who you are and which
accounts it may read from or publish to. Each person does that under
Settings. Some connections also need one-time work by the administrator of
the PULSE instance in a platform's developer console: those pages say exactly
what to set.

Business profile: Name, industry, timezone, language, tone, active channels.
Connections: Every card under Settings › Integrations, and what each one unlocks.
Public address and redirects: PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL, the three sign-in callbacks, the TIDDE edge.
Meta (Instagram): META_APP_ID / META_APP_SECRET, permissions and app review.
Google: One OAuth client: YouTube, Search Console, Gmail, Google sign-in.
LinkedIn: LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID / SECRET, products, company pages.
Website repository: A fine-grained GitHub token for one repository; fixes as pull requests.
Email: Each person's own mailbox: Gmail, Microsoft 365 or SMTP.
Voice: Spoken output for Reels, read-back and calls.

What needs which connection



Feature
Needs




Brand Analysis (the audit, the diagnosis, content ideas), Campaigns, Studio drafts
Nothing: PULSE reads your public site and writes with its own model


Search demand in Brand Analysis and plans
Google Search Console


Publishing to Instagram, and reading its results, comments, mentions and messages
Meta


Publishing to YouTube, and reading its results and comments
Google


Publishing to LinkedIn, as yourself or a company page
LinkedIn


Fixes to your own website as pull requests
Website repository


Sending outreach email from your own address
Email


Voiceover on the Reels and Stories PULSE makes, read-back, podcasts
Voice


Lead sync and the WhatsApp sender allowlist
HubSpot, see Connections


Website traffic and forecasts
Google Analytics, see Connections


Ads performance
Google Ads, see Connections



A connection never publishes by itself. Whether anything may leave PULSE is
decided by the administrator's switches; see
Switches and arming order.

docs/admin-guide/setup/business-profile/.title: Business profile
docs/admin-guide/setup/business-profile/.body:
Business profile

Settings › Account (/settings?tab=account) holds your profile, the
appearance, and your business profile and content defaults. The page reads them with ConfigService.GetConfig
and saves them with UpdateConfig. Nothing is saved until you choose Save
changes.
Settings has four tabs: Account, Integrations (see
Connections), Clients (for agencies) and
Subscription (your plan and seats).
Business profile



Field
Used for




Business name
How PULSE names your business


Industry
Context for analysis and generation


Timezone
Scheduling and dates



Content defaults



Field
Choices




Interface language
System default, English, Spanish, French, Portuguese. This changes the app's own labels.


Default content language
English, Spanish, French, Portuguese (Brazil)


Default tone
Professional, Casual, Friendly, Authoritative




Note: Each generation request sets its own language and tone. When a request leaves
the tone empty, content generation uses professional.

Active channels
Settings › Integrations is one grid of cards. Under Publish to, each
channel PULSE can publish to (LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, Website, Podcast,
Audiobook) has its account, an Active switch (saved with Save
changes), and one status line: "Ready to publish", or "Can't publish" with
the first reason. Tap the line for every reason and the channel's recent
dispatches. Switch names and user ids in those reasons are shown to admins
only. Measure & CRM holds the read-only accounts (Google Analytics, Google
Ads, HubSpot) in the same cards, without the switch.
Active is a real gate. An active channel is planned in the campaign
roadmap and starts the content strategy's channel picks. It gets PULSE's
daily drafts (the
LinkedIn draft, the Instagram caption, the blog article, the podcast episode,
the audiobook chapter, the YouTube Short) and may publish. A channel you turn
off gets no drafts, and anything already queued for it is recorded
withheld: channel not active instead of being sent. A new account starts
with every channel PULSE can publish to active. Channels saved before Active
became a gate (when the chips only meant focus) gained, once, every channel
that could publish then (LinkedIn, YouTube, website, podcast, audiobook), so
nothing that was publishing stopped. What may publish is also an
administrator setting, armed channel by channel. See
Publishing controls and
which channels can publish.
Stored preferences
AppConfig also has a free-form preferences map of string keys and values.
The Settings page keeps whatever is stored there when it saves, but has no
fields for it. API clients can set it.

docs/admin-guide/setup/connections/.title: Connections
docs/admin-guide/setup/connections/.body:
Connections

Settings › Integrations (/settings?tab=integrations) is one grid of
cards, one per account or channel. Publish to holds the places PULSE can
publish to; Measure & CRM holds the accounts it only reads. Every
credential is your own, stored per user and sealed (encrypted) before it is
written to PULSE's store. A card that needs the administrator to set something
first says which setting is missing.
How each one connects:



Card
How you connect




Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn
Sign in at the platform (OAuth): Connect with Instagram, Connect with YouTube, Connect with LinkedIn


Google Search Console
Sign in with Google (OAuth, read-only): Connect Search Console


Google Business Profile
Sign in with Google (OAuth, business.manage): Connect with Google, then choose the locations


Email
Sign in with Google or Microsoft (OAuth), or your own SMTP server


Website repository
A fine-grained GitHub token limited to that one repository, entered by an administrator


Website (blog publishing)
A GitHub token


Google Analytics, Google Ads
A Google Cloud service-account key you create


HubSpot
A HubSpot Private App token



Publish to
LinkedIn, Instagram and YouTube
Each card offers Connect with LinkedIn, Connect with Instagram or
Connect with YouTube when the administrator has set up the platform's app
(see LinkedIn, Meta,
Google). You sign in at the platform and approve what
PULSE asks for; PULSE stores the token, sealed, and renews it before it runs
out where the platform allows. The card shows connected, expiring, expired,
missing permission or not set up, the end date, and for each feature
(publishing, results, comments, direct messages) whether the permission it
needs was granted. Disconnect withdraws PULSE's access at the platform
where its API allows it, then deletes the stored tokens.
Fallback while sign-in is not set up. Until the administrator configures
the platform's app, the card says sign-in is not set up and accepts a token
you created on the platform yourself. Test then asks the platform whose
token it is: LinkedIn GET /v2/userinfo (it needs the
openid and profile scopes, or the test fails with a 403) and Meta Graph
GET /me.
On LinkedIn you can post as yourself or, when the administrator turned on
company pages, as a page you administer.
Website
Blog posts reach your website as a pull request, or a commit, made with a
GitHub personal access token stored on this card. The repository, branch and
folder are set by the administrator (PULSE_SITE_REPO and friends); see
Site pipeline.
Website repository
Your site's own GitHub repository, where PULSE proposes fixes from the site
audit as pull requests for you to review and merge. An administrator connects
it with a token limited to that one repository. See
Website repository.
Podcast and Audiobook
Episodes and chapters are published through PULSE's own podcast feed, which
podcast platforms poll. There is nothing to connect; the administrator sets
the public address the feed needs.
Email
Connect Gmail, Connect Microsoft 365 or an SMTP server: your own
mailbox, so that Send on a lead's email draft sends from your address.
See Email.
Measure & CRM
Google Search Console
What people type into Google before they find your site. Connect Search
Console signs in with Google, read-only, and PULSE reads clicks,
impressions, click rate and position once a day. See
Google.
Google Business Profile
Your Google reviews and Business Profile figures, drafted replies for your
approval, posts you approve, and a review request proposed when you mark a
deal won. Nothing is posted without your approval. See
Google.
Google Analytics
Paste the full JSON key of a Google Cloud service account that has access to
the GA4 property, and the numeric Property ID (GA4 Admin › Property
Settings). Both are required. It feeds website traffic and the forecasts.
Without it, those places say Google Analytics isn't connected yet.
Google Ads
Paste the JSON key of a service account with domain-wide delegation (scope
adwords), the Ads Customer ID, a Developer Token, an optional
Login Customer ID (manager account), and the Subject email the service
account impersonates. All but the login customer ID are required.
Test on Google Analytics and Google Ads runs a real API call with PULSE's
own client.
HubSpot
A HubSpot Private App token. It enables Sync Now on Leads, pushes new
prospects to HubSpot, and backs the WhatsApp sender allowlist (see
Telephony and messaging).
Website form and SAM.gov
The website form gives you a link your site's contact form can post to, so
enquiries become leads. See Website form.
SAM.gov takes your own API key so Leads can read US federal tenders.
PULSE has no connector for X (Twitter), Mailchimp or TikTok. Connections to
them saved by older versions are hidden and never tested.
What Autopilot reads on Instagram and YouTube
Autopilot reads results, comments, mentions and direct messages back with the
same token publishing uses. Each needs a permission on that token; PULSE never
assumes one is granted. When a platform refuses a read for a missing
permission, the account shows Reconnect to allow … for that kind only
(the rest keeps working), and the reply queue says the same. To re-consent,
connect again with the platform's sign-in, which asks for every permission
below, or paste a new token that has them (it replaces the old one).



Platform
Kind
Permission / scope




Instagram (Graph API with Facebook Login: a Meta token and the Instagram professional account ID)
Results (reach, views, likes, comments, saves, shares where the post type reports them)
instagram_basic, instagram_manage_insights, pages_read_engagement, pages_show_list



Comments and replies; mentions (posts that tag the account)
instagram_basic, instagram_manage_comments, pages_read_engagement, pages_show_list



Direct messages and replies
instagram_basic, instagram_manage_messages, pages_manage_metadata, pages_read_engagement, pages_show_list; the Instagram app setting Allow access to messages must be on


YouTube (a Google access token and its refresh token)
Publishing
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.upload



Views, likes, comment counts; comments and replies
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.force-ssl



Average view duration and percentage
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/yt-analytics.readonly



Every Meta permission above needs Advanced Access through Meta App Review (and
business verification) before it works for accounts that have no role on the
Meta app. The three Google scopes are sensitive scopes: the instance's OAuth
client needs Google's verification before people outside the project can grant
them. A reply to a direct message is sent only within 24 hours of the person's
last message (Meta's messaging window); after that PULSE says so and sends
nothing. YouTube has no mentions and no direct messages: the app says "not
available on YouTube". A figure a platform did not report for that kind of post
is shown as not measured, never as 0.

docs/admin-guide/setup/public-address/.title: Public address and redirects
docs/admin-guide/setup/public-address/.body:
Public address and redirects

For the administrator. Several connections send a person's browser to a
platform and back, and some platforms fetch files from PULSE. Both need the
instance's public address.
Set PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL
Runink sets it on your deployment, to the origin people use to open PULSE, for example
https://pulse.example.com, with no trailing path.
It must be https. Over plain http PULSE does not offer Connect with
Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn or Search Console at all, because a
sign-in code must never travel in clear text; the cards say what is missing.
The same address is used for:

the redirect URIs below;
the signed, expiring /media/ links Instagram fetches photos, carousels and
videos from (without it the Instagram channel is not ready);
absolute links in the podcast feed (/podcast/feed.xml answers 503
without it);
the Twilio callbacks (/comms/twilio/inbound, the AI-call routes);
a trusted browser origin for the session cookie.

Register the redirect URIs



Redirect URI
Register it in
Used by




/oauth/social/callback
the Meta app, the Google OAuth web client, the LinkedIn app
Connect with Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn


/oauth/search-console/callback
the Google OAuth web client
Connect Search Console


/oauth/mail/callback
the Google OAuth web client, the Microsoft Entra app (Web platform)
Connect Gmail, Connect Microsoft 365



Each must match exactly, including https and the absence of a trailing
slash. A connect link works once and for ten minutes.
Route them through the TIDDE edge
The callbacks are plain HTTP routes on the backend's one port, like /media/
and /health. The TIDDE edge that serves the PULSE host must pass
/oauth/social/callback, /oauth/search-console/callback,
/oauth/mail/callback, /media/, /podcast/feed.xml and the Twilio paths
through to the backend unchanged. If a callback does not reach the backend,
the platform's sign-in seems to succeed and the card stays not connected. See
HTTP endpoints for the full list.

docs/admin-guide/setup/meta/.title: Meta (Instagram)
docs/admin-guide/setup/meta/.body:
Meta (Instagram)

For the administrator: what to set up so people can press Connect with
Instagram under Settings › Integrations. Without it, the Instagram card
says sign-in is not set up and accepts a pasted token instead.
In the Meta developer console

Create an app with Facebook Login for Business. PULSE uses the
Instagram API with Facebook Login (Graph API v23.0): the person signs in
at Facebook, and PULSE finds the Instagram professional account through the
Facebook Page it is linked to.
Add /oauth/social/callback to the valid OAuth
redirect URIs (see Public address and redirects).
Request these permissions. The sign-in asks for all of them at once:
| Permission | Needed for |
|---|---|
| instagram_basic, pages_show_list, pages_read_engagement | Every feature |
| instagram_content_publish | Publishing posts, carousels, Reels and Stories |
| instagram_manage_insights | Results (reach, views, likes, comments, saves, shares), and checking an @mention before it is tagged (business discovery) |
| instagram_manage_comments | Comments, replies, and posts that tag the account |
| instagram_manage_messages, pages_manage_metadata | Direct messages and replies to them |

Every permission needs Advanced Access through Meta App Review, and
Meta asks for business verification, before it works for accounts that have
no role on the app. Until then, only people with a role on the app can
connect.

For direct messages, the Instagram account's setting Allow access to
messages must also be on.

What @mentions need
Tagging an account in a post, carousel, Reel or Story is part of publishing
(user_tags on the media container): it needs no permission beyond
instagram_content_publish. Before tagging, PULSE checks each account with
business discovery (GET /?fields=business_discovery.username(…)),
which needs instagram_basic, instagram_manage_insights and
pages_read_engagement, all already in the sign-in. Business discovery finds
only business and creator accounts: a personal account, or any account when
instagram_manage_insights is missing, is shown as not checked in Studio
and stays in the caption as @name without being tagged (the person decides).
Instagram allows 20 @mentions in one caption.
In PULSE
Set META_APP_ID and META_APP_SECRET (the secret from the instance's
secret store, never from a repository secret) and an https
PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL.
PULSE exchanges the sign-in for a long-lived token, stores it sealed, and
renews it in its last ten days; a failed renewal is shown on the card. A
permission the person did not grant is listed on the card, and a read that
needs it says Reconnect to allow …. Disconnect removes PULSE's grant
at Meta (DELETE /me/permissions), then the stored tokens.
Connecting publishes nothing. Publishing also needs PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED and
PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM; replies need PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM_REPLIES or
PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM_DMS. See
Switches and arming order.
What the Instagram API allows for comments and messages (checked 2026-11-27)
Each line was read on the Meta developer page named; the label says what was
and was not established.



Fact
State
Source




The comment-moderation page lists no call that creates a comment on another account's media. Its scope is "Instagram Media owned by your app users". What it lists: GET //comments, GET //replies, POST //replies (reply), POST / (hide or show), DELETE /, POST / (turn comments off or on)
VERIFIED that no such call is listed on that page
https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-api-with-instagram-login/comment-moderation (2026-11-27)


Hashtag search: "You cannot comment on hashtagged media objects discovered through the API"; 30 unique hashtags per rolling 7 days
VERIFIED
https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-api-with-facebook-login/hashtag-search (2026-11-27)


Business discovery returns other accounts' profile data and media fields; no write call is documented, and a direct read of the returned media fails for lack of permission
VERIFIED
https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-api-with-facebook-login/business-discovery (2026-11-27)


GET //tags lists media where the account was tagged, POST //mentions replies to a comment or caption mention, "Mentions on Stories are not supported", "You cannot comment on photos where you were tagged"
VERIFIED
https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-api-with-instagram-login/mentions (2026-11-27)


Comments, replies and hiding on the account's own media need instagram_basic, instagram_manage_comments and pages_read_engagement (Facebook Login); sending a private reply to a comment also needs instagram_manage_messages
VERIFIED
the comment-moderation page above and https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-api-with-instagram-login/messaging-api/private-replies


Private replies: POST //messages with the comment id as recipient, within 7 days of the comment (an Instagram Live comment only during the broadcast), one message to the commenter; follow-ups only if they answer, within 24 hours
VERIFIED
the private-replies page above (2026-11-27)


Access levels: Advanced Access for professional accounts you do not own or manage, Standard Access for your own
VERIFIED (the pages do not describe the App Review steps)
the pages above


Webhook notifications "can describe comments, mentions, story insights, messages". The webhook pages (setup, fields, examples) list the field names comments, mentions, messages and their permissions; a story mention is a messages event whose attachment type is story_mention, and a story reply carries reply_to.story; the pages give no dedicated example for either, and no polling endpoint or conversations call for stories
VERIFIED on the pages named (2026-11-28) that these field names and shapes are documented; NOT VERIFIED against live traffic. Under Facebook Login the fields table lists messages as not available (it lists it for Instagram Login and for the Messaging API), so which setup delivers a story event to PULSE is NOT VERIFIED
https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-api-with-instagram-login/webhooks and https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-api-with-instagram-login/messaging-api (2026-11-27), and the setup, fields and examples pages under developers.facebook.com/documentation/instagram-platform/webhooks (2026-11-28)


mentioned_media and mentioned_comment fields
NOT VERIFIED: the mentions page does not describe them, so PULSE does not call them
n/a



So, for Instagram: Runink PULSE never comments on another account's post.
There is nothing to arm: the Approvals page offers Draft an Instagram
comment to post by hand (the person pastes the post's link and text, PULSE
drafts words, the person posts them in Instagram), labelled "Instagram does
not allow apps to comment on other accounts", with no send button.
What PULSE reads on the account's own posts

Comments, followed by cursor (paging.cursors.after, 50 per page) up to
PULSE_ENGAGEMENT_MAX_PAGES pages (default 4, at most 10) per post, newest
first, stopping at the first page older than the window. The next-page URL is
never followed: PULSE builds the request itself.
The window: PULSE_ENGAGEMENT_WINDOW_DAYS days back (default 14, at most
60) for the posts PULSE sent, mentions and direct messages.
Mentions: the media that tag the account (/tags, paged the same way).
Caption @mentions are not read. Story mentions are read only through the
Meta webhook, when an administrator has armed it (see below).
Direct messages: the Page's conversations (20 a page, paged), answered only
inside Meta's 24-hour window.
A permission Meta refuses (error codes 3, 10 and 200 to 299) is shown as
Reconnect to allow …, the same words as on YouTube.
Spam under a post (a link that is not the account's own site together with
an offer, or three or more links) is proposed for hiding in Approvals: a
person approves it, it passes the same switches, My rules and conscience check
as a reply, and only then is POST / (hide) called. It can be shown
again in the Instagram app. YouTube's equivalent hides permanently from PULSE
(rejected; the API cannot restore it), which the proposal says. Nothing is
hidden without a person.

Story mentions, story replies and comment events: the Meta webhook
Instagram sends story mentions and story replies to apps only by webhook (a
call Meta makes to PULSE when something happens). PULSE answers that call on one
route, /meta/webhook, which does not exist until an administrator arms it.
What it does. An event Meta reports becomes an ordinary item in
Campaigns › Approvals, exactly as if PULSE had read it by polling: the same
categories, drafts, My rules and conscience check, switches and trace.
The webhook only tells PULSE sooner. It never sends anything, and a reply to a
story mention or a story reply is an Instagram direct message, so it keeps
Meta's 24-hour window. The kinds it acts on:



Event
What PULSE keeps
Becomes




A story mention (a message with a story_mention attachment)
the sender's id, the message id and a fixed line, "Mentioned you in their story."
a direct-message item


A story reply (a message that replies to a story)
the sender's id, the message id and the words
a direct-message item


A direct message
as the polled path keeps it
a direct-message item


A comment on the account's own post
the comment id, the post id and the words
a comment item



Everything else Meta may send (reactions, read receipts, edits, echoes of
PULSE's own messages, shared posts, pictures with no words, comment replies,
caption mentions, live comments) is ignored and only counted. The story's own
picture or video is never requested or stored: the address in the payload is
not read, so the webhook cannot be made to fetch anything.
Nothing goes out by itself. Auto-reply keeps its own rules, unchanged: off by
default per account, and never for a story mention (it is not one of the three
allowed kinds). A reply still needs the kill switch, the channel switches, My
rules and the conscience check, and is traced.
Setup, in this order.

In the Meta app, add the Instagram webhooks product and note the App Secret
(App settings › Basic). Choose a verify token: a long random value.
Create the Secret meta-webhook-secrets in the PULSE namespace with two
keys, verify-token and app-secret. They are mounted read-only as files in
/etc/runink/meta-webhook/ (deploy/gx10/SECRETS.md) and are never read from
an environment variable, never logged and never shown in the app.
Set PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL (https) and PULSE_META_WEBHOOK=on, then restart.
The route is registered only when the switch is on and both files are
present; otherwise /meta/webhook answers 404 as if it did not exist.
In the Meta console, enter the callback URL that Settings › Integrations shows
under the Instagram card (/meta/webhook) and the same
verify token. Meta then calls PULSE once to verify it.
Subscribe the app to the fields comments and messages. Meta's own pages say
which permission and which Instagram API setup each field needs; PULSE does not
claim more than they say.

Not done, and not claimed. Every permission still needs Advanced Access
through Meta App Review (and business verification) before it works for accounts
with no role on the app. This release does not apply for it and does not assume
it was granted. The webhook shapes PULSE reads come from Meta's published pages
and were not checked against live traffic; read the status line on the card
after the first real event.
What PULSE checks on every call.

The handshake answers only a request whose hub.verify_token equals the verify
token (compared in constant time) and echoes the challenge only then.
A notification is accepted only with a valid X-Hub-Signature-256: the
HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with the App Secret, compared in constant time
before the body is read as JSON. Missing or wrong is answered 403, and the log
line says so without any value.
The body is capped (PULSE_META_WEBHOOK_MAX_BODY, 256 KiB by default) and parsed
strictly: one JSON value, unknown fields ignored.
An event id is remembered for PULSE_META_WEBHOOK_DEDUPE_HOURS (48 by default,
at most 168; Meta retries for up to 36), so a replay or a retry is dropped; an
event older than that window is dropped as stale.
Each address and the verified traffic as a whole have a rate limit. PULSE
answers 200 at once and works through a bounded queue; when it is full the
event is dropped and counted, and Meta is never kept waiting.
An event is matched to an account by the Instagram business account id in the
notification (entry.id) against the connected integrations. No match, or two
PULSE users claiming one account, means the event is ignored and counted; the
answer is the same as for a match, so nothing reveals which accounts exist.

What the administrator sees. /health has a meta_webhook block: whether it
is configured, the time of the last event and counts by outcome (ok,
bad_signature, unmatched_account, duplicate, queue_full, and a few more),
counts only. The Instagram card in Settings › Integrations shows a status line
from recorded facts, such as "Webhook not configured: needs the app secret and the
verify token", and the callback address as text. The verify token's value is
never displayed.
Until the webhook is armed, the app says plainly that story mentions and story
replies are not read, and every other kind keeps working by polling.

docs/admin-guide/setup/google/.title: Google
docs/admin-guide/setup/google/.body:
Google

For the administrator. One Google OAuth web client serves Google sign-in,
Connect with YouTube, Connect Search Console, Connect Google Business Profile and Connect Gmail.
Its id and secret are GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, set by
Runink on your deployment from its secret store. Google Analytics and Google Ads do not use this client:
each person pastes a service-account key (see
Connections).
In the Google Cloud console

In the project that owns the OAuth client, enable the APIs for what you
want people to connect:
| API | For |
|---|---|
| YouTube Data API v3 | Publishing, statistics, comments and replies |
| YouTube Analytics API | Average view duration and percentage |
| Google Search Console API | Search Console |
| Gmail API | Sending from Gmail and seeing replies |
| My Business Account Management API | Google Business Profile: the accounts |
| My Business Business Information API | Google Business Profile: the locations |
| Google My Business API (v4) | Google Business Profile: reviews, replies and posts |
| Business Profile Performance API | Google Business Profile: views, calls, website visits, directions |

Create (or open) the OAuth client of type Web application and add the
redirect URIs, each under your https PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL:
/oauth/social/callback (YouTube), /oauth/search-console/callback
(Search Console), /oauth/google-business/callback (Google Business
Profile) and /oauth/mail/callback (Gmail). See
Public address and redirects. For Google sign-in in the
browser, Google also requires the app's origin under Authorized
JavaScript origins.

On the OAuth consent screen, add the scopes below.
Submit the app for verification. The YouTube scopes and
webmasters.readonly are sensitive scopes and gmail.readonly is a
restricted one: until Google verifies the app, only test users of the
project can grant them (and restricted scopes are capped at 100 users).

YouTube
Connect with YouTube asks for:

https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.upload (publishing);
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.force-ssl (views, likes, comment
counts, comments and replies);
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/yt-analytics.readonly (average view
duration and percentage).

PULSE stores the access and refresh tokens sealed and renews the access token
shortly before it expires. A scope the person did not grant is listed on the
card. YouTube has no mentions and no direct messages through its API; the app
says "not available on YouTube". Uploads are private unless
YOUTUBE_PRIVACY_STATUS says unlisted or public. Publishing also needs
PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED and PULSE_PUBLISH_YOUTUBE.
What the YouTube Data API allows for comments (checked 2026-11-27)
Each line was read on the page named; nothing here is from memory.



Fact
State
Source




commentThreads.insert posts a top-level comment given snippet.channelId, snippet.videoId and snippet.topLevelComment.snippet.textOriginal; scope youtube.force-ssl; 50 quota units a call
VERIFIED
the YouTube Data API reference, page commentThreads.insert, https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs (2026-11-27)


The page does not say the video must be one of the caller's own: it names no such rule, and says each thread "must be linked to a video". Whether a given video accepts a comment is answered by the call (comments turned off, an ineligible account)
VERIFIED that the page is silent; NOT VERIFIED beyond that
same page


comments.insert (a reply) needs snippet.parentId; 50 units; it cannot reply to a private comment
VERIFIED
https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs/comments/insert (2026-11-27)


commentThreads.list and comments.list cost 1 unit; videos.list costs 1; comments.setModerationStatus and comments.delete cost 50
VERIFIED
https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/determine_quota_cost (2026-11-27)


The default quota is 10,000 units a day for all endpoints other than search and video uploads; it belongs to the Cloud project, not to an account
VERIFIED (the page also lists separate allowances for search.list and videos.insert; its search cost line reads inconsistently, so this PULSE feature never calls search.list)
same page


commentThreads.list: maxResults 1 to 100 (default 20), pageToken / nextPageToken, order time or relevance, videoId or allThreadsRelatedToChannelId
VERIFIED
https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs/commentThreads/list (2026-11-27)


A comment thread "represents comments on a video": the pages mention no community posts, no channel mentions and no direct messages
VERIFIED that the pages are silent. PULSE therefore keeps "mentions and direct messages: not available on YouTube"
https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs/commentThreads (2026-11-27)


comments.setModerationStatus with rejected hides a comment and its replies and cannot be changed back to published; only the owner of the channel or video may call it; scope youtube.force-ssl; 50 units
VERIFIED
the YouTube Data API reference, page comments.setModerationStatus, https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs (2026-11-27)



Suggested comments on other people's videos. Under Settings › Account an
administrator of an account can switch on Suggest comments on other people's
videos (off by default). Runink PULSE then picks videos that Brand Analysis › What people are talking about already
found for the account (no new search), reads the public title and channel of
one (1 unit), drafts one short comment and puts it in Campaigns › Approvals.
It is never posted by itself: a person approves it, and only then does it
pass, in order, the account's switch, the comment rules once more (no link, no
promotion, no invented claim), the daily limit and the channel cooldown, the
quota budget, the kill switches below, My rules and the conscience check
(the publishing door, with the rules of the marketing agent). It is posted as
the account's own connected YouTube channel and nothing else.
Quota: PULSE keeps a daily budget (PULSE_YT_QUOTA_DAILY_BUDGET, default 8,000
of the default 10,000 units) in each running process and stops before it: a
read that would go over is not made and the app says so; a comment (50 units)
is held in the approval queue until the next day. Google's own quota answer is
also read and stops the pass. The count restarts at midnight Pacific time,
when Google's quota resets, and is not shared between replicas or kept over a
restart, which is why the budget leaves room.
Without the client, the YouTube card accepts a pasted Google access token and
its refresh token instead.
Search Console
Connect Search Console asks only for
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters.readonly (with PKCE and offline
access), then lists the properties the Google account can read. PULSE picks
the one that matches the audited site, otherwise the person chooses. Once a
day it reads clicks, impressions, click rate and average position per search
and per page for the last 28 days and the 28 before (Google's figures lag
about two days). It spends at most 25 Search Console calls per account a day,
manual reads included; a quota answer from Google is recorded and the read is
retried the next day. Not connected, every place that would show these
figures says "not measured".
Google Business Profile

Warning: Not yet available. The Google Business Profile connection, review replies
and posts are built and are waiting on Google's approval of API access. What follows describes how it is meant to work once
access is granted.

The Business Profile APIs are gated by Google: before they answer, request
access for the Cloud project with Google's Business Profile API access
request form (business.google.com, API access), with the project number.
Until Google grants it, every call answers with a quota of 0 and the card
shows the read failed with Google's reason. Then enable the four APIs above
and add the https://www.googleapis.com/auth/business.manage scope to the
consent screen (a sensitive scope: verification as in step 4).
Connect Google Business Profile asks only for business.manage (with
PKCE and offline access) and lists the locations of every account the Google
user manages; a single location is managed at once, several wait for the
person to choose. Every 6 hours (and on Read now) PULSE reads the
managed locations' reviews (the newest 200 each) and the last 28 finished
days of views on Search and Maps, calls, website visits and direction
requests, at most 60 calls per account a day. A figure Google does not
report is left out, never shown as 0; not connected says "not connected".
Each new review without a reply gets a reply DRAFTED by PULSE's own model
(checked by PULSE's safety rules and the plan gate). Only a person's Approve posts it, through
PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED, PULSE_PUBLISH_GBP and PULSE_PUBLISH_GBP_REPLIES;
a negative review (1 or 2 stars, or 3 with a complaint) is flagged and also
needs the person to tick that they read it. Posts (update, offer, event) are
made in Brand Analysis › Google reviews › New post, wait in Campaigns ›
Approvals on the Google Business Profile channel, and publish on approval
through PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED and PULSE_PUBLISH_GBP.
When a deal is marked won, PULSE proposes one review-request email in that
lead's outreach: from the person's own mailbox, after their approval, with
the outreach footer, suppression list, daily cap and working hours. Google
forbids offering anything for a review or asking only happy customers; every
won customer gets the same request, and an approval whose text offers an
incentive is refused.
Gmail
Connect Gmail asks for gmail.send, openid email, and gmail.readonly
so PULSE can see who answered. See Email.
Google sign-in
With GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID set, the login screen offers Google sign-in. Who may
sign in is AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS (empty means nobody); AUTH_GOOGLE_ONLY=true
hides the password form. See
Users and access.
The Android app asks Google for a token for the web client, and Google only answers an app it knows: in the same
Google Cloud project, create an OAuth client of type Android for the
package org.runink.pulse with the SHA-1 of each key the app is signed with.
Until then the Android app says it is not registered with Google.

docs/admin-guide/setup/linkedin/.title: LinkedIn
docs/admin-guide/setup/linkedin/.body:
LinkedIn

For the administrator: what to set up so people can press Connect with
LinkedIn, and optionally post as a company page. Without it, the LinkedIn
card accepts a pasted token instead.
In the LinkedIn developer portal

Create an app, associated with the company's LinkedIn page.
Under Auth, add /oauth/social/callback to the
authorized redirect URLs (see Public address and redirects).
Under Products, add Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect
(scopes openid, profile) and Share on LinkedIn (w_member_social).
That is all a person needs to post as themselves.
To post as a company page, request the Community Management API. Once
LinkedIn approves it, the app may ask for r_organization_social,
w_organization_social and rw_organization_admin.

In PULSE



Setting
What to set




LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID, LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET
The app's client id and secret (the secret from the instance's secret store). With both and an https PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL, the card shows Connect with LinkedIn.


LINKEDIN_COMPANY_PAGES
true only after LinkedIn approved the Community Management API. The card then also offers Connect company pages, which asks for the three page scopes and lists the pages the member administers to post as.



LinkedIn access tokens last 60 days. PULSE renews one in its last ten days
only when LinkedIn issued a refresh token (LinkedIn does that only for apps it
enabled for programmatic refresh); otherwise the card shows "reconnect
before" the date. Disconnect revokes the token at LinkedIn, then deletes
it.
Connecting publishes nothing. LinkedIn posts also need PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED,
PULSE_PUBLISH_LINKEDIN and the content owner in PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS;
the daily LinkedIn draft is never scheduled by itself. See
Switches and arming order.

docs/admin-guide/setup/website-repositor.title: Website repository
docs/admin-guide/setup/website-repositor.body:
Website repository

The customer's own website repository on GitHub. When a site audit finds
something PULSE can fix in the site's files, Propose as pull request opens
one branch and one pull request there for a person to review and merge. PULSE
never pushes to the base branch and never merges.
Create the token on GitHub
PULSE uses a fine-grained personal access token, not a GitHub OAuth app:
an OAuth app's narrowest write scope opens every repository the person can
reach, while a fine-grained token can be limited to one.

On GitHub: Settings › Developer settings › Fine-grained tokens › Generate
new token.
Repository access: Only select repositories, and pick the site's
repository only.
Permissions: Contents read and write, and Pull requests read
and write. Nothing else.
Choose an expiry you will remember to renew.

No OAuth client and no server secret are needed for this connection.
Connect it in PULSE
An administrator opens Settings › Integrations › Website repository,
enters the owner (user or organization), the repository name, the base
branch (main when empty) and the token, and presses Connect and check.
The token is sealed with the envelope key; leaving the field empty later keeps
the stored one. The card shows one of: Connected, Missing permission, Token
rejected, Base branch not found, GitHub unreachable, Not connected, with when
it was last checked.
Arm proposals
Proposing is off until the administrator sets both PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true
and PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY=true, and only an administrator may propose. Either
switch off refuses the proposal before anything is read from or sent to
GitHub. PULSE_APPLY_ROOT is not needed. See
Switches and arming order.
What a proposal does

Reads the base branch over the GitHub REST API, places the fix for one
audit finding with the same stack logic as the server-side apply agent, and
has the plan gate judge the edit against the measured finding. A dissent
opens nothing and the proposal shows as withheld.
Writes a new branch pulse/- and opens a pull request whose
body cites the finding and the gate's verdict. One proposal per finding.
Never edits .github/workflows/ or .git/, refuses .. paths and links,
and is capped at 20 files, 256 KiB each and 1 MiB in all.
A fix already in the repository, or one that cannot be placed, is "No pull
request needed" with the reason. The pull request's state (open, merged,
closed without merging) is read back from GitHub when asked.

This is separate from the Website card, which publishes blog posts with
the repository set in PULSE_SITE_REPO; see
Site pipeline.

docs/admin-guide/setup/email/.title: Email
docs/admin-guide/setup/email/.body:
Email

The Email card connects your own mailbox, so that Send on a lead's
email draft sends from your address. PULSE has no shared sender and uses no
email service provider. Connect one of:



Option
How it connects
What PULSE may do




Gmail
Connect Gmail opens Google's consent page (OAuth with PKCE).
Send mail (gmail.send), your address (openid email), and read your mail (gmail.readonly) so PULSE can see who answered. PULSE keeps only a short snippet of each reply to an email it sent, never the message.


Microsoft 365
Connect Microsoft 365 opens Microsoft's consent page.
Send mail as you (delegated Mail.Send), read your mail (Mail.Read) to see who answered, read your profile (User.Read), and stay connected (offline_access).


SMTP
Host, port (587 for STARTTLS, 465 for TLS), username, password and from address.
PULSE logs in before saving. A server that does not offer STARTTLS is refused: no password or message is sent unencrypted.



Tokens and the SMTP password are sealed in the integrations table like every
other credential. Test asks the provider who the mailbox is and sends
nothing: Google's token check (which must show gmail.send), Graph GET /me,
or an SMTP login. An expired Google or Microsoft token is refreshed once.
If several mailboxes are connected, PULSE sends from the most recently
connected one that passed its check; the sheet names the address before you
send.
What Send does
Leads → Email → Send sends the newest saved draft to the lead, records the
attempt (outreach_sends: lead, provider, provider message id, time, status)
and moves a new lead to contacted. Nothing is sent automatically. Send is
shown only when all of these hold; otherwise the sheet says which one is
missing and keeps Copy and Open in email:

your account is an editor or admin;
the administrator armed PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED and did not set
PULSE_PUBLISH_EMAIL=false (see Switches);
a mailbox is connected and its last check passed;
you are under the daily limit (PULSE_EMAIL_DAILY_LIMIT, 50 by default).

Outreach from the sheet is one-to-one, so it carries no List-Unsubscribe
header. A marketing send through the API (marketing=true) adds one.
Replies
PULSE looks for answers to the emails it sent, every 15 minutes and each time
you open Leads, for sends from the last 30 days. A reply is matched on the
sent email's own thread (Gmail) or conversation (Microsoft 365), so other mail
is never matched. A lead who answered is marked replied and shows under
To do today on Leads, with the first words of the answer and Answer,
until you move it past Talking. Only a short snippet (200 characters) is
kept, sealed like every credential.

A Gmail or Microsoft 365 mailbox connected before reply tracking, or without
the reading permission, is never read. The Email card and To do today say to
Reconnect, which asks for the permission again.
An SMTP mailbox has no inbox PULSE can read: replies are not tracked, and
the page says so. (IMAP is not supported.)

For the administrator
Gmail and Microsoft 365 use the instance's own OAuth clients, read from the
instance configuration, never from a repository secret:

Set PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL. The redirect URI is
/oauth/mail/callback.
Gmail: in the Google Cloud project behind GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, enable the Gmail API, add the redirect URI to the
web client, and add the gmail.send and gmail.readonly scopes to the consent screen (gmail.readonly is a restricted scope: Google requires app verification beyond 100 users). The same scope serves Read my inbox for vendor pitches (off for every account until it is switched on). Whether to complete Google's restricted-scope verification for users outside the project is not decided yet; until it is, grant that switch only to accounts inside the project.
Microsoft 365: register an app in Microsoft Entra, add the redirect URI as a
Web platform, grant the delegated Graph permissions Mail.Send, Mail.Read,
User.Read and offline_access, create a client secret, and set
MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID, MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET and, for a single-tenant
app, MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID (default common).

A connect link works once and for ten minutes.
SMTP needs nothing from the administrator: each person enters their own
server. Sending by any route still needs PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true and
PULSE_PUBLISH_EMAIL not set to false; PULSE_EMAIL_DAILY_LIMIT (50) caps
each person's sends per 24 hours. See
Switches and arming order.

docs/admin-guide/setup/voice/.title: Voice
docs/admin-guide/setup/voice/.body:
Voice

For the administrator. Everything PULSE says aloud comes from the platform's
shared speech service: the voiceover on Reels and Stories PULSE makes,
read-back in the app, podcast and audiobook audio, and calls.
Runink sets the speech service for your deployment; there is nothing to configure.
If the speech service is unreachable, a Reel or Story PULSE
makes is a silent video that says "no voiceover: speech service unavailable",
and the features that need speech say it is unavailable instead of returning
silence. Voice input depends on the platform's speech-to-text, which your
deployment provides.
Making a video also needs ffmpeg on the server (the backend image has it;
FFMPEG_PATH overrides the binary). Without it, the app says "video is not
available on this server".

docs/admin-guide/switches-and-arming-ord.title: Switches and arming order
docs/admin-guide/switches-and-arming-ord.body:
Switches and arming order

Runink PULSE: Prescriptive Unified Lead & Social Engine ships with every
outward action switched off. This page lists each switch in one place: what it
defaults to, what it does, and the order to turn them on safely. The detail
behind each one is on Publishing controls
and Users and access.
These are set by Runink on your deployment; ask Runink to change one.
Yes and no values
The keys do not all parse yes and no the same way, and the difference matters:

PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED arms only on the exact value true. yes, on,
1, and TRUE leave it off, and the server warns about it at startup.
PULSE_PUBLISH_, PULSE_PUBLISH_AUTOMATIONS, PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY,
PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS and PULSE_AI_CALLS accept 1, t, true, y, yes, on and 0, f, false, n, no,
off, in any case. Anything else, including empty, counts as unset, which
for the last four means off.
AUTH_GOOGLE_ONLY is on only for the exact value true.
PULSE_GRPC_REFLECTION is on for true in any case.
SELF_HEAL_AUTONOMOUS and PULSE_OPPORTUNITIES_DISCOVERY default to
on, so they read the other way round: they take the same tokens, and
unset or unparseable leaves them on. Only an explicit no turns them off.
PULSE_LIPSYNC is on for on, true, 1 and yes (any case); anything else, including empty, is off.
PULSE_IMAGEGEN reads the same way: on, true, 1 and yes (any case) are on; anything else, including empty, is off.
PULSE_JUDGEMENT is on unless set to off (any case).
PULSE_RERANKER is on unless set to off (any case).
LINKEDIN_COMPANY_PAGES is on for 1, t, T, true, TRUE or
True; anything else, including yes, leaves it off.
PULSE_WHATSAPP_AUTOREPLY takes the same tokens and is off unless set to
an explicit yes.

The switches



Key
Default
Effect




PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED
off
The global kill switch for every outward channel, the first half of the audit-apply gate, and what starts the daily site-audit engine. While it is off, nothing publishes, and approving a draft does not queue it at its planned date.


PULSE_PUBLISH_
follows the kill switch
Narrows one channel: BLOG, PODCAST, AUDIOBOOK, YOUTUBE, INSTAGRAM, SPOTIFY, LINKEDIN, EMAIL, WHATSAPP, SMS. Can only turn a channel off.


PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM
follows the kill switch
Approving (or a schedule or Autopilot reaching) an Instagram piece publishes it by what it is: a post (one photo, with caption, hashtags and alt text), a carousel (its rendered 1080×1350 slides), a Reel (the owner's own video, attached in Studio; MP4/MOV, 3 s to 15 min, at most 300 MB and 1920 px wide, index at the start) or Stories (each attached photo or video, 3 to 60 s; no caption, and stickers cannot be posted through the API). A Reel or Story with no video of the owner's gets one made by PULSE at approval (or on download), and so does a YouTube Short (9:16, at most 3 min, uploaded through PULSE_PUBLISH_YOUTUBE; the owner's own video goes first). Reels made by PULSE are at most 90 s and Stories are split into parts of at most 60 s; Instagram's API publishes no stickers, so a Story's stickers are listed on a checklist to add by hand. Without speech the video is silent and says so; a server that cannot make video says "video is not available on this server". A piece without its media is refused for scheduling and withheld at approval with "needs a video / photo: upload one in Studio". Instagram fetches every file from PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL at an unguessable, signed address that expires within two hours; without that URL the channel is not ready. Before publishing PULSE reads the account's content_publishing_limit; at the limit the post moves to after the 24-hour window with the reason. Mentions go in the caption as @name; each one is looked up again with business discovery right before posting and only a found (business or creator) account is sent in user_tags (a photo at its centre, a Reel or the first Story by username); one that cannot be looked up is not tagged. Needs the Instagram professional account connected with instagram_basic and instagram_content_publish (Meta app review); a missing permission is recorded as "reconnect Instagram to allow …".


META_APP_ID, META_APP_SECRET
unset
The instance's own Meta app (Facebook Login for Business). With both set, Settings › Integrations shows Connect with Instagram: the person signs in at Facebook, PULSE stores a sealed long-lived token, finds the Instagram professional account through their Page, and renews the token in its last ten days (a failed renewal is shown on the card). The app must allow the redirect PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/oauth/social/callback. Unset: the card says sign-in is not set up and accepts a pasted token instead.


LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID, LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET
unset
The instance's own LinkedIn app. With both set (and an https PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL), the LinkedIn card shows Connect with LinkedIn: the person signs in at LinkedIn (openid profile w_member_social), PULSE stores the sealed token and the member, and approved LinkedIn posts use that token. LinkedIn tokens last 60 days; PULSE renews them only when LinkedIn issued a refresh token, otherwise the card shows "reconnect before" the date. The app must allow the redirect PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/oauth/social/callback. Unset: the card accepts a pasted token instead. PULSE_PUBLISH_LINKEDIN and PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS still decide whether anything is posted.


LINKEDIN_COMPANY_PAGES
off
Set true only once LinkedIn approved the app for the Community Management API. The card then offers Connect company pages, which also asks for r_organization_social, w_organization_social and rw_organization_admin, and lists the pages the member administers to post as.


PULSE_PUBLISH_EMAIL
follows the kill switch
Send on a lead's email draft (SendOutreachEmail): one email, sent when the user taps Send, from that user's own connected mailbox (Gmail, Microsoft 365 or SMTP, see Connections). There is no shared sender, so PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS does not apply. Off, a send is recorded withheld and the sheet keeps Copy and Open in email. Editors and admins only.


PULSE_PUBLISH_WHATSAPP, PULSE_PUBLISH_SMS
follows the kill switch
A WhatsApp message or SMS through the shared Twilio carrier: Do it on a lead's next step under Leads › To do today, and Send on a result. Each send needs the person to confirm its preview. Recipients are the contacts an admin added under Settings › Messaging, plus, for SMS only, the person's own open leads whose phone number has a recorded source (see below). Off, the send is refused as "not configured" with the switch named; nothing is sent. Calls are not affected.


PULSE_PUBLISH_LINKEDIN_REPLIES, PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM_REPLIES, PULSE_PUBLISH_YOUTUBE_REPLIES
follows the kill switch
Replies PULSE sends from the Autopilot reply queue (Campaigns › Approvals): an answer to a comment (and, on Instagram, to a post that tags the account). A reply needs this switch and the channel's own PULSE_PUBLISH_, so false here keeps posting on and answering off. Off, an approved reply is recorded withheld with the switch named; nothing is sent.


PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM_DMS
follows the kill switch
Answers to Instagram direct messages from the reply queue. Needs PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM too. Independently of every switch, a message is answered only within 24 hours of the person's last message (Meta's window); after that the reply is withheld with that reason.


PULSE_PUBLISH_YOUTUBE_COMMENTS
off (unlike the other switches, the kill switch alone does not arm it)
A comment on someone else's YouTube video, posted as the account's own channel, only after a person approved the suggestion in Campaigns › Approvals. Needs true here and PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED and PULSE_PUBLISH_YOUTUBE, and the account's own switch (Settings › Account › Suggest comments on other people's videos, default off). Off, an approved comment stays recorded withheld with this switch named; nothing is sent. There is no automatic option: no setting makes PULSE post one without a person. See Google.


PULSE_AB_MIN_SENDS
30
The subject test of outreach sequences (it only exists once a person writes a second subject): how many emails each subject needs before the Subject test card shows a comparison (1 to 100000). Below it the card shows the counts only. PULSE never picks or switches a winner. Opens are not measured.


PULSE_YT_COMMENT_DAILY_CAP, PULSE_YT_COMMENT_CHANNEL_COOLDOWN_DAYS
3, 14
Per account: how many comment suggestions are staged and how many are posted in 24 hours (1 to 10), and how many days a channel is left alone after a suggestion on one of its videos (1 to 90). Both hold again when a person approves: past the cap the comment waits in the queue with the reason.


PULSE_YT_QUOTA_DAILY_BUDGET
8000
Units of the YouTube Data API's daily quota (10,000 by default per Google Cloud project) PULSE may spend in this process: 1 per read, 50 per comment or hide. A call that would go over is not made. Counted in memory by Pacific-time day (when Google resets), so it is not shared across replicas or kept over a restart; keep it under the project's quota with room for other tools. At most 10,000.


PULSE_ENGAGEMENT_WINDOW_DAYS, PULSE_ENGAGEMENT_MAX_PAGES
14, 4
How far back Autopilot reads comments, mentions and direct messages on the account's posts (1 to 60 days), and how many pages it follows per post or inbox in one pass (1 to 10; 50 Instagram comments or up to 100 YouTube comment threads a page). A value that is unset, zero, negative or not a number counts as the default; one above the maximum counts as the maximum. YouTube pages cost 1 unit each.


PULSE_META_WEBHOOK
off
Arms the secure Meta webhook (GET and POST /meta/webhook) that brings Instagram story mentions, story replies, comments and direct messages into Campaigns › Approvals as soon as Meta reports them. The route is registered only when this is on and both files of the optional Secret meta-webhook-secrets (verify-token, app-secret, mounted under /etc/runink/meta-webhook/) are present; otherwise it answers 404. It sends nothing: every reply keeps the kill switch, the channel switches, My rules and the conscience check. See Meta (Instagram).


PULSE_META_WEBHOOK_MAX_BODY, PULSE_META_WEBHOOK_DEDUPE_HOURS
262144, 48
The largest notification body the webhook reads, in bytes (4096 to 1048576), and how many hours an event id is remembered so a retry or replay is dropped (1 to 168; Meta retries for up to 36). A value that is unset, zero, negative or not a number counts as the default; one above the maximum counts as the maximum.


PULSE_META_WEBHOOK_SECRETS_DIR
/etc/runink/meta-webhook
The directory the two secret files are read from. Only a test or an unusual mount changes it.


PULSE_PUBLISH_GBP
follows the kill switch
Approving a Google Business Profile post (update, offer, event) publishes it on the managed location it names, with the account's own Google sign-in. Not connected, or a location PULSE no longer manages, is withheld with the reason.


PULSE_PUBLISH_GBP_REPLIES
follows the kill switch
A reply to a Google review, posted only when a person approves it (a negative review also needs the person to confirm they read it). Needs PULSE_PUBLISH_GBP too, so false here keeps posts on and review replies off. Off, the approval is recorded withheld with the switch named.


PULSE_EMAIL_DAILY_LIMIT
50
Emails one user may send in any 24 hours, to protect their mailbox's reputation. A positive whole number; anything else means 50.


GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET
unset
The instance's own Google OAuth client. Also used for sign-in and token refresh. Needed for Connect Gmail, which asks for gmail.send and, to see replies, gmail.readonly. Also Connect with YouTube (asks for youtube.upload, youtube.force-ssl, yt-analytics.readonly; redirect PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/oauth/social/callback must be allowed on the client). Unset: the YouTube card accepts a pasted token instead. The same client connects Google Search Console (read-only webmasters.readonly, redirect PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/oauth/search-console/callback); see Google.


MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID, MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET, MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID
unset, unset, common
The instance's own Microsoft Entra app registration, for Connect Microsoft 365 (delegated Mail.Send, Mail.Read for replies, User.Read, offline_access). Set the secret from the instance's configuration, never from a repository secret.


PULSE_PUBLISH_CONFIG_PATH, PULSE_PUBLISH_CONFIG_JSON
a file set by Runink, none
The same per-channel opinions as a file, or inline JSON. An environment key wins over the file.


PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS
empty, which means nobody
