User ids (as shown in Admin, not emails) allowed to publish through the channels that post as the deployment: LinkedIn, blog, podcast, and audiobook. Anyone else's dispatch is recorded withheld.


Settings › Integrations › Active (per user, not an env var)
every channel active until the user saves
A channel its owner switched off gets no daily drafts, and its queued posts are recorded withheld: channel not active. It can only narrow: it never arms a channel the switches above leave off.


PULSE_PUBLISH_LINKEDIN
follows the kill switch
Keep this false to keep LinkedIn drafts-only. See the daily LinkedIn draft.


Settings › Integrations › Autopilot (per account, not an env var)
off for every account
After a person approves a post, PULSE queues it at the account's best time instead of sending it at once, and the publishing worker sends it through the same gate as any scheduled post: the kill switch, PULSE_PUBLISH_, PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS and the Active switch above all still decide at send time. Autopilot never queues content nobody approved, and never queues on a disarmed channel (the approval then sends, and is recorded withheld, as before). It pauses the account by itself on an expired connection, a rate limit, or repeated failed sends, and says so under Leads › To do today with a Reconnect link. Turning Autopilot off withholds its queued posts. See Autopilot and agencies.


Autopilot › Answer simple comments by itself (per account)
off
Replies to comments PULSE reads (LinkedIn, Instagram and YouTube; on Instagram also mentions and direct messages) are drafted into Campaigns › Approvals. A person may let three low-risk kinds go out by themselves: thanks, an answer taken from approved FAQ content, and a link to the business's own site. Each one must pass PULSE's safety rules and the plan gate (with PULSE_JUDGEMENT=off nothing replies by itself) and is logged on its row. A reply is an outbound post on the channel, so it also needs the kill switch, PULSE_PUBLISH_, the channel's reply switch (PULSE_PUBLISH__REPLIES, or PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM_DMS for a direct message), the publisher allowlist and the Active switch.


Settings › Account › Answer vendor pitches (per account, not an env var)
off for every account
An unsolicited vendor pitch that reaches the account (website form; Instagram direct messages; not LinkedIn, WhatsApp, SMS or website chat, and mail that only arrives in the mailbox only when the account also switched on Read my inbox for vendor pitches, below) is answered with the account's own counter-offer and no per-message approval once the account turns it on and fills in its terms, its Outreach sender name and postal address (and PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is https). Each answer still needs the kill switch, the channel's own switch (PULSE_PUBLISH_EMAIL for the form's answer; PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM and PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM_DMS for a direct message), My rules and the conscience gate, the loop gate, ten answers a day and one per sender. A refused answer waits in the partner pipeline for a person. See Answer vendor pitches.


Settings › Account › Read my inbox for vendor pitches (per account, not an env var; with a sub-option for promotions)
off for every account
New mail in the account's connected Gmail inbox, read-only, is given to Answer vendor pitches: inbox folder only (promotions, updates, social and forums with the sub-option; spam and sent mail never), only mail received after the switch was turned on, at most 7 days back. Needs Answer vendor pitches on too and gmail.readonly (a restricted Google scope; verification for users outside the project is still to be decided). Gmail only for now. See Answer vendor pitches.


PULSE_VENDOR_INSIGHTS_WINDOW_DAYS, PULSE_VENDOR_INSIGHTS_MIN_PITCHES
unset, unset
The window in days and the fewest pitches for What vendors pitching us tell us. Either unset: the card shows nothing and names what is missing. Fewer pitches than the minimum: nothing is said. Nothing is sent: a weekly digest is a record in the app. See Answer vendor pitches.


Settings › Account › First response to website enquiries (per account, not an env var)
off for every account; the second switch, Send acknowledgements automatically, is also off
A new website-form enquiry from a business email address gets a short acknowledgement composed from a template and the account's own words. Switched on, it only prepares a draft that waits for a person's tap; with the second switch on, the clearest cases go without the tap. Nothing happens until the account's Outreach sender name and postal address are filled in and PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is https. Each send still needs the kill switch, PULSE_PUBLISH_EMAIL, the account's working hours and daily cap, My rules and the conscience gate, the loop gate, and goes at most once per lead. See First response to enquiries.


PULSE_MESSAGE_STEP_DAILY_CAP, and the step Send a WhatsApp or SMS (with your tap)
10; the step is an outbound automation step (needs PULSE_PUBLISH_AUTOMATIONS, the kill switch PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED and the channel's own PULSE_PUBLISH_SMS / PULSE_PUBLISH_WHATSAPP)
The most messages a day (1 to 200) the step may make or send per account; past it the step is refused with the reason. The step only MAKES a message: each one waits for a person's tap (Content › Automations › Messages), and only a contact with a consent a person recorded for that channel is messaged. A STOP reply, the account's contact hours and the switches are checked again at the tap. No consent, no message.


Content › Automations › Re-engage a quiet lead (per account, not an env var)
off for every account
Switching it on installs the automation "Re-engage a quiet lead" disarmed; arming it stays the person's own step. Each morning it takes the leads in stage Contacted that never replied and, for each one whose last email from PULSE is at least the quiet period old (default 14 days, 3 to 90), drafts ONE short follow-up that waits for a person's approval in the lead's sequence. It sends nothing itself: after the tap the email goes through the same send as every sequence email (working hours, daily cap, suppression list, footer with the unsubscribe link, My rules, PULSE_PUBLISH_EMAIL). At most 2 re-engagements per lead ever and 10 drafts a day per account. It stops on a reply, a bounce or an unsubscribe.


PULSE_RESPONSE_TIME_WINDOW_DAYS, PULSE_RESPONSE_TIME_MIN_LEADS
unset, unset
The window in days and the fewest answered leads for the Response time card on Leads › Inbound. Either unset, or too few leads: it says Not measured, never zero. Nothing is sent. See First response to enquiries.


PULSE_VENDOR_PITCH_RETENTION_DAYS
90
Days before an answered pitch's sender address, company, quoted sentence and draft are erased (codes and stage stay).


PULSE_LINKEDIN_CTA_URL
https://runink.org
The address the daily LinkedIn draft ends with.


PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY
off
The second half of the audit-apply gate. With the kill switch, it allows the apply, commit, and pr modes of ApplyAuditActions (audit fixes), and Propose as pull request on the website repository, for administrators only. Off (or the kill switch off) refuses both before anything is read from or sent to GitHub.


Settings › Integrations › Website repository (per account, not an env var)
not connected
The customer's own site repository on GitHub, with a fine-grained token limited to that repository (Contents and Pull requests: read and write), sealed with the envelope key. An administrator connects it; the card shows connected, missing permission, token rejected, branch not found or unreachable. A proposal is one branch pulse/- and one pull request through the GitHub API: PULSE never pushes to the base branch, never merges, never edits .github/workflows/ or .git/, refuses .. paths and links, and caps a proposal at 20 files, 256 KiB each and 1 MiB in all. The plan gate judges the edit before the pull request is opened; a dissent opens nothing.


PULSE_APPLY_ROOT
unset, which refuses every mode
The only directory an audit fix's repo_path may resolve into. Applies to plan too.


PULSE_PUBLISH_AUTOMATIONS
off
Lets automations (the automation card a person opens on a lead or a campaign item) do outbound work: schedule a post, write to HubSpot, send email from the owner's mailbox, and place AI calls (which also need PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS, PULSE_AI_CALLS and the lead's consent record). Under the kill switch: both must be on, and each step still needs its own channel switch and the publisher allowlist. Each automation must also be armed by its owner; a dry run never sends.


PULSE_OPPORTUNITIES_DISCOVERY
on
The daily read of open procurement data (EU TED, UK Find a Tender and Contracts Finder, Brazil PNCP, CanadaBuys, and US SAM.gov for accounts that added their own key) and of requests for proposals found by PULSE's crawler, for every account with an offering to match. Reading only: nothing is sent or submitted, and the kill switch does not apply. Off stops the daily read; Find → Public tenders: look now on Leads still reads for the person who presses it. Drafting a response (on request, or the opt-in auto-draft) spends model time on the account's own inference.


PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS
off
One of the switches an AI call needs (with PULSE_AI_CALLS and the kill switch). The caller must also be an editor or admin.


PULSE_AI_CALL_ALLOWED_NUMBERS
unset
A comma-separated list of E.164 numbers. While it is set, this server places a call (AI call from the Call sheet, a plan, a sequence or an automation, or a Send / Call to a saved contact) only to a number on the list; every other number is refused with a plain reason, and only the last four digits are ever logged. Unset: no restriction. Set it to the test number before the first call and unset it afterwards. GET /health shows call_guard (list set yes/no and its size, the three switches), never a number.


Settings › Integrations › AI calls › Pause all AI calls now (per instance, not an env var)
running
An administrator pauses every AI call on this instance at once, with no restart, and resumes them later. Read at every call gate and again at the dial (a Send / Call to a saved contact too); a setting that cannot be read refuses the call. A call dialled but not yet answered is hung up; a conversation already running ends when someone hangs up. Each change is an audited record (who, when). GET /health call_guard.calls_pause shows running, paused or unreadable, and call_guard.languages the languages calls can speak: calls speak English until a translated call wording exists, whatever the account language is.


PULSE_AI_CALLS
off
Allows AI voice calls to leads (AICallService.PlaceAICall, AI calls). Needs PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true and PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS as well, an editor or admin, Twilio voice settings, PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL (https), and for each lead a recorded consent, a time zone and a drafted call script.


Settings › Integrations › AI calls (per account, not an env var)
off
The account's switch for AI calls from outreach sequences (Cold and follow-up calls from Leads). Only an administrator changes it. Off: a sequence's call step stays a task for the person and no call plan is drafted. On: the call step drafts a plan that a person must approve, call by call; the call is then placed through AICallService.PlaceAICall, so every switch and guard above still applies. Also per account: AI calls a day, how long transcripts are kept, how long an approval lasts, and the calling hours (inside allowed hours). Nothing about this feature is on by default, and recording is not an option: no audio is kept.


PULSE_AI_CALL_DAILY_CAP_DEFAULT, PULSE_AI_CALL_DAILY_CAP_MAX
5, 20
An account's AI calls in 24 hours: the default, and the most an account may set.


PULSE_AI_CALL_RETENTION_DAYS_DEFAULT, PULSE_AI_CALL_RETENTION_DAYS_MAX
7, 90
How long a call's transcript is kept (sealed) before it is erased; the outcome, answers and summary stay on the lead. The most an account may set.


PULSE_AI_CALL_APPROVAL_HOURS_DEFAULT, PULSE_AI_CALL_APPROVAL_HOURS_MAX
24, 168
How long an approved call plan may wait for the calling window before it lapses and must be approved again.


PULSE_SITE_CHAT_SITE_MESSAGES_PER_MINUTE, PULSE_SITE_CHAT_SITE_BURST, PULSE_SITE_CHAT_VISITOR_MESSAGES_PER_MINUTE, PULSE_SITE_CHAT_DAILY_MESSAGES
unset, which turns the website chat's visitor side off (503)
The website chat (Settings › Website chat): the PULSE assistant answering visitors of the account's own site from its public facts only (offerings, approved FAQ content, pages of its own site), on PULSE's own inference. Each one a positive number: the sustained rate and burst per site key, the rate per visitor address (held in memory only) and the visitor messages one site may send per UTC day (a contact or ask-a-person form counts as one). All four must be set, and PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL too for the snippet; Settings names what is missing. The site key in the snippet is public, works only from the addresses the owner listed, and is revoked or replaced there. Nothing is sent from it: a lead it makes (only with the visitor's consent) waits in Leads › Inbound like a website-form lead.


PULSE_SITE_CHAT_RETENTION_HOURS
168 (7 days), at most 720
How long a visitor's chat is kept before the hourly sweep deletes it. The widget states it to the visitor.


PULSE_RESULTS_PLAN_WINDOW_DAYS, PULSE_RESULTS_PLAN_MIN_EVIDENCE
unset, which stops the weekly results review from proposing anything (Settings names what is missing)
The weekly results-to-plan loop (per-account switch in Settings › Account, default off; loop results-to-plan, L1, one run per account per week, one structured model call): how many days of results it reads, and how many outcomes (leads, posts with readable results, replies) one row needs before it may decide anything. Both positive whole numbers; an unset, zero, negative or non-numeric value counts as unset. Runink's recommended starting values are 42 days and 6 outcomes, pending the owner's confirmation. Setting them does not switch the review on: each account still switches it on itself. It only proposes: a person approves or rejects on the plan page, and the live plan changes only on approval.


PULSE_MARKET_MEMORY_WINDOW_DAYS, PULSE_MARKET_MEMORY_MIN_EVIDENCE
unset, which stops the weekly market learning from learning anything (Settings names what is missing)
The weekly market-learning loop (per-account switch in Settings › Account, default off): how many days of results it reads, and how many outcomes one row needs before anything is remembered from it. Both positive whole numbers; an unset, zero, negative or non-numeric value counts as unset. Runink's recommended starting values are 60 days and 5 outcomes, pending the owner's confirmation. Setting them does not switch learning on: each account still switches it on itself.


Settings › Account › Use what PULSE learned when drafting (per account, not an env var), PULSE_MEMORY_DRAFT_MAX_FACTS
off for every account; the cap is 5 when unset
Lets PULSE give a drafting skill (posts, captions, stories, reels, video scripts, LinkedIn company updates, newsletters, blog articles; never a reply, a message or an extraction) a few of the entries of What PULSE has learned about your market, fenced as data and ranked in code by channel and topic, then confidence, then recency. Needs weekly learning on and the two PULSE_MARKET_MEMORY_ settings above; Settings names what is missing, or says "No learned facts yet". Only active entries built from the account's own counts, not imported and unconfirmed, above the confidence floor, with no link, address or phone number. The cap is a whole number from 1 to 10 (unset, zero or unreadable is 5, above 10 is 10). A draft keeps the entry numbers it used; each saved draft logs one line with counts only. See What PULSE has learned.


PULSE_ADVISOR_WINDOW_DAYS, PULSE_ADVISOR_MIN_EVIDENCE
unset, which stops the weekly growth advisor from suggesting anything (Settings names what is missing)
The weekly growth advisor (per-account switch in Settings › Account, default off; loop advise-growth, L1, one run per account per week, no model call): how many days of results it reads, and how many outcomes one row needs before an option may rest on it. Both positive whole numbers; an unset, zero, negative or non-numeric value counts as unset. The owner chooses the values. Setting them does not switch the advisor on: each account still switches it on itself. It only suggests: a person approves (one edit of the plan, as their own) or rejects with a reason, and nothing is sent, published or called.


PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL
unset
The public origin for absolute podcast-feed links, and the base of the mailbox OAuth callback /oauth/mail/callback. Without it, an armed feed answers 503 instead of rendering links nobody can fetch, and Gmail / Microsoft 365 cannot be connected (SMTP still can). It must be https for Connect with Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn and Search Console to be offered, and for Instagram to fetch media; the TIDDE edge must route /oauth/social/callback and /oauth/search-console/callback to PULSE. See Public address and redirects.


PULSE_JUDGEMENT
on
off turns the plan gate off: proposals are no longer judged before they are saved, and Autopilot answers nothing by itself (an auto-reply needs the plan gate to agree). Leave it on.


PULSE_RERANKER
on
off (any case) stops the relevance ranking that picks which of the pages and search results gathered for a diagnostic go into the analysis. On, a small ranking service scores each passage against the question and the best ones that fit the budget are kept. Off, or when that service is unreachable or does not answer in time, the passages are ranked by word overlap with the question instead, for the whole set, and the diagnostic's progress card says which ranking was used. Nothing is blocked either way: only the choice of passages can differ.


PULSE_DATA_EXPORT
on
off, 0, false or no stops Export my data: a request is refused with a plain message and nothing is prepared. PULSE_DATA_EXPORT_MAX_MB (default 200) is the most one copy may hold; a larger one fails with that reason.


PULSE_ROADMAP_WINDOW_DAYS, PULSE_ROADMAP_MIN_EVIDENCE
unset, which stops the weekly roadmap proposer from suggesting anything (Settings names what is missing)
The weekly roadmap proposer (per-account switch in Settings › Account, default off; loop propose-roadmap, L1, one run per account per week): how many days of results it reads, and how many measured outcomes a channel needs before a post may be suggested for it. Both positive whole numbers; an unset, zero, negative or non-numeric value counts as unset. The owner chooses the values. It only suggests new posts (topics from the audit, channels with enough measured results, days inside the account's own weekly capacity, each with its evidence): a person adds them to the roadmap, edits them or rejects them, and nothing is drafted, scheduled, sent or published. See Weekly roadmap suggestions.


PULSE_ROADMAP_DRAFT_AHEAD_DAYS, PULSE_ROADMAP_DRAFT_DAILY_CAP
3, 2
Drafting approved roadmap posts ahead of time (per-account switch in Settings › Account, default off; loop draft-roadmap, L1, one run per account per day): how many days ahead of a post's day its draft is written, and how many drafts one account gets a day. Positive whole numbers; an invalid value is ignored (the default is used) and Settings names it. Only posts a person approved from a roadmap suggestion are drafted, through the same content skills as the Studio and behind the audit work in the model lane; every draft waits in the approval queue (pending_review) and nothing is approved, scheduled or published by it. Switching it on does not publish anything.


PULSE_SHORTS_ENGINE, PULSE_SHORTS_DAILY_CAP
on, 1
The daily short-video draft (per-account switch in Settings › Account, default off; loop shorts-engine, L1, one run per account per day): exactly off stops it for every account, and the cap is how many drafts one account gets a day (0 to 10). It only drafts: the piece waits in the approval queue and nothing is scheduled or published until a person approves it. Switching it on does not publish anything. See Short videos.


PULSE_VOICEOVER_MAX_PARALLEL
1
How many voice-overs are spoken at once on the whole server (1 to 4). The speech service is shared GPU capacity, so the default is one: other jobs show "waiting for a free voice slot". It does not change the per-account rule (one voice-over being made at a time) or the daily limit (20, counted when the voice-over is asked for). See Voice-over studio.


PULSE_LIPSYNC
off
Exactly on (also true, 1, yes) lets a person make a lip-synced presenter video from their own twin, on the platform's own servers (no third-party AI). Off, or with the service not available, the button is disabled and says why; nothing is sent anywhere. Only for the person's own twin while its appearance consent is active; every video carries a visible "AI-generated" label, and is deleted if the consent is withdrawn or the twin deleted. See Lip-synced presenter videos.


PULSE_IMAGEGEN
off
Exactly on (also true, 1, yes) lets a person make still images from a description (Studio › Create image), on the platform's own servers. Off, or with IMAGEGEND_URL unset, nothing is sent to the service and a person still gets a branded card drawn by PULSE in the account's colours (labelled "Branded card"); the switch only turns on the AI upgrade. Each account also has its own switch (Settings › Account, off by default) that governs only the AI picture. Every image is a draft and is never used or sent without a person's approval. See Create an image.


IMAGEGEND_URL
unset
The address of the platform's image service. Unset means "not set up": a stated state, not an error.


IMAGEGEND_CALLER_KEY_FILE
/etc/runink/imagegend-caller/pulse
Where PULSE's caller key for the image service is mounted. The key is read again on every call, so a rotated key needs no restart.


PULSE_IMAGEGEN_DAILY_CAP
20
Pictures one account may ask for per day (at most four per request). A value that is not a positive number is 20.


PULSE_OWN_VOICE
off
Exactly on (also true, 1, yes) lets a person make voice-overs in their own voice, from their own consented recording in Digital twins. Off, or with the account's own switch (Settings > Account, off by default) off, or with the platform's voice service having recorded voices off, the option is not offered or reads "not available on this server", and nothing is sent to the voice service. The voice service must have custom voices enabled (its own setting, off by default; it keeps two speech models in memory and uses the server's graphics card, so raise its memory first). A voice is never used for calls and is never described as watermarked. See Voice-overs in your own voice.


PULSE_OWN_VOICE_DAILY_CAP
5
Voice-overs in their own voice one account may make per day, on top of the 20 a day all voice-overs share. A value that is not a positive number is 5. A script is at most 3,000 characters.


PULSE_STUDIO_MEDIA
on
Exactly off is the one emergency flag that stops the package a person's Studio request makes for a script (YouTube Short, Reel, Story): its short video and its image (an AI picture, else a branded card). Default on; the shorts-engine and image switches never stop it. The video waits for an encoder (PULSE_VIDEO_ENCODER, default auto: h264, else vp9) and the reason is in /health video.


PULSE_ENV
unset
production (any case) turns the startup security check from a warning into a refusal to start. The platform sets it on production deployments. See below.


PULSE_GRPC_REFLECTION
off
true turns on gRPC reflection. For local work only; PULSE_ENV does not affect it.


AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS
empty, which means nobody
Who may sign in with Google.


AUTH_GOOGLE_ONLY
off
Exactly true hides the password form.


AUTH_SEED_USERS
unset
Operator-granted roles as email=persona,…, re-applied at every start. See Seeded roles.


SELF_HEAL_AUTONOMOUS
on
An explicit no stops the self-healing loop applying anything; plans are still reasoned and recorded. See Operations.


PULSE_WHATSAPP_AUTOREPLY
off
An explicit yes lets PULSE answer inbound WhatsApp and SMS messages with a model-written reply. Each reply is a send, so it also needs PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true and PULSE_PUBLISH_WHATSAPP (or PULSE_PUBLISH_SMS for an SMS) not switched off. Each reply also passes My rules and the partnerships agent's limits; one they hold is not sent. Off, messages are still received and nothing is answered. See Telephony and messaging.



Every switch is also reported in the server log at startup; ask Runink to
confirm what is armed.
Safe arming order
Turn things on one at a time, and check the startup log after each restart.

Confirm the production gate passes
With PULSE_ENV=production, the server refuses to start on an insecure
configuration. Before setting it, confirm that the current pod logs
security config validated. See Operations.

Name who may publish as the deployment
Set PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS to the owner's , as shown in Admin. Do this before arming, so that the moment the
kill switch goes on, only the owner's content can leave on LinkedIn, the blog,
or the podcast feed.

Narrow the channels you do not want
Set PULSE_PUBLISH_=false for each channel that must stay off,
including PULSE_PUBLISH_LINKEDIN=false if LinkedIn is to stay drafts-only,
PULSE_PUBLISH_EMAIL=false if users must not send email from PULSE, and
PULSE_PUBLISH_WHATSAPP=false / PULSE_PUBLISH_SMS=false if nobody may message
from PULSE.
Narrowing first means arming the global turns on only what you meant.

Set up the sign-in apps, if people should connect with one click
Set an https PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL routed by the TIDDE edge, then the app
clients: META_APP_ID / META_APP_SECRET, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID /
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID / LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET. None of
them publishes anything: connecting only stores a sealed token. What each
developer console needs is on Setup. Leave
LINKEDIN_COMPANY_PAGES off until LinkedIn has approved the Community
Management API for the app.

Arm the kill switch
Set PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true. Confirm with Runink that each channel shows as
armed in the startup log, and that audit-apply is still off.

Arm server writes, only if you need them
To let administrators apply audit fixes, set PULSE_APPLY_ROOT to the
directory that holds the site checkouts, then PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY=true. Leave
both unset to keep the server read-only. The same two switches arm Propose as
pull request on a connected website repository (Settings › Integrations ›
Website repository), which needs no PULSE_APPLY_ROOT: it writes only to a new
pulse/ branch on GitHub and opens a pull request for a person to merge.

Arm automations, only if you need them
Set PULSE_PUBLISH_AUTOMATIONS=true once the channels the automations use are
armed and allowlisted. Each automation still runs by itself only after its owner
arms it, and every step runs with the owner's role.

Let accounts run on Autopilot, only if you want that
Autopilot is switched on per account by its owner, under Settings ›
Integrations › Autopilot. It adds no server key: it sends only through
channels you armed above, so a channel you narrowed stays off for Autopilot
too. To stop every Autopilot post at once, unset PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED (or the
channel's PULSE_PUBLISH_): queued posts are then recorded
withheld when they come due and are never replayed when you re-arm.
Two things are separate from Autopilot's switch and off until someone turns
them on: suggested YouTube comments on other people's videos (the
PULSE_PUBLISH_YOUTUBE_COMMENTS row, off even when everything else is armed)
and hiding spam on the account's own posts (it uses the reply switches). Both
only ever act after a person approves.

Arm outbound calls, only if you need them
Set PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS=true and PULSE_AI_CALLS=true once the Twilio voice
settings are in place and the compliance work for calling real numbers is done. See
Telephony and messaging.


To disarm, reverse the order, or simply unset PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED: that stops
every channel, the audit-apply modes and the daily site-audit engine at once.
It also stops every automation's outbound steps. It does not stop outbound calls, WhatsApp and SMS replies, or self-healing,
each of which has its own key.
PULSE_ENV=production
The platform sets PULSE_ENV=production on production deployments. With it set, the server refuses to
start, logging refusing to start in production, when:

the session key (PULSE_JWT_SECRET) is missing or is one the platform
refuses, or
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset or contains *. The backend serves no web
bundle, so there is no same-origin exemption: pin the origins in the
deployment.

A missing or refused session key stops startup whatever PULSE_ENV says; what
production adds is that the CORS problem stops it too, instead of warning.
PULSE_ENV also changes one TLS log line. It does nothing else: no billing,
usage counting, or plan behavior reads it, and it does not turn reflection on or off.
Messaging a lead at their own number
Do it on a lead's WhatsApp or SMS step can text the lead's own number, not
only a contact an admin added. Every rule below is enforced on the server:

SMS only, after a confirm tap. The person sees the exact text and the
masked number, and taps to send. It still needs PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true
and PULSE_PUBLISH_SMS not switched off.
Only a number with a recorded source. A phone number counts only when
PULSE recorded where it came from: the lead's own web page (the audit), a
person typing it into PULSE, your website form, or HubSpot. The Leads page
shows the source. A number without a source is never texted.
STOP is honoured. A reply of STOP (also STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END,
QUIT, PARAR, SAIR, BAJA, ARRET) is recorded for that number. After that, the
lead's step no longer offers WhatsApp or SMS, and a message that was already
previewed is refused when confirmed. START, YES or UNSTOP lifts the block.
When Twilio itself refuses a send because the number unsubscribed (error
21610), PULSE records the same block. For the replies to reach PULSE, set the
Twilio number's "A message comes in" webhook to
/comms/twilio/inbound. PULSE checks Twilio's
signature on every request, and the webhook refuses everything (503) while no
auth token is set.
WhatsApp needs an approved template. Meta only lets a business start a
WhatsApp conversation with a template it has approved. The shared carrier
sends plain text only, so PULSE never starts a WhatsApp conversation with a
lead. Do it says so plainly and offers SMS or email instead. WhatsApp to
a contact an admin added works as before.

Checked against the code
Every key on this page is read by the backend or,
for AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS and PULSE_JWT_SECRET, by the shared security
library it uses. The backend also reads these keys, which arm nothing and are
listed on the configuration reference:
LINKEDIN_API_BASE,
LINKEDIN_API_VERSION, LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN, LINKEDIN_AUTHOR_URN,
GOOGLE_TOKEN_ENDPOINT, MESH_ISSUER_URL, MESH_ISSUER_TOKEN_FILE,
FFMPEG_PATH and the rest of the storage, inference, telephony and billing
settings.
Knowledge export and import (market memory)
Settings › Account › market memory can export what PULSE learned as an Open
Knowledge Format bundle and read one back. There is no switch to set: both
actions are for a person's own session (an editor or administrator; service
accounts and automated runs are refused), the export needs the media store the
data export already uses, and the import needs the account's learning switch on.
Limits: one export an hour per account, a 1 MiB file, at most 700 files and 4 MiB
unpacked, and 300 imported entries per account. The export is sealed in the
media store under the account and removed after two hours; the link is the store's
signed, short-lived download link, so no new public address exists. Each use is
one counts-only line in the log.

docs/admin-guide/publishing-controls/.title: Publishing controls
docs/admin-guide/publishing-controls/.body:
Publishing controls

PULSE drafts a great deal on its own: daily social copy, blog posts, podcast
episodes, videos. Whether any of it leaves the building is decided by two
layers of switches, and nothing is armed by default.
Every switch, with its default and the order to turn them on, is in one table
on Switches and arming order.
The rule
armed(channel) = PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED is exactly "true"
                 AND the channel's own setting is on


PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED is the kill switch. It is off unless it is exactly
the lowercase string true. When it is off, no channel can publish, whatever
else is set.
Each channel can then be narrowed. A channel with no setting of its own
follows the kill switch. A channel setting can only turn a channel off.
It can never turn one on when the kill switch is off.

The channels



Channel key
What it publishes




blog
A Hugo post on your website, through GitHub. See Site pipeline.


podcast
Podcast episodes, by adding them to the public RSS feed


audiobook
The weekly long-form book, in the same feed


youtube
Real uploads to a YouTube channel, under the operator's Google identity


linkedin
Text posts as the connected member, or as the company page chosen on the LinkedIn card. The daily LinkedIn draft is written whatever this says; see below.


instagram
Has its own control, so the channel is governed by the same switch


spotify
Has its own control, under the same rule



Setting a channel
A channel's own setting comes from the first of these that holds a clear yes or
no:

An environment variable, PULSE_PUBLISH_, for example
PULSE_PUBLISH_YOUTUBE=false. It accepts 1, t, true, y, yes, on
and 0, f, false, n, no, off.
A config file, at PULSE_PUBLISH_CONFIG_PATH (a file Runink places on
your deployment), or the same JSON inline in
PULSE_PUBLISH_CONFIG_JSON when there is no file.
The built-in default, which is on. Combined with a kill switch that is
off by default, nothing publishes until someone arms the global.

The config file accepts either shape:
[{"channel": "youtube", "armed": false}]

{"channels": [{"channel": "youtube", "armed": false}]}

A channel missing from the file has no opinion. A file that cannot be read or
parsed is ignored and changes nothing in either direction.
Checking what is armed
At startup the server logs, for each channel, whether it is armed and which
layer decided; a refused publish logs which layer refused it. Ask Runink for
that log.

Warning: PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=yes, on, 1, or TRUE does not arm anything. The
server warns about it at startup. Write exactly true.

What disarming does to queued posts
The kill switch applies at the moment of publishing, not only when a post is
queued. A scheduled post that comes due on a disarmed channel is marked
withheld, with the reason. That is final. Re-arming does not replay the
backlog; schedule the content again to re-queue it.
Approving content does not bypass the switch either. An approval is consent to
the content, and the switch is a statement about the channel.
Who may publish as the deployment
Some channels publish with the user's own connected account (youtube,
instagram, spotify), so a user can only ever post as themselves. Others
publish as the deployment:



Channel
Why it is the deployment's




linkedin
The user's own LinkedIn connection (Settings → Integrations); the deployment's LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN only for a user with no connection


blog
The operator's PULSE_SITE_REPO


podcast, audiobook
The one public RSS feed at /podcast/feed.xml



On these channels, being armed is not enough. The content's owner must also be
listed in PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS, a comma-separated list of PULSE user
ids (as shown in Admin, not emails). Empty means nobody.

A dispatch by anyone else is recorded as withheld, with a reason naming
the owner gate. It is never reported as posted, and nothing is sent.
The daily blog, podcast and audiobook engines skip other users' campaigns
before generating, and log SKIPPED with the same reason.
The feed lists only allowlisted owners' episodes, and only for the channels
that are armed. With both podcast and audiobook disarmed,
/podcast/feed.xml returns 404.

A  is a user id as shown in Admin.
The daily LinkedIn draft
Once a day the social engine writes one LinkedIn post per active
campaign: a hook line, short paragraphs, three to five hashtags, and a closing
link to PULSE_LINKEDIN_CTA_URL (default https://runink.org). The row
belongs to the campaign's owner and waits on Approval with a Copy draft
button, so a person pastes it into LinkedIn.

The draft is never scheduled. The engine writes no scheduled_posts row
for it, and it needs no switch to be written.
A draft over LinkedIn's 3,000-character limit is still kept, and its title
says OVER 3000 CHARS, trim before posting.
A generation that fails, comes back empty, or is only a refusal is logged
and not stored.
One draft per campaign per day. A restart does not write a second one.

Approving a LinkedIn draft still offers it to the LinkedIn publisher. It is
recorded withheld, and nothing reaches LinkedIn, when the channel is
disarmed (PULSE_PUBLISH_LINKEDIN=false or the kill switch off), when no
LinkedIn token is configured (neither a connection nor, for a user without one, LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN), or when the owner is not in
PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS. The content stays approved, ready to copy.

Warning: Drafts-only is a setting, not a property of the code. With the kill switch
armed, LinkedIn not narrowed, a token configured, and the owner allowlisted,
approving a draft posts it. To keep LinkedIn drafts-only while other
channels are armed, set PULSE_PUBLISH_LINKEDIN=false.

A campaign that an audit created is a draft until someone activates it, so an
audit on its own produces no daily LinkedIn draft.
Outbound calls
The one call path is an AI call (AICallService.PlaceAICall). It needs
PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS=true and PULSE_AI_CALLS=true, both off by
default, PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true, a caller whose current role is editor or
admin, and the lead's consent, calling hours, do-not-call and attempt checks.
The Asterisk path (CallLead) is retired.
The same switch gates server writes
PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true is also what arms the daily blog drafting in the
social engine, and what starts the daily site-audit engine. With it off,
neither runs and neither costs model time.
It is not enough for the audit-fix modes of ApplyAuditActions (apply, commit, pr),
which write to the server's filesystem and run git with the server's
credentials. Those also need:



Variable
Default
Meaning




PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY
off
A narrowing key AND-ed with the kill switch. Unlike the channel keys it defaults off, so arming every channel does not arm server writes. Same yes/no tokens as PULSE_PUBLISH_.


PULSE_APPLY_ROOT
none
The only directory a repo_path may resolve into. Unset refuses every mode, plan included.



and the caller must be an administrator, read from the users table on every
call.
Channel-specific safeguards



Channel
Also needs




blog
A GitHub data source with a token, PULSE_SITE_REPO, and the content owner in PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS.


youtube
YOUTUBE_PRIVACY_STATUS. Unset means private, so an unreviewed upload is never public by accident.


linkedin
The token on the user's LinkedIn card (sealed in PULSE's store), else, for a user with no LinkedIn connection, LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN and LINKEDIN_AUTHOR_URN (a person or an organization URN). A company page also needs the app's Community Management API approval. The content owner in PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS.


podcast, audiobook
The owner in PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS, PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL, and the episode's audio must exist. Then submit /podcast/feed.xml once to each podcast platform.



Posting to LinkedIn as a company page
The LinkedIn card under Settings → Integrations holds the token PULSE posts
with. A user who has a LinkedIn connection always posts with it; a
disconnected one posts nothing (the deployment token is not used instead). The
deployment's LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN is used only for a user with no LinkedIn
connection at all. The server log says which token each post used, and the
channel's readiness (ListChannelReadiness: credential_source,
author_kind, author_urn) shows it before anything is posted.
Choose who posts on the card lists the company pages the token may post as
(LinkedIn roles ADMINISTRATOR or CONTENT_ADMINISTRATOR). Pick one, and
approved posts are authored by urn:li:organization:. Leave it on Me
to post as the member; PULSE then reads the member id from LinkedIn
(/v2/userinfo, which needs the openid and profile scopes).
Owner action first. LinkedIn lets an app list and post as company pages
only after it approves the app for the Community Management API. The token
then needs w_organization_social (to post) and rw_organization_admin (to
list the pages). Until then the list is empty and the card says why. Every
other gate still applies: PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED, PULSE_PUBLISH_LINKEDIN, and
the owner in PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS.
With the instance's LinkedIn app configured (LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID,
LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET) and LINKEDIN_COMPANY_PAGES=true, Connect company
pages on the card signs in with the page scopes instead of a pasted token.
See LinkedIn.

docs/admin-guide/site-pipeline/.title: Site pipeline
docs/admin-guide/site-pipeline/.body:
Site pipeline

PULSE can run a company website's content loop end to end: it writes blog posts
and publishes them to the site's Hugo repository, audits the live site every
day, and opens pull requests that fix what the audit finds. Runink runs its own
site this way. Each deployment points PULSE at its own site. There are no
defaults that name Runink.
Blog posts to your Hugo site
How a post gets there

A post is written. Either the social engine drafts one blog article per
active campaign per day, or you approve blog-channel content yourself.
It is scheduled. The social engine schedules its draft two hours
ahead. That window is a chance to cancel it on the Schedule screen before
the worker dispatches it.
It is published over git. PULSE renders the content as a Hugo post at
/.md and, by default, opens a pull request on branch
pulse/publish-. Nothing goes live until someone merges it.

No third-party social API is involved. The post goes to your own repository
with your own GitHub token.
Settings



Variable
Default
Meaning




PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED
off
Must be exactly true.


PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY
off
Audit-fix apply/commit/pr only (not the blog). Must also be on for those modes.


PULSE_APPLY_ROOT
none
The only directory an audit-fix repo_path may point into. Unset refuses every mode.


PULSE_PUBLISH_BLOG
follows the global
Set false to silence only the blog.


PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS
empty (nobody)
User ids whose content may publish to the site. Others are withheld, and their campaigns get no daily draft.


PULSE_SITE_REPO
none, required
owner/repo of your site.


PULSE_SITE_BRANCH
main
Base branch.


PULSE_SITE_BLOG_DIR
content/blog
Where posts go.


PULSE_SITE_PUBLISH_MODE
pr
pr opens a pull request. commit pushes to the base branch and is live at once.


PULSE_SITE_AUTHOR
omitted
The author in the post's front matter.


PULSE_SITE_BASE_URL
omitted
Your site's base URL, used for the canonical link.



The GitHub token comes from the GitHub connection of the user who owns the
content. See Connections.
When it refuses



Message
Cause




website publishing is disabled: ...
The blog channel is not armed. The message names the layer that decided.


no github integration/token configured for user ...
The content's owner has no GitHub connection.


PULSE_SITE_REPO is not set — refusing to publish; set it to YOUR site repo as owner/repo
No target repository.


invalid site repo "...": expected owner/repo
The repository is malformed.


refusing to publish empty content
The post has no title or body.



The daily blog drafting only runs while the blog channel is armed. A disarmed
channel costs no model time.
The daily site audit
Once a day, at 03:47 UTC, the site audit engine runs the relevance audit
against one URL and stores the full report. It also files a readable digest as
content on the site_audit channel. That channel is not publishable: the digest
exists to be read.



Variable
Meaning




PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED
Must be exactly true, or the engine does not start at all. One autonomy switch covers the engine and the publishers alike.


PULSE_SITE_AUDIT_URL
The site to audit.


PULSE_SITE_BASE_URL
Used when PULSE_SITE_AUDIT_URL is unset.



Disarmed, the engine logs
Site Audit Engine: NOT started — autonomy is disarmed (PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED is not "true").
Armed but with no target, it logs
Site Audit Engine: NOT started — no target site; set PULSE_SITE_AUDIT_URL (or PULSE_SITE_BASE_URL).
The first audit after a deploy waits for the next 03:47 UTC slot. For a score
now, start a New site audit on Brand Analysis; its full report is the
site-score report. Each audit is limited to 10 minutes. A
run that scored nothing, for example because the site was unreachable, is
recorded as a failure rather than a result.
The engine audits and records. It never fixes. Fixing stays a human
decision.
Audit-fix pull requests
From a relevance audit report, a person can apply the fix artifacts to a site
repository (ApplyAuditActions). See
Apply the fixes.

Every mode, plan included, needs PULSE_APPLY_ROOT set and a repo_path
that resolves inside it. Anything else gets one generic refusal.
plan is a dry run. Like every ApplyAuditActions call, it needs an editor
or admin (the RBAC write tier).
apply, commit, and pr need PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true, PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY=true,
and a signed-in administrator. The role is read from the users table on
every call, not from the token.
In pr mode with a GitHub connection, PULSE opens the pull request against
the connection's owner and repo, on branch seo/pulse-remediation by
default, against main.
Copy and infrastructure changes are returned as manual and never applied.

Fixes proposed to the customer's own repository
Without any server checkout, a connected website repository (Settings ›
Integrations, connected by an administrator with a fine-grained token for that
one repository) lets an administrator press Propose as pull request on an
audit finding. PULSE reads the repository through the GitHub API, places the
fix, has the plan gate judge it, and opens one pull request from a new
pulse/- branch. It never pushes to the base branch and never
merges. It needs PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true and PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY=true, but
not PULSE_APPLY_ROOT. See Website repository.

docs/admin-guide/billing/.title: Billing
docs/admin-guide/billing/.body:
Billing

Settings → Subscription (/settings?tab=subscription) is the shared Runink
billing page from org-runink/ui. It is its own tab, beside Account and
never inside it: plan, seats, usage and purchases live here and nowhere else,
and the Account tab shows none of them. PULSE serves its API,
runink.ui.billing.v1.BillingService, over the org-runink/billing library,
with PULSE-specific hooks. The page shows PULSE's own plan, never another product's. For what an
administrator must know about plans and the trial, see
Plans; for prices, the
PULSE product page.
Where the subscription comes from
PULSE runs one deployment per tenant. The subscription is read from environment
variables that Runink's TIDDE platform sets on the deployment:



Variable
Meaning
When missing




TENANT_ID
The tenant
No subscription on record


SUBSCRIPTION_TIER
The plan tier, set by Runink.
trial


SUBSCRIPTION_SEATS
Number of seats
1


SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS
Subscription status
active


SUBSCRIPTION_PERIOD_END
End of the current billing period (RFC 3339)
No period shown



The tier, seat, and status defaults apply only when TENANT_ID is set. Without
TENANT_ID, the tab shows that no subscription is on record. It does not
invent a plan. A subscription whose SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS is not active,
trialing, or past due grants nothing: it is shown as suspended, never degraded
to a free tier.
The page derives the current period from SUBSCRIPTION_PERIOD_END. With no period on record, it shows no period.
Several purchasers on one instance
On an instance shared by several customers, RUNINK_ACCOUNTS_FILE (the
member-to-purchaser file the TIDDE platform provides) maps each signed-in person
to the purchaser who pays for their seat. A purchaser's own row sets their
plan and seats. People with no row fall back to
the instance's SUBSCRIPTION_* variables.
What each part of the page does



Feature
In PULSE




Overview of your subscription (GetOverview)
Works, from the variables above.


Estimate
Every line is either computed or says why it cannot be.


Checkout and the billing portal (StartCheckout, OpenPortal)
Subscriptions are bought through Runink, so both answer "not configured" and nothing on this page can charge.


Seats (ListSeats, AssignSeat, RevokeSeat)
Seats come from the subscription; the page shows no seats section.



Billing actions are logged to the process log as billing audit lines.

docs/admin-guide/plans/.title: Plans
docs/admin-guide/plans/.body:
Plans and the trial

This page holds only what an administrator needs to know. For plans and
prices, see the PULSE product page.

PULSE is sold on its own, per seat. A PULSE subscription does not include
FACE or any other Runink product. There is no compute meter, no overage and
no per-action or outcome fee.
Accounts are approved by Runink. There is no open sign-up and no
self-invite. To start, contact Runink through the product page.
The trial lasts 14 days, the same for every account. When it ends, the
workspace is read-only until a plan is bought; contact Runink. Trial work
runs in spare shared capacity and can be slower at busy times.
Roles follow the subscription. Runink's TIDDE platform keeps your
organisation's subscription and sets each listed account to editor or
viewer; an ended trial or a cancelled subscription makes it read-only.
Administrators are added by Runink. See
Users and access.
No plan sends your data to an outside AI service. See
Sovereign inference.

How the subscription reaches the Subscription tab of your deployment is on
Billing.

docs/admin-guide/telephony-and-messaging.title: Telephony and messaging
docs/admin-guide/telephony-and-messaging.body:
Telephony and messaging

PULSE has four voice and messaging paths. All of them are off until you
configure them.
The carrier settings themselves are admin-only, and they live on the
Account page under Messaging — not in the navigation rail.
Someone who is not an admin of this instance never sees the carrier fields.
Calls to leads
The one way PULSE calls a lead is an AI call over Twilio
(AICallService.PlaceAICall; see AI calls). Every
call passes the same guards: an editor or admin places it, the lead's recorded
consent covers that exact number, it is inside the calling hours, the
number is not on the do-not-call list (an unreadable list refuses the call), the
attempt cap holds, and the AI says it is an AI in its first sentence.
The earlier Asterisk path (LeadService.CallLead, the ASTERISK_* and
AUDIOSOCKET_ADDR variables) is retired: it dialled with none of those guards.
Browser voice calls
The app's full-screen call view lets a signed-in user talk with the assistant.
The platform's shared calling service carries the audio, and PULSE is only
the authenticated door to it. Where voice calling is not set up, the app says
so. Voice input also needs the platform's speech-to-text, which your
deployment provides.
WhatsApp and SMS
PULSE accepts inbound WhatsApp and SMS messages from Twilio at
/twilio/message, and answers with its marketing personas: the same set it
offers over A2A.

Every request must carry a valid Twilio signature (TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN).
Only senders who are contacts in PULSE's HubSpot account may talk to it.
PULSE_WHATSAPP_USER_ID picks whose HubSpot connection is used. The default
is to deny.
The edge generates text: analysis, content, strategy, research. Creating
leads or campaigns and approving content stay behind the signed-in gRPC API.
Replies are automatic only when switched on (below). Each one passes PULSE's
guardrails, and the incoming message is treated as data, never as
instructions. Replies run as the user set in PULSE_WHATSAPP_USER_ID; with
none set, nothing is answered.
Automatic replies are off by default. To turn them on, set
PULSE_WHATSAPP_AUTOREPLY=true; each reply is a send, so it also needs
PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true and PULSE_PUBLISH_WHATSAPP (or PULSE_PUBLISH_SMS)
not switched off. Otherwise messages are received but not answered.
My rules judge every reply. After the switches and before the reply
leaves, the account's My rules, its persona and the partnerships agent's
limits (contact hours 9 to 18, at most 10 a day) apply. Nobody is there to
confirm a warning, so a reply they do not allow is not sent; the draft is
kept on the lead's history as a withheld automatic reply with the reason, and
What was checked shows the steps.




Variable
Meaning




TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID, TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
The Twilio account


TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM, TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER
The WhatsApp sender and the SMS number


PULSE_WHATSAPP_USER_ID
The user whose HubSpot contacts form the allowlist, and as whom replies run


PULSE_WHATSAPP_AUTOREPLY
true turns automatic replies on (they also need the publish switches). Default: off



Send / Call to a saved contact
PULSE also has Send / Call to saved contacts, with an allowlist, a
confirmation for each send, a rate limit, a body cap, the recording notice and
an audit trail.

Only a saved contact can be reached. Admins add contacts on Account →
Messaging; a number that is not on the list is refused. A service
account can never message or call anyone.
The carrier settings are sealed with TIDDE_ENVELOPE_KEK. Without that
key the page refuses to store a secret rather than writing it in the clear.
Contacts, sealed settings and the delivery trail are kept in PULSE's
sealed store.
Variables. TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID and TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN come from the
secret store (with an environment fallback); TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM,
TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER and TWILIO_VOICE_FROM are settings. TWILIO_VOICE_FROM
is optional and falls back to TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER. What an admin saves on the
page overlays the environment.
Delivery states are posted back to /comms/twilio/status. Without
PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL there is no callback URL to give the carrier, so
states stay at accepted.
A call speaks and ends. It opens with the AI statement ("An automated AI
assistant makes this call."), then the recording notice, PULSE's greeting
and the summary; there is no interactive media leg on this path.

docs/admin-guide/operations/.title: Operations
docs/admin-guide/operations/.body:
Operations

Health
GET /health always answers HTTP 200 with:
{"status":"ok","model_ready":false,"port":8080}

The status code is deliberately unconditional. PULSE serves every non-AI
feature without a model, so a readiness probe here should catch a wedged or
unbound server, not an AI outage. Read model_ready for the model. It is true
only when the engine is running and has confirmed it can serve a request.
Self-healing
PULSE watches its own health and reacts to what it finds.
SelfHealService/GetStatus shows it working: whether it is healthy, the
last event, recent events, and how many remediations were tried and failed.
The service only observes.
Remediation is automatic by default and limited to non-destructive actions, otherwise it notifies you.
Nothing deletes data or touches a security control. See the
self-healing operations agent card.
To turn automatic remediation off, set SELF_HEAL_AUTONOMOUS=false. Plans are
still reasoned and recorded, but none is applied.
Logs
Logs are OpenTelemetry-shaped JSON on stdout, with service.name
pulse-backend and the version from APP_VERSION. Lines worth watching:



Log line
Meaning




refusing to start: ...
A fatal startup condition. The rest of the line names it.


AUTHENTICATION DISABLED — every request will be rejected as Unauthenticated
The session key is one that authz refuses. Fix PULSE_JWT_SECRET.


gRPC reflection ENABLED
Reflection is on. It should not be on a deployed instance.


security config validated, or a warning listing problems
The result of the production gate



The production gate
At startup PULSE checks for insecure configuration:

The session key is missing or refused.
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset or contains a wildcard. The backend serves no
web bundle and the image no longer sets PULSE_WEB_DIR, so there is no
same-origin exemption unless someone sets it by hand (do not).

With PULSE_ENV=production, either problem stops the server with refusing to
start in production. Otherwise it is a warning.
A missing or refused session key is the exception: it stops startup on every
deployment, whatever PULSE_ENV says, because a server that cannot verify its
own sessions has nothing safe to do. What production adds is that the CORS
problem stops it too.

Warning: Runink sets PULSE_ENV=production on production deployments, so a
deployment refuses to start on an insecure configuration.
Before applying it to a running instance, confirm the current pod logs
security config validated; otherwise the new pod will not start. PULSE_ENV
has no other effect: it does not touch billing or plans, and reflection has its
own opt-in, PULSE_GRPC_REFLECTION.

Audit pipeline health
Each stage of a one-line audit (Audit a domain)
reports its health to the operator console. A stage that wedges shows as stale
there rather than idle.
Every run ends with one log line, audit  ():  . A run has a time limit.
TLS
Pick one:



Setup
How




TLS at the edge (usual)
Nothing to set. The edge terminates TLS and speaks plain HTTP to PULSE.


Direct exposure
PULSE_TLS_CERT and PULSE_TLS_KEY. TLS 1.2 minimum, forward-secret AEAD suites only.


Service-plane mutual TLS
MESH_MTLS=true, with the mesh CA. Every client needs a mesh certificate. TLS 1.3 only. If the CA is unavailable, the server refuses to start rather than downgrade.



Rate limiting
PULSE_RATE_RPS and PULSE_RATE_BURST cap calls per peer IP. Over-limit calls
get ResourceExhausted before any other work. Off by default.
Licence gate
With a licence configured (LICENSE or LICENSE_FILE, verified with
LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY), every non-public call is refused with license expired
or invalid when its signature is bad or it has expired. With no licence
configured, nothing is gated.
Where the data is, and backups
Everything PULSE keeps is in its appfs root, bucket pulse on the platform's
object store. Every object there is sealed under PULSE's own key, derived from
TIDDE_ENVELOPE_KEK. Back up that bucket with the object store, and keep the
KEK: without it the backup cannot be read.
Once encrypted rows in the new envelope format exist, do not roll back to a
build from before that format: it cannot read them.
The speech block
GET /health also carries a speech block, so one request shows whether voice and audio can
work: configured (voice output is set up), caller_key_set and caller_key_ok (a caller key
file is named; it is there and not empty: yes or no, never its value), reachable (ttsd answered
its voice catalogue within the last 30 seconds), unreachable_code (why not: voice_unauthorized
means ttsd refused this app's key, voice_key_unreadable means the mounted key file is missing or
empty, voice_unreachable means no answer) and last_error_code (the code of the latest real
synthesis error, empty when the latest one worked). It never carries a URL, a key or ttsd text.

docs/admin-guide/web-reading/.title: Web reading settings
docs/admin-guide/web-reading/.body:
Web reading settings

Every page PULSE reads from the public web (search results, lead and buyer
pages, trending posts, competitor channels, the site audit, the new-audit
preview, tender searches) goes through one reading profile, shared with the
rest of the Runink platform.
How PULSE reads the web



Behaviour
Value




robots.txt
Obeyed. A missing or unreadable robots.txt allows; an explicit Disallow skips the page.


Identity
One identity for every web read; PULSE never switches between identities.


Pacing
Reads are paced so that no site is burdened.


Private addresses
Loopback, private, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are refused, on the address and on every redirect.



When robots.txt disallows a page
The page is not requested. The skip is counted and shown where the results
are shown, with the reason skipped: robots.txt disallows . It is never
an empty answer and never a failure that is retried.

Check-up research (leads, trending posts, competitor channels, guests):
the stage line says how many pages were skipped and for which sites.
Lead search: the progress log and the run's report say the same.
Site audit: a disallowed page carries the reason instead of a result.
New-audit preview: the wizard shows the reason instead of the page.

The site audit still reads a site's robots.txt, llms.txt and sitemap as audit
signals: reading robots.txt is how a disallow is learned.
Search engines' own result pages obey robots.txt too: an engine whose
robots.txt disallows its result pages is never asked, and the skip is
recorded like any other.
Other sources



Source
Behaviour




Public tender APIs (TED, OCDS, PNCP, CanadaBuys, SAM.gov, job boards)
Documented APIs, not pages.


Your connected accounts (Google Ads, Google Analytics, HubSpot and others)
Read through their APIs with your own grant, not from the web.

docs/admin-guide/agents-reach-the-user/.title: Agents that reach the user
docs/admin-guide/agents-reach-the-user/.body:
Agents that reach the user

When PULSE's assistant cannot answer from the account's own data, it can ask
the account's owner one short question. The owner answers in the app or by
replying to a message on their own phone. Everything is off by default.
What the owner sees

Settings › Account › Agents that ask you: the open questions with an
answer box and Dismiss, and the switches.
The bell shows "An agent has a question for you" while one is open.
A question is always shown in the app. It needs no carrier.

When a message goes to the phone
A message (SMS or WhatsApp) goes out only when the owner has opted in and an
administrator has set up messaging. If a message is not sent, the reason is
written on the question ("Not sent as a message: why") and the question stays
in the app.

Opt-in. Agents may message me on my phone is on (default off). The
person picks one of the contacts an administrator added in Admin ›
Messaging; a lead is never offered.
Approval. The assistant proposes the question as a card the person
confirms, like every assistant action, unless the person has switched on
Don't ask me first each time (off by default, revocable).
Quiet hours. The person chooses them.
Administrator switches. The carrier is configured (Admin › Messaging) and
PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED with PULSE_PUBLISH_SMS or PULSE_PUBLISH_WHATSAPP are
armed. These are the same switches every message uses.
Pause. An administrator can pause questions in Admin ("paused by your
administrator").

SMS is the default channel; WhatsApp only accepts a business-initiated
message inside its own messaging window. A refusal leaves the question in the
app with the carrier's reason.
Calls are not part of this. The one call path stays PlaceAICall.
Replies
Point the Twilio "A message comes in" webhook of the SMS sender at
/comms/twilio/inbound; the WhatsApp edge (/twilio/message) is wired too. A
reply to the message is attached to the question. A reply of STOP closes the
question and switches the opt-in off. The answer is removed with the account.

docs/admin-guide/answer-vendor-pitches/.title: Answer vendor pitches
docs/admin-guide/answer-vendor-pitches/.body:
Answer vendor pitches

Answer vendor pitches lets an account's PULSE answer an unsolicited vendor
pitch with that account's own counter-offer (see the user
guide). It is the first thing PULSE
sends to a stranger on its own, so it is off for every account and has no
switch of its own on the server: it is armed by the arming switches you already
know, plus the account's own switch.
What decides whether anything is sent
Every answer passes, in this order, and stops at the first refusal:

the account's switch (Settings › Account, off by default) and its terms
(client offer, partnership offer, upfront-payment rule, signature) plus the
Outreach sender name and postal address and an https PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL
for the unsubscribe link. Missing any of these, nothing happens and Settings
names what is missing;
the fixed classification of the message, the one-answer-per-sender rule, the
suppression list and the ten-a-day cap;
the loop gate (Answer vendor pitches in the loop controls: a paused loop
sends nothing) and the screening of the answer;
My rules and the conscience gate, as the partnerships agent (contact
hours 09:00 to 18:00 and at most ten a day, plus the account's own rules);
the global kill switch PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED and the channel's own switch:
PULSE_PUBLISH_EMAIL for an answer sent from the account's mailbox (website
form), and PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM with PULSE_PUBLISH_INSTAGRAM_DMS for a
direct message, which also needs Autopilot on for Instagram and Meta's
24-hour window.

An answer a gate refuses is not lost: it waits in the account's partner
pipeline for a person.
Arming order

Arm nothing; let accounts fill in their terms and read the card's channel
lines.
Set PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL to the https address (needed for the
unsubscribe link) and the Outreach sender name and postal address.
Arm PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED and PULSE_PUBLISH_EMAIL as in the switches
page, then turn the account's
switch on.
Watch What PULSE did and why and the loop run list before arming
Instagram direct messages.

Honest limits

E-mail that arrives only in the mailbox is read only for an account that
switched on Read my inbox for vendor pitches (default off, separate from the
vendor-pitch switch), on a connected Gmail mailbox. Microsoft 365 and SMTP
mailboxes cannot be listed yet: the card says "Gmail only for now". There is no
unified inbox view and no measured response time for mail read this way yet.
Reading the inbox needs the gmail.readonly scope, a restricted Google scope.
Google verification is needed for users outside the project; that process, and
whether to start it, are decisions still open. Until they are made, leave the
switch for accounts you control. Nothing reads a mailbox unless the account
switched it on.
The reader lists at most 50 messages a page, four pages a tick, and 400 messages
an account a day. After an expired position it re-lists from the last message
seen minus one hour and skips what it already handled.
LinkedIn, WhatsApp, SMS and website chat have no answer path and are said so
on the card.
Nothing is ever sent to a sender who asked to stop; the one-click link in
every answer puts the sender on the same suppression list as outreach.

Questions: contact@runink.org.
Insights, the digest and retention
Three settings control what the account sees and how long senders' details stay:



Setting
Default
Effect




PULSE_VENDOR_INSIGHTS_WINDOW_DAYS
unset
Days the insights look back.


PULSE_VENDOR_INSIGHTS_MIN_PITCHES
unset
The fewest pitches before anything is said.


PULSE_VENDOR_PITCH_RETENTION_DAYS
90
Days before a pitch record's address, company, quoted sentence and draft are erased.



With the first two unset, the card What vendors pitching us tell us shows
nothing and names them. Fewer pitches than the minimum also shows nothing. Each
week with something measured, a digest record appears in the app for a person to
mark reviewed; nothing is sent. The insights are codes and counts only: the
pitches' text is not kept and no amount a sender wrote is stored.
A lead is made from a pitch only when a person accepts the proposal, from a
business address, never for a sender on the suppression list. Starting an outreach
sequence from it is still a person's approval.
Senders are third parties: PULSE processes their business contact details to
answer them and to summarise what pitches say. The records are sealed, belong to
one account, are removed with it, are part of its data export, and are never
logged with their text.

docs/admin-guide/first-response-to-enqui.title: First response to enquiries
docs/admin-guide/first-response-to-enqui.body:
First response to enquiries

First response lets an account's PULSE acknowledge a new website enquiry (see
the user guide). This page is what
an administrator needs: the switches, the order to arm them, and every gate.
Defaults



Setting
Where
Default




First response
Settings › Account, per account
off


Send acknowledgements automatically
Settings › Account, per account
off


First response wording
Settings › Account, per account
empty (a neutral sentence)


Unanswered threshold (hours)
Settings › Account, per account
unset (count with no threshold)


PULSE_RESPONSE_TIME_WINDOW_DAYS, PULSE_RESPONSE_TIME_MIN_LEADS
server
unset



Only an editor or an administrator, in their own session, changes the switches.
Arming order

The global kill switch PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED and the email channel switch
PULSE_PUBLISH_EMAIL (see Switches and arming order).
PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL must be an https address: the unsubscribe link is built
from it.
A connected mailbox, and the account's Outreach sender name and postal
address.
The account turns on First response. From that moment, new enquiries get a
draft. Nothing is sent without a tap. Enquiries from before that moment are
never looked at.
Only then, if the account wants it, Send acknowledgements automatically.
It applies to enquiries received after it was switched on.

If the sender name, the postal address or the https address is missing, nothing
happens and Settings lists exactly what is missing.
Every gate, in order
For each new enquiry from the website form: the feature is on; the sender name,
postal address and https address are present; the enquiry arrived after the
feature was switched on; the address is a business address, not suppressed, not
the account's own, not a customer's, not already contacted; the acknowledgement is
composed from a Go template (no model call); a draft is stored (loop
first-response, Allow("save first response draft")).
An automatic send additionally passes, in the one function deliver: the account's
working hours and daily cap; the loop gate (Allow("send first response")); the
outreach footer and its compliance check; OpenBias on the text; My rules and the
conscience gate, acting as the role pack partnerships-agent (contact hours 9-18,
ten a day, no first-contact approval of its own; the account's own rules still
apply); the shared mail service (the kill switch, PULSE_PUBLISH_EMAIL, the
mailbox limit). A person's Send runs the same function as that person; a
warning is confirmed with Send anyway, and a block stays a draft.
The record is claimed before the send, so one lead gets at most one
acknowledgement ever. The unsubscribe link (/first-response/unsubscribe/,
public like the website form's route) puts the address on the account's
suppression list.
What is kept
Per lead: the arrival time, the state, a reason code, and, while it is a draft or
after it was sent, the address and the text, sealed. The enquiry's own text is
never stored by this feature. The records are removed with the account and are
part of the Leads area of Export my data.
Response time
The card needs a window and a minimum, set on the server:



Variable
Meaning




PULSE_RESPONSE_TIME_WINDOW_DAYS
Days of enquiries the median and the 90th percentile cover.


PULSE_RESPONSE_TIME_MIN_LEADS
The fewest answered leads before a figure is shown.



Either unset, or fewer answered leads than the minimum: the card says Not
measured and why. It is never shown as zero.
Automations
The automation triggers trigger.form_submitted, trigger.reply_received,
trigger.engagement_received, trigger.meeting_detected and
trigger.lead_scored start flows from the same events. They carry ids and codes
only. See Automations.

docs/admin-guide/knowledge-probe/.title: Knowledge probe
docs/admin-guide/knowledge-probe/.body:
Knowledge probe

The knowledge probe is a command an administrator (or Runink's TIDDE platform)
runs on demand. It asks the model plane PULSE already uses a fixed set of
questions from PULSE's own work and reports, per domain, which questions the
model answers consistently, which it half knows and which it does not know.
It only reports. Nothing is promoted, no routing changes and no request is
refused because of a probe result. Using the result to gate anything waits for
a measurement on the production-size model, taken by the owner.
What it measures
Each question is asked once at a low temperature and then several times at a
higher one. Answers that mean the same thing (each entails the other, judged by
the shared claim-check service) form one group. A question whose answers fall
into one group is known; one whose answers scatter is unknown; the band
around the fitted threshold is partial. The threshold is fitted per domain
from that domain's own questions.
The domains are the ones PULSE's agents work in, and nothing is pooled across
them:



Domain
Agents
Questions on




analyst
market analyst
Site audit, search and AI visibility, market analysis


copywriter
copywriter, content creator
Social and email copy craft, platform rules


outreach
sales, partnership and voice agents
Cold email and call etiquette, deliverability, consent and opt-out


market
research, strategy and marketing agents
Competitors, channels, attribution, funnel metrics



There are 40 questions per domain, 160 in all: enough for the per-domain
threshold (it needs at least 20 answered questions) with room for failures.
Every question has a one-sentence reference answer and a source, which is a file
of this repository or a named public rule. The reference is used to score
whether the model's low-temperature answer was correct, which the comparison
needs.
It reads no customer data
The questions are data files shipped inside the program. They are written from
PULSE's own code, skills and documentation or from published rules, never from a
customer's leads, messages, calls or any account. The program reads no database
and no account file while probing, and tests refuse any e-mail address,
telephone number or URL in the question files. The probe's output holds ids,
labels and numbers only: no question text and no model answer.
Running it
A run is a deliberate act: inference time on the shared plane is used by every
app, and a full run is about 160 questions times 11 model calls. It is a
command, never a scheduled job, and no remote call can start it.
INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL= \
CLAIMCHECK_URL= \
CLAIMCHECK_CALLER_KEY_FILE= \
pulse probe --out  --label ""



Option
Meaning




--out
Required. Where the files are written. Refused inside a git work tree; files are never overwritten


--domains
Only these domains


--limit
Only the first N questions per domain (below 20, no threshold can be fitted and the domain reads not measured)


--samples
Samples per question (default 10)


--fake
A scripted generator and checker, no network: proves the pipeline only, writes no labels and can never be compared



The claim-check service needs a caller key issued to this caller. Without
CLAIMCHECK_URL and a key the command stops and says so.
Verified and unverified references
Each question's reference answer is the ground truth its correctness is scored
against. A reference taken from this repository's own code, skills or
documentation counts as ground truth. A reference taken from a public rule
(a law, a standard, a platform's published guidance) counts only once it has
been checked against the official text: it then carries the date it was checked
and the official address. Until then it is marked unverified.
Of the 160 questions, 31 are verified against official texts (the FTC's
CAN-SPAM guide, Canada's anti-spam Act, 47 CFR 64.1200, RFC 7489, Google's
sender and Search documentation, web.dev, W3C, the FTC's substantiation
statement and disclosures guide, and others), 92 come from this repository, and
37 remain unverified. Unverified questions are still asked and still listed in
the report with their count, but they are reported apart: the headline accuracy
uses verified and repository-sourced questions only, and a comparison never
uses an unverified one. If too few ground-truth questions remain in a domain,
that domain reads not measured for the comparison, never zero.
Probing a training pool
pulse probe --pool train/.jsonl --pool-meta meta/.train.jsonl --out 
The second mode probes a training pool itself, so that training can leave out
what the model already knows. Each line of the pool file is a training item
({"messages": [...]}); the meta file is line-aligned with it and gives each
item's id and domain. The prompt asked is the item's last user turn, the
question id is the item's meta id, and items with images are skipped and
counted. A minimal pool is also accepted: one {"id": "...", "prompt": "..."}
per line (add "domain", or pass --domain). The output is report.json,
summary.txt and one labels.jsonl (runink.knowprobe.labels/1) whose ids
are the meta ids, which is what the training run reads.
The pool is training data, never customer data: it is a file you name, the
command reads no account, appfs or database record, and it refuses a path
inside any such store. A pool with a duplicate id, a malformed line (the error
names the line), a missing id, prompt or domain, or a meta file that is not
line-aligned is refused. An empty pool reads not measured and writes no
labels. A pool run has no references, so it reports labels only, writes no
accuracy and can never be compared. --fake proves the pipeline and writes no
labels.
Outputs



File
Content




report.json
Schema runink.pulse.probe.report/1: per domain the counts, unknown share and threshold; per question the label, entropy and whether the answer matched its reference


summary.txt
The same, as a table


labels..jsonl
Schema runink.knowprobe.labels/1: id, domain, label and entropy, one line per labelled question. The analyst and copywriter files are the ones meant for the matching training data



A domain that could not run (no answer, too few questions, no spread between
answers) reads not measured with the reason. It never shows zero.
Comparing two runs
pulse probe --compare before.json after.json [--json]
For each domain the comparison asks the shared knowprobe gate whether the
candidate beats the baseline: the unknown share must not grow, accuracy on the
questions that were unknown must rise, and accuracy on those that were known
must not fall. Both reports must be live runs on the same question set. The
command prints the verdict and exits successfully whatever it says; the
promotion decision, and the call to this command, belong to TIDDE.

Architecture in one paragraph
A Go gRPC backend and a Flutter app for Android (iOS is planned and not yet
built) talk over gRPC on one port. The backend keeps all its data (every table, account, session and media
file) in a sealed store on the platform's object store; there is no database,
and one writer, so one instance. All AI is the platform's own, with no third-party model.
