docs/developer-guide/calling-the-api/.title: Calling the API
docs/developer-guide/calling-the-api/.body:
Calling the API

PULSE's API is gRPC, package pulse.v1, plus the shared runink.ui.*.v1
services. There is no REST or JSON API for business data.
Transports
Everything is on one port.



Client
How it connects




Native gRPC (Go, grpcurl, the Android app)
HTTP/2 with content-type: application/grpc


Browsers
gRPC-Web over the same port



For browsers served from another origin, the origin must be listed in
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS. The allowed request headers include Authorization,
X-Grpc-Web, grpc-timeout, x-agent-trace-id, x-idempotency-key,
x-pulse-csrf, and x-pulse-session.
Authenticate
On a development server, call IdentityService/Login with the break-glass
admin's username and password (people sign in with Google; see
Users and access). The token is in
accessToken:
TOK=$(grpcurl -plaintext -d '{"username":"admin","password":""}' \
      localhost:52000 pulse.v1.IdentityService/Login | jq -r '.accessToken')

Send it on every other call:
grpcurl -plaintext -H "authorization: Bearer $TOK" -d '{}' \
      localhost:52000 pulse.v1.CampaignService/ListCampaigns

Only three things work without a token: IdentityService/Login,
ModelService/GetModelStatus, and reflection (when it is turned on).
Refresh a session at POST /auth/refresh. See
HTTP endpoints.
Browsers: the session cookie
A browser has nowhere safe to keep a token — anything the page can store, any
script on the page can read — so the web client never receives one. It asks for
cookie mode by sending x-pulse-session: cookie on Login or on
POST /auth/google. The backend answers with no token in the body and sets the
session as a host-only, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie, which
the browser then attaches to every call by itself. Sign out at
POST /auth/logout, which revokes the session and clears the cookie; page
scripts cannot clear it themselves.
Because a cookie travels with any request to the host, whoever wrote the page, a
call authenticated by the cookie must prove it came from the PULSE app, in
two ways, both required:

the header x-pulse-csrf: 1 — a cross-site form cannot set a custom header;
an Origin the server trusts: the server's own host, PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL,
or an exact entry of CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS. A * never counts.

Native clients are unaffected: a bearer header is not sent automatically, so it
is not a cross-site risk, and neither proof is needed for it.
Roles
A valid session is the first gate; your account's role is the second, read fresh
from the server on every call rather than from the token. Reads that spend no
model time and change nothing need viewer; anything that generates, writes,
dials out or places a call needs editor; the access and messaging-settings
methods need admin. A call above your role fails with PermissionDenied.
GetCurrentUser and Logout work for any signed-in account, so someone with no
role assigned can still see that and sign out.
Discover the schema
With PULSE_GRPC_REFLECTION=true on a local server:
grpcurl -plaintext localhost:52000 list
grpcurl -plaintext localhost:52000 describe pulse.v1.LeadService

Reflection is off by default and must stay off on deployed instances. Without
it, use the API reference, or ask Runink for the
.proto files.
Streaming calls
Every AI generator is a server-streaming RPC that returns stream StreamChunk:



Field
Meaning




text
The next piece of output. May be empty.


is_final
True on the last chunk


section
A section marker, for example positioning, swot, or grounding


progress
0.0 to 1.0


metadata
Extra key-value data


agent_tasks
Actions the backend actually performed, such as a scrape. These are recorded facts, not model claims. A chunk with tasks may have no text.



Long generations can go quiet while the model thinks. When a stream has been
silent for a while, the server sends a status frame so proxies do not drop
the connection and so you can tell waiting from stalled. A status frame has
empty text and is_final false — append text blindly and you append nothing
— and says what it is in metadata:



Metadata key
Meaning




keepalive
1 on a frame that exists to keep the stream open


phase
queued, generating, finishing, editing, refused, or at_capacity


tokens
Progress so far, approximate


token_budget
The limit for this pass, not a prediction



refused means a guardrail declined to release the output: a complete answer,
and the next move is to change the brief rather than retry it. at_capacity
means the inference plane is saturated, where retrying later is right.
Use a generous deadline: a long document can take a long time.
When the model is busy, a call can fail with
ResourceExhausted. Retry after a few minutes.
Tie runs to your screen
Set x-agent-trace-id on your calls, and send the same value as session
in ActivityService/SubscribeAgentActivity. Then the activity stream shows
only the runs your client started. See Agent activity.
Errors
PULSE uses standard gRPC codes and puts a sentence meant for a person in the
message. Common ones:



Code
Typical cause




Unauthenticated
Missing, expired, or revoked token


PermissionDenied
Licence invalid, or your role does not allow the call


FailedPrecondition
Something must be set up first, for example a HubSpot connection or PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED


InvalidArgument
A required field is missing or has a bad value


ResourceExhausted
Rate limit, or the inference plane is at capacity


Unavailable
A dependency failed: HubSpot, GA4, speech synthesis, media storage


Unimplemented
The feature does not exist in this deployment, for example a feature this deployment does not include


NotFound
No such record, or it belongs to another account


Aborted
A long run ended in failure; the stream closes with this and the run's own error



See Troubleshooting for specific messages.
A2A: calling PULSE from another agent
PULSE publishes itself as an Agent2Agent (A2A) agent for Runink FACE and the Runink TIDDE
fleet:

Discovery: GET /.well-known/agent-card.json.
Calls: JSON-RPC at /a2a, with a PULSE session as a bearer token in the
Authorization header. Calls without a valid session are refused.

Choose a persona with the message metadata key skill. The default is
market-analyst.



Skill
Persona




market-analyst
Diagnostics, SWOT, positioning


content-creator
Channel content


copywriter
Long-form content and whitepapers


strategy-agent
Prescriptive 30-day plans


radar-agent
Trend and profile research

API reference

The API of Runink PULSE: Prescriptive Unified Lead & Social Engine is
gRPC, package pulse.v1. The contracts are PULSE's .proto files.
Browsers use gRPC-Web on the same port.
The few plain HTTP routes are listed under HTTP endpoints.
To call the API, see Calling the API.
The service pages below are generated from the protos and from the server's
role table, and a check fails when they fall behind, so every method listed is one the server has.

HTTP endpoints
Brand analysis and audits: Audit pipeline, diagnosis, research, Search Console, website repository
Leads, tenders and accounts: Leads and public tenders, AI calls, Integrations, agencies
Campaigns and results: Campaigns, plans, Autopilot, automations, metrics
Studio and content: Content, Studio, skills, publishing
AI and platform: Model, activity, identity, config, self-heal
Shared components: Billing, Connections, Profile, Access, Voice, Comms
Common types: commons.proto and unused types

Conventions

Authentication. Every method needs authorization: Bearer ,
except the ones whose least role is "none (public)" and gRPC reflection. The
browser client authenticates with a session cookie instead; see
Calling the API.
Roles. Each method has a least role, read fresh from your account on
every call: viewer for reads that spend no model time and change nothing,
editor for anything that generates, writes, dials out or places a call,
and admin for access and messaging settings. A call below your role
fails with PermissionDenied. "Any signed-in" methods (who am I, sign out)
work for an account with no role. Some methods check more than the role (an
admin row, an arming switch); the page notes say which.
Scoping. Data is scoped to the signed-in user. Request fields named
user_id do not let you read another user's data.
Streaming. AI generators return stream StreamChunk. See
Common types.
Errors. Standard gRPC status codes with a human-readable message. See
Troubleshooting.

HTTP endpoints

Besides gRPC and gRPC-Web, the backend answers a short, fixed list of plain
HTTP routes on the same port. None of them is a data API. Campaigns,
content, leads, and everything else are gRPC only.



Route
Auth
Purpose




GET /health
None
Always 200. Body: {"status":"ok","model_ready":,"port":}


GET /auth/config
None
{"google_client_id":"…","password_auth":} for the login screen


POST /auth/google
None (it is the sign-in)
Exchanges a Google ID token for a PULSE session. Same JSON shape as Login. With x-pulse-session: cookie it sets the session cookie and returns no token. A refusal is JSON {"error": , "message": …} (plus "email" for not_allowed), with codes not_configured (503), missing_token (400), csrf, sso_closed, not_allowed (403), invalid_token, wrong_client, email_unverified (401) and server_error (500).


POST /auth/refresh
Refresh token
Exchanges a refresh token for a new pair in the same session. Refused once the session is signed out.


POST /auth/logout
The session cookie
Revokes the browser session and clears the cookie. It clears the cookie even when the session has already expired, which is how a stale one is cleaned up.


/creatives/, /media/
The owner's session, or a server-signed URL
Generated media, decrypted from the sealed store


GET /podcast/feed.xml
None, on purpose
The podcast RSS feed that podcast platforms poll. Needs the deployment's public address.


POST /voice/webrtc/offer
Session
Starts a voice call with the assistant. 503 when calling is not set up.


POST /voice/transcribe
Session
Audio in, {"text":"…"} out


GET /.well-known/agent-card.json
None
The A2A agent card


/a2a
Session (bearer header only)
A2A JSON-RPC. See Calling the API.


POST /twilio/message
Twilio signature
Inbound WhatsApp and SMS


POST /inbound/leads/ (and OPTIONS)
The secret in the path; no session, no cookie
A website enquiry becomes a lead. Form-encoded, multipart or JSON, at most 16 KiB. CORS only for the sites listed on the link. See Website form.


POST /comms/twilio/status
Twilio signature
Delivery-status callbacks for messages and calls sent from the Send / Call panel. An unsigned callback is refused and changes nothing.


POST /comms/twilio/inbound
Twilio signature
Replies to PULSE's SMS sender: STOP and START (and their synonyms) are recorded for the number; other replies are not stored. Refuses everything (503) while no Twilio auth token is set.


POST /pulse/aicall/twilio/answer, POST /pulse/aicall/twilio/status
Twilio signature
An AI call's answer and its final status.


/pulse/aicall/twilio/stream/
A single-use token
The AI call's audio.


GET /oauth/mail/callback
The single-use state from the connect link
Google or Microsoft returns here after Connect Gmail or Connect Microsoft 365.


GET /oauth/social/callback
The single-use state from StartSocialConnect
Meta, Google or LinkedIn returns here after Connect with Instagram, YouTube or LinkedIn; the tokens are sealed and the window shows the result.


GET /oauth/search-console/callback
The single-use state from StartSearchConsoleConnect
Google returns here after Connect Search Console.


anything else
None
Not found (404). The backend serves no web app; PULSE is an Android app (iOS planned, not yet built).



Requests with gRPC-Web content types go to the gRPC server before any of these
routes are checked.
The three /oauth/…/callback routes are what you register as redirect URIs
in each developer console, under your deployment's public address. The social and Search Console sign-ins are
offered only when that address is https. The public edge routes them to the backend. See Public address and redirects.

docs/api-reference/shared-components/.title: Shared components
docs/api-reference/shared-components/.body:
Shared components

These services are defined in Runink's shared component library, not in
PULSE, and PULSE serves them with its own behaviour. This page covers what
PULSE does with each service.
runink.ui.billing.v1.BillingService
The Billing page. See Billing.



Method
In PULSE




ListPlans, QuotePlan
Work. Pure price arithmetic over PULSE's own plans, in US-dollar list prices.


GetOverview
The viewer's subscription (from their purchaser's row in RUNINK_ACCOUNTS_FILE, else TENANT_ID and SUBSCRIPTION_*) and, on a trial, the seat's daily fast-task count.


StartCheckout, OpenPortal
No payment provider: the answer is "not configured", never an error and never a URL that leads nowhere.


ListSeats, AssignSeat, RevokeSeat
PULSE keeps no seat roster.



runink.ui.datasources.v1.ConnectionsService
The Data sources tab. PULSE serves it over its own integrations table and
narrows the catalog to HubSpot and GitHub.



Method
Purpose




ListConnectionTypes
The connector types offered: HubSpot and GitHub


ListConnections, ListConnectionNames, GetConnection
Read your connections


CreateConnection, UpdateConnection, DeleteConnection
Manage them


RotateCredentials
Replace the stored token


TestConnection
Check the token against the platform



A connection that sets a runner, an environment, or properties is refused, and
nothing is stored.
runink.ui.datasources.v1.RunnersService
PULSE runs its connectors inside the server and has no remote runners. The
service is registered so the shared page can say so. It reports no runners.
runink.ui.profile.v1.ProfileService
The Account page. Plan and usage are the billing section embedded in it.



Method
In PULSE




GetProfile
Your email, display name, and role from the users table, plus your session. Tenant from TENANT_ID (the platform keeps no tenant display name). PULSE has no platform admin, so the page does not show that row.


ListInstances
The one instance this deployment serves, with your role and, when the instance's member list states it, when your access ends (or that it does not). Without that list the expiry shows as not stated. Marked as a local development instance only when not running in a cluster. The app's Admin menu entry reads this.


EndAllSessions
Ends all of your own sessions on every device



runink.ui.access.v1.AccessService
The Admin page. Admins only; the role is read fresh on every call. See
Users and access.



Method
Purpose




ListMembers
Members and their roles


InviteMember
Grant a person a role. PULSE does not limit invites by seats.


SetMemberRole
Change a role. Not your own, and never the last admin.


RemoveMember
Remove a member. Not yourself, and never the last admin.



runink.ui.comms.v1.CommsService
Send and Call: WhatsApp, SMS and voice calls to a contact an admin has
configured. Reads are open to any signed-in account, sending needs editor, and
the contact list and carrier settings are admin-only. Carrier settings are
sealed before they are stored.



Method
Purpose
Least role




GetCarrierStatus
Whether messaging is configured
viewer


ListContacts
The configured contacts
viewer


GetDelivery, ListDeliveries
What was sent and what became of it
viewer


PrepareSend
Draft and confirm a message before it leaves
editor


SendNotification
Send a WhatsApp message or SMS to a configured contact
editor


PlaceCall
Place a call to a configured contact
editor


UpsertContact, DeleteContact
Manage the contact list
admin


SetCarrierConfig
Set the messaging carrier credentials
admin



Delivery status arrives back on POST /comms/twilio/status; see
HTTP endpoints.
runink.ui.chat.v1.ChatService
The assistant's chat history (Settings › Chat history). The assistant
starts empty on every page load, sign-in and app start; each question and
answer is saved here instead, in PULSE's own database, with the text sealed.
Every method needs viewer and works only on the caller's own chats: another
person's chat is NotFound.



Method
In PULSE




ListChats
The caller's chats, newest first. An unreadable history is Unavailable, never an empty list.


GetChat
One chat and its messages, oldest first. A failed answer is kept and marked failed; a run or report it produced is its link.


CreateChat
A new chat, titled after its first question. The subject is always assistant.


AppendMessages
Adds the question and the answer. A chat keeps its newest 400 messages.

docs/troubleshooting/.title: Troubleshooting
docs/troubleshooting/.body:
Troubleshooting

Find the message you see, then read the cause and the fix. Messages are quoted
from the source; ... marks a part that varies.
The server will not start



Message
Cause
Fix




refusing to start: no session signing key configured (PULSE_JWT_SECRET unset)
PULSE_JWT_SECRET is unset
Set it to a new random value. There is no default and none is generated.


refusing to start: the pulse appfs root cannot be mounted: ...
The sealed app root has no usable backend
Check the object store settings, or PULSE_APPFS_DIR for a local root.


Failed to initialize database: ...
Usually TIDDE_ENVELOPE_KEK is missing; PULSE's store refuses to open without it
Ask Runink to set the key.


refusing to start in production: insecure configuration: ...
PULSE_ENV=production and a check failed
Fix each listed problem. For the CORS problem, set CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS to pinned origins (no wildcard); the backend serves no web bundle, so there is no same-origin exemption.


TLS misconfigured: set BOTH PULSE_TLS_CERT and PULSE_TLS_KEY (or neither)
Only one of the two is set
Set both, or neither.


MESH_MTLS=true but mesh identity unavailable: ...
No mesh identity could be set up
Provide MESH_ISSUER_URL and MESH_CA_CERT (preferred), or the older MESH_CA_CERT and MESH_CA_KEY; or turn off MESH_MTLS.


Server exits with no output, no log file
Locally: pkill -f 'pulse-server serve' matches the shell running that command, so it kills your own session
Stop the server by its PID instead.


address already in use
A previous server holds the port
Stop it by PID, then restart.



Signing in



Message
Cause
Fix




invalid credentials
The break-glass admin's username or password is wrong, or no break-glass admin was seeded (people sign in with Google)
Use the break-glass username, not an email. On a local server, start it with PULSE_ADMIN_PASSWORD.


authorization token is not provided
The call had no bearer token
Send authorization: Bearer .


invalid token: ...
The token expired, or its session was signed out
Sign in again.


a cookie session requires the x-pulse-csrf header and a trusted Origin
A browser call authenticated by the session cookie arrived without the x-pulse-csrf: 1 header, or from an origin this deployment does not trust
For a browser front end, add its origin to CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS exactly; a wildcard is never accepted.


token contains an invalid number of segments
A script read .token; the field is accessToken
Read accessToken.


Google sign-in: "not set up on this PULSE" (/auth/google answers not_configured)
Google sign-in is off
Set GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID.


Google sign-in: "Nobody can sign in with Google on this PULSE yet" (sso_closed)
AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS is empty
Add the allowed addresses.


Google sign-in: "… is not on this PULSE's list of people allowed to sign in" (not_allowed)
The email is not on the allowlist
Add it to AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS.


Google sign-in: "Google signed you in for a different app" (wrong_client)
The ID token was issued to another OAuth client than GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
Use the web client's ID in GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID; the Android app asks Google for a token for that same client.


Android: "This copy of the app is not registered with Google yet"
The Google project of GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID has no Android OAuth client for org.runink.pulse with the SHA-1 of the key the installed app is signed with
Add one for each key the app is signed with.


license expired or invalid
A configured licence failed verification
Install a valid licence.


Log: AUTHENTICATION DISABLED — every request will be rejected as Unauthenticated
This deployment's session key is one PULSE refuses to sign or verify with, so no token can be accepted
Replace PULSE_JWT_SECRET with a fresh value that has never been committed to a repository, and restart.



AI features



Message
Cause
Fix




inference server is not running / model service is not ready — the inference server is not running
No inference server, or it is still loading
Check INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL or the local model files. Watch model_ready on /health.


the inference plane is at capacity and declined this request; nothing was generated — retry in a few minutes
The server is busy
Retry in a few minutes.


the model returned no content for ...
The model produced an empty response
Retry. Check the inference server's log.


still-image generation is not available: the image-generation tier was retired ...
Still images and videos are not made from a prompt
Make a document or a podcast, or make a short video from a piece's script (Short videos).



Site score and audit fixes



Message
Cause
Fix




could not read ... — a reachable website with readable content is required to run the diagnostic
PULSE could not load the site
Check the URL is public and returns readable HTML.


url is required / repo_path is required
A field is missing in ApplyAuditActions
Fill it in.


apply modes are disabled on this server; set PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED=true (exactly, lowercase) and PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY=true to allow write/commit/pr
The kill switch or PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY is off
Use plan, or have an admin arm both.


apply modes require an administrator
Your role is not admin
Ask an admin to apply the fixes.


repo_path is not an allowed repository on this server
The path is outside PULSE_APPLY_ROOT, missing, or escapes it
Use a checkout inside the root.


audit apply has no repository root on this server; an administrator must set PULSE_APPLY_ROOT
PULSE_APPLY_ROOT is unset
Set it to the directory holding site checkouts.


github integration is missing a target owner/repo — ...
pr mode without a target
Set owner and repo on the GitHub connection.


scoring config: ...
PULSE_SCORING_CONFIG is unreadable or invalid, or the profile is unknown
Fix the file or the profile name.



The one-line audit



On the audit card
Cause
Fix




"…" is not a domain (expected something like example.com)
You gave an IP address, localhost, or something that is not a host name
Type a public domain, for example Audit example.com.


Nothing happens; the assistant answers in chat instead
The line has a question mark, or no verb it recognizes
Write Audit example.com, with no ?. See Audit a domain.


Waiting for the model (position N in the queue)
Another audit's model calls are ahead of yours
Nothing. Your steps run in turn.


Publishing schedule is skipped: no draft to put the plan's times on
The plan had no draft to carry its dates
Expected. The tasks are on the 90-day plan; the audit is not partial because of it.


A post in the Scheduled column of Campaigns says missed
Its time passed while the piece was waiting for approval
Reschedule it, or remove it. A missed post is never sent late.


A step is skipped with blocked: …
A step it needs did not finish, for example blocked: the site could not be read (…)
Fix the first failed step, then Resume the audit.


A phase reads … — not completed within the 3-minute budget
The diagnosis has a time limit. A phase that did not finish inside it is reported as not done rather than left to look finished
Expected under load. Run it again when the inference server is quieter.


diagnosis: … or the analysis was written but no plan was produced
The model returned nothing usable, or the plan step failed
Resume the audit. Steps already done are not repeated.


every lead discovery search failed (…) — the web was not reached
No lead search answered
Check the server's web access, then resume.


this domain was audited at … UTC (less than 24h ago) — returning that run
A finished audit of the domain is less than a day old
Use Run it again to force a fresh one.


PermissionDenied when you start an audit
Your role is viewer
Ask an admin to make you an editor.



Leads and connections



Message
Cause
Fix




HubSpot isn't connected yet — configure it on the Integrations page first
No HubSpot connection
Connect it on the HubSpot card in Settings → Integrations.


HubSpot integration has no access token configured
The connection has no token
Rotate the credential.


HubSpot sync failed: ...
HubSpot rejected the call
Check the token's scopes.


unsupported lead platform: ... (only hubspot is supported today)
SyncLeads with another platform
Use hubspot.


a niche is required to prospect for leads
ScrapeLeads without a niche
Provide one.


a lead needs at least a name, email, or company
Empty CreateLead
Fill one in.


`invalid pipeline stage "..." (want new\
contacted\
qualified\
won\
lost)`
Unknown stage
Use one of the five.


outbound calling is disabled on this server; an administrator must set PULSE_OUTBOUND_CALLS=true
Calls are not armed
Have an admin set it.


outbound calls require an editor or administrator
Your role is viewer
Ask an admin to change your role.


Scheduled post withheld: ... is owner-gated: user "" is not in PULSE_PUBLISHER_USER_IDS
The channel publishes as the deployment and the content's owner is not allowlisted
Add the owner's user id, or leave it withheld.


/podcast/feed.xml returns 404
Both podcast and audiobook are disarmed
Arm one, if the feed should exist.


lead has no phone number
Nothing to dial
Add a phone number.


Google Analytics isn't connected yet — configure it on the Integrations page first
No GA4 connection
Connect it on the Google Analytics card in Settings → Integrations.


no GA4 property ID configured — set it when connecting Google Analytics
The connection lacks a property ID
Reconnect with the property ID.


A forecast shows history only (too_few_days)
Fewer than four days of Google Analytics data are synced
Run SyncGaData with a longer lookback.



Sign-in connections and the website repository (administrators)



Message
Cause
Fix




Instagram sign-in isn't set up on this server yet: an administrator must set META_APP_ID and META_APP_SECRET (also YouTube … GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, LinkedIn … LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID and LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET)
The platform's app client is not configured
Set both keys; see Meta, Google, LinkedIn. Until then the card accepts a pasted token.


… sign-in isn't set up on this server yet: an administrator must set PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL to the https address the sign-in returns to
PULSE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is unset or not https
Set the https address; see Public address and redirects.


Company pages aren't set up on this server yet: …
LINKEDIN_COMPANY_PAGES is off
Turn it on only after LinkedIn approved the Community Management API.


The platform says the redirect URI does not match
The callback is not registered exactly in the developer console
Register /oauth/social/callback (or /oauth/search-console/callback, /oauth/mail/callback), https, no trailing slash.


Sign-in completes at the platform but the card stays not connected
The public edge did not send the callback to the backend, or the connect link was older than ten minutes
Route the /oauth/…/callback paths to the backend; start the connection again.


your Search Console properties could not be read: …
The Google Search Console API is not enabled in the client's project, or the account has no property
Enable the API; add the site to Search Console.


GitHub rejected the website repository token; reconnect it in Settings → Integrations
The token expired or was revoked
Create a new fine-grained token and reconnect.


GitHub refused to …: the token is missing a permission (…)
The token lacks Contents or Pull requests (read and write), or does not cover the repository
Regenerate it with both permissions on that repository.


apply modes are disabled on this server; … on Propose as pull request
PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED or PULSE_AUDIT_APPLY is off
Arm both, if proposals are wanted.


No video was made: video is not available on this server.
The server's video tool is missing, or did not pass its check when the server started
Look at the video part of /health, and use the backend image.



Publishing



Message
Cause
Fix




website publishing is disabled: ...
The blog channel is not armed
See Publishing controls. The message names the layer.


PULSE_SITE_REPO is not set — refusing to publish; set it to YOUR site repo as owner/repo
No target repository
Set PULSE_SITE_REPO.


no github integration/token configured for user ...
The content owner has no GitHub token
Paste one on the Website card in Settings → Integrations.


no publishing integration for channel ... yet
The post was scheduled to a channel PULSE drafts for but does not post to, for example Facebook or X
Download it and post it yourself. See Publishing.


A scheduled post shows withheld
Its channel was disarmed when it came due
Arm the channel, then schedule the content again.


LinkedIn post withheld: LinkedIn publishing is not configured: … (drafts-only: the content stays approved for manual posting)
No LinkedIn token or author is configured
Expected on a drafts-only deployment. Download it from its card and post it by hand.


Startup warning that PULSE_APPLY_ENABLED is ambiguous
The value is not exactly true
Write true, lowercase.



Voice, billing, media



Message
Cause
Fix




voice calling is not configured (HTTP 503)
Voice calling is not set up on this deployment
Ask Runink to set it up.


speech synthesis is not configured
The platform's speech service is not available on this deployment
Ask Runink to set it up. See Voice.


media storage is not available: ... / media unavailable
The sealed media store is not mounted
Check the app root's backend.


Log: Site Audit Engine: NOT started — no target site; ...
No daily audit target
Set PULSE_SITE_AUDIT_URL.



The app looks empty
PULSE never fills a gap with an estimate. A figure it could not read is drawn
as —, and a page with nothing behind it reads as empty rather than as a row
of zeros. An empty page is usually a missing input, not a fault.

Brand Analysis says "No check-up yet", and its cards say "Not checked
yet". Choose New site audit. See Getting started.
Results read "Not measured". Nothing measured the period yet. Connect
Google Analytics, Google Ads or Search Console in Settings →
Integrations. The work PULSE did is still counted, under What PULSE
did. See Results and reports.
"Results of your posts: not measured yet". No platform reported results
for your posts this week: connect Instagram, LinkedIn or YouTube, or wait
for the first results after a post goes out.
Campaigns has no drafts, and Leads has no tasks. Run a check-up. A
finished check-up fills them.
A card shows — where you expected a number. PULSE could not read that
figure — usually a connection that is not set up, or a run that has not
happened yet. Nothing is wrong with the card. See
Measured and not measured.

Connecting accounts and planning



What you see
Cause
Fix




… sign-in isn't set up on this server, with a list of settings
Your administrator has not registered PULSE with that platform
Paste a token instead, or ask your administrator to set what the card lists. See Connections.


The sign-in has ended. Reconnect … to keep publishing.
The platform ended the sign-in, or renewing it failed
Reconnect on the card.


Missing permission: …. Reconnect and allow it.
You declined a permission when signing in
Reconnect and allow it.


The sign-in page could not be opened
The browser blocked the pop-up
Allow pop-ups for PULSE and try again.


This Google account has no verified site in Search Console
The Google account you signed in with owns no Search Console property
Add your site at search.google.com/search-console, then reconnect.


Website repository: Missing permission, Token rejected or Base branch not found
The fine-grained token lacks Contents or Pull requests (Read and write), has expired, or the branch name is wrong
Fix the token or the branch, then Check again. See Website repository.


connect your website repository in Settings → Integrations first
Propose as pull request with no repository connected
Connect it.


PULSE does not know who you talk to yet: run a site audit (it asks who buys from you) or add leads, then plan again
A campaign plan needs at least one persona
Run a check-up, or add leads, then plan again.


This can't move from … to … / A post moves to Sent only when it goes out.
A move the board does not allow
See Approve and schedule.


Not connected, so PULSE will not post it
The piece's channel has no connected account
Download it and post it yourself, or connect the channel.

privacy/.title: PULSE — Privacy Policy
privacy/.body:
This policy covers the PULSE app published by Runink (Android application
id org.runink.pulse, and the web app) and the PULSE backend it talks to. For
the rest of the Runink platform, see the general privacy policy.
PULSE is a marketing workspace sold to organisations per seat. You use it
through your organisation's PULSE deployment.

Who can use PULSE
You sign in with your Google account. The first sign-in creates your PULSE
account on your organisation's deployment, if your organisation has admitted
your address. The app does not sell seats.

What PULSE collects

Your account: your name and email address from Google sign-in, and your
role. Stored encrypted.
What you make in PULSE: audits of the websites you ask about, drafts,
campaigns, plans, leads and follow-ups, your business profile and brand
colours.
Images and files you add: logos, pictures and documents you pick or take
with the camera app.
Voice commands: when you use the voice bar or the assistant call, your
speech is sent to Runink's own speech-to-text service and turned into text.
The audio is not kept. The server log records the size and loudness of the
clip, not the words. The text becomes an assistant message, kept in your
chat history like a typed one.
Digital twins: the photos, short videos and voice recordings you add to
make your own presenter, the consent you record with each, and the
presenter videos PULSE makes from them. See
Digital twins below.
Connected accounts: when you connect LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, Google
Business Profile, Search Console or an email mailbox, the access tokens they
issue, stored encrypted, and what PULSE reads with them (your posts' results,
reviews, comments and messages on those accounts).
Usage: how many tasks you ran today, for your seat's daily limit.

PULSE does not collect your location, contacts, calendar, health data or
device identifiers. The app has no advertising or analytics SDK. Its only
permissions on Android are the internet and the microphone.

Digital twins
A digital twin is a presenter for your own presentations and course materials.
There are two kinds.

Built-in presenters are drawn, animated characters with a stock voice.
They are not real people and hold no recording of anyone. Tapping one plays a
short greeting.
Your own twin is made from your own photo or a short video of your
face (a video of at most 60 seconds), and, if the voice service supports
it, your own voice from a recording of 5 to 60 seconds that the app
guides you through.

Consent. PULSE refuses a photo, video or recording that does not come with
a consent you recorded in the last 24 hours: the consent text you were shown,
a statement you give, and the time. The text says the voice, face and likeness
are your own, or that the person in them agreed in writing, and that PULSE may
use them only to make a digital version of you for your own presentations and
course materials. PULSE does not check your statement against the recording.
Where it is processed. Your photo, video and voice recording are stored
encrypted on Runink's servers and are not
published or listed for anyone else. The voice sample is sent to Runink's own
speech service to make your voice, and, for a lip-synced video, your photo and
the narration go to Runink's own services on Runink's own hardware. No third-party AI service receives your face,
voice or videos. PULSE does not identify people from their faces and does not
match a face against any other.
Presenter videos. You can turn a script into a presenter video: a voice-over
video, an animated presenter (an illustration),
or a lip-synced video of your own twin. A lip-synced video is
AI-generated. It shows an
"AI-generated" label on the picture, and
PULSE offers no way to switch the label off. Videos are yours: PULSE does not
publish them unless you approve it, and publishing stays off until your
organisation turns it on.
Withdrawing consent and deleting. You can withdraw consent at any time in
the twin's screen. PULSE then deletes the recordings and the videos made from them. A withdrawn consent is not restored; to use your face or voice again you
add the recording again with a new consent. Deleting a twin, replacing or
removing its photo or video, and deleting your account
delete the same things. A record that consent was given and withdrawn is kept
until you delete your account. You can also edit a twin after you made it.
How long. PULSE keeps your recordings and videos until you withdraw
consent or delete the twin or your account. It sets no shorter period.

AI phone calls to leads
PULSE can place a phone call in which an AI assistant talks to one of your
leads for you. It is off by default. It needs your organisation's
administrator to turn it on, the account's own setting, and, for each lead, a
record that the lead agreed to calls from an AI. A call that comes from an
outreach sequence is placed only after you approve that call's plan. PULSE
refuses a call outside the allowed calling hours, to a number on your do-not-call list, or more often than the limits
allow.

It says what it is. Every call opens by saying it is an automated AI
assistant and whom it is calling for, then gives a recording notice. If the
lead says to stop, the call ends and the number goes on your do-not-call
list.
What is kept. PULSE keeps no audio. It keeps a written transcript,
encrypted, with the call, readable by your organisation's editors and
administrators, and the call's outcome and summary. The transcript is erased
after 7 days unless your administrator set a longer period, 90 days at
most. The outcome and summary stay on the lead.
The carrier. The call goes over Twilio, which carries the call and holds
the number it calls. Runink's own voice speaks and Runink's own services
understand: Twilio is not used for speech recognition or voice for PULSE.


Questions from the assistant to you
When the assistant cannot answer from your own data, it may ask the account's
owner one short question. The question is always shown in the app. It is also
sent by text message or WhatsApp to the owner's own contact only if the owner
opted in (off by default), approved the question, and it is outside
the owner's quiet hours. The owner can reply STOP to withdraw.

Email
PULSE sends email only from your own connected mailbox (Gmail, Microsoft 365
or an SMTP server), never from a shared sender, and only when your organisation
has turned sending on. Each email carries your identity, postal address and an
unsubscribe link. PULSE reads replies in that mailbox to stop a sequence and to
show you the answer. Disconnecting the mailbox removes its tokens.

Website chat and Google Business Profile
If you embed PULSE's chat on your own website, a visitor's messages are kept
for 7 days unless your organisation sets another period (30 days at most), and
then erased. The chat says
it is an AI assistant, and stores no IP address. Contact details are kept only
if the visitor submits the form. If you connect Google Business Profile, PULSE
reads your locations, reviews and results with your own Google sign-in and posts
or replies only when you approve.

Data about other people
PULSE finds business leads from public sources and from your website form:
company names, public business contact details and the pages they came from. It
keeps them for your organisation's use in PULSE. PULSE is for business-to-business
contact: it uses business addresses, keeps a suppression list that every
outreach sequence respects, and a do-not-call list for calls. Someone who is a
lead can ask your organisation, or us at contact@runink.org, to remove their
details. When a lead takes part in an AI call, the call's transcript is handled
as described above.

How it is used and shared

Your data is used to run PULSE for you and your organisation.
AI in PULSE runs on Runink's own servers. No third-party AI service receives
your data.
PULSE publishes to LinkedIn, Instagram or YouTube, sends an email from your
mailbox, or sends a WhatsApp or SMS message only after you approve it, and
only when your organisation has turned publishing on.
Service providers act for Runink: Twilio carries calls and messages, and your
own Google, Microsoft, LinkedIn, Meta and YouTube accounts receive only what
you send them.
PULSE can report each agent run to Runink TIDDE's console for audit. Nothing
is sent today: this stays off until it is approved and this page says so.
Runink does not sell your data.


Deleting your account
In the app: Account › Privacy and your account › Delete my account. This
signs you out everywhere and deletes your account and what PULSE keeps under
it: your twins, recordings and presenter videos, call transcripts, leads,
connections and settings. Earlier encrypted versions stay in storage history for
about a day, until it is compacted and cleaned. Posts already published stay on
the networks they went to.
Without the app: email contact@runink.org from your account's address,
with the subject "Delete my PULSE account". What is deleted and what is kept:
Delete your account.

Children
PULSE is a marketing workspace for businesses. It is not directed at children
and is for people aged 18 and over; only people an organisation has admitted
can use it.
